titulo: Optimizing Routes for UVA's Facilities Management Fleet: Enhancing Sustainability and Pedestrian Safety
fonte_periodico: 2025 IEEE Systems and Information Engineering Design Symposium Sieds 2025
resumo: To enhance pedestrian safety and sustainability, UVA's Facilities Management (FM) fleet aims to reduce emissions and limit vehicle presence in high-foot-traffic areas. This supports UVA's goal of carbon neutrality by 2030 while creating a safer environment for pedestrians around Grounds. This project identifies optimal routes for FM vehicles traveling to reduce overall fuel consumption and minimize interactions with students in busy areas. Using vehicular telematics data available from the Geotab Platform, current routes were analyzed based on travel time, fuel usage, safety hazards, and proximity to popular student pathways. By looking at the most popular to and from locations of the FM fleet, we identified all reasonable route options and selected the best ones based on the above metrics. Recommended routes enhance efficiency and safety while also avoiding pedestrian-heavy areas like McCormick Road. We analyzed three high-frequency origin-destination pairs and assessed route options at different times of day, focusing on trip duration and peak pedestrian times like class changes. The final recommendations avoid McCormick Road during peak times or altogether while maintaining low trip durations and minimal safety concerns. These findings offer FM practical adjustments to support UVA's sustainability goals and pedestrian safety across grounds.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: ASSESSING THE IMPACT OF ORGANISATIONAL CULTURE ON DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN THE SRI LANKAN FACILITIES MANAGEMENT INDUSTRY
resumo: Amid rapid global technological advancements, the Facilities Management (FM) profession has undergone a significant transformation. Digitisation has emerged as a key driver in improving the efficiency, organization, and sustainability of physical infrastructure. Practitioners often perceive digital transformation beyond mere technological adoption, emphasizing the need for organizational change and strategic alignment to fully realize its benefits. This paper aims to analyse the impact of organisational culture on the digitalisation of FM functions in the Sri Lankan FM industry. To achieve the objective, this study employed a quantitative methodology using a survey approach. Data were collected through a questionnaire administered to a sample of 51 respondents3 from the FM industry. Eight hypotheses were tested using a t-test to examine the impact of cultural dimensions on the digitalisation in FM functions. The findings indicate that organisational culture has a significant impact on the digitalisation of the FM functions. Specifically, factors such as, hierarchical structure, leadership support and advocacy, risk acceptance, cross-department collaboration, employee empowerment, learning and skill development, flexibility and the influence of subcultures were found to positively affect the digitalisation. Conversely, change management practices were not found to have a significant impact. This study makes a novel contribution by addressing an important gap in the existing literature, specifically, underexplored intersection of organizational culture and digitalization within the FM sector, an area that has received limited scholarly attention despite its growing relevance in the digital era. © 2025, Ceylon Institute of Builders. All rights reserved.

titulo: Management of Physical Asset. Problem and Possible Solutions Applicable Through Use of Spatial Web Tools
resumo: An effective Building Maintenance Management (BMM) must integrate and manage information such as inspections, drawings, manuals, contracts (Chen et al., 2013) checklists, maintenance reports and maintenance records (Lin & Su, 2013). However, current practices do not integrate these systems and still manually process dispersed and unformatted data. There is a significant waste of time and money for search information or to try to make decisions with limited information (Akinci, 2014). The efficiency of the maintenance process is expected to be highly increased with the availability of an integrated digital database (Akcamete et al., 2011). In this paper we gonna see in details the potential benefits of the integration of data of Building Maintenance Management (BMM) in Building Information Modelling (BIM). There is a vastly number of studies about the application of BIM during design, planning and construction phases developed both by practitioners and academics. Dong et al. (2014) pointed that specifically the use of BIM for FM during the O&M phase is still limited. In this paper we will deal with the problem both from the point of view of the management of the building and from the point of view of the management of spare parts that may be present in the project and how to manage them through the use of BMM and BIM web tool. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

titulo: Bridging the gap between the project management and facility management-Use of Uncertainty management in Facility management
resumo: This paper focusing bridging the gap between project management and facility management. The aim of the paper is to analyse and discuss how uncertainty management methods, tools and techniques can be used in FM one a Iland with existing infrastructure. Literature review relevant to the topic has been the primarily method in use. The main conclusion from the research is that effective uncertainty management related to FM needs a holistic approach, not only focusing on the individual elements of a system, but also an understanding of the connection and interaction between the elements of the system. Good cooperation between the FM manager and the owner may give a holistic understanding of the risk and opportunities that management team on the island need to monitor and control. titulo: Design of Intelligent Operation and Maintenance Management System for Substation Integrating Digital Twin and BIM
fonte_periodico: Proceedings 2025 International Conference on Power Electrical Engineering Electronics and Control Peeec 2025
resumo: Targeting the cutting-edge field of power systems, we have developed an intelligent substation operation and maintenance system based on a four-layer architecture of 'acquisition-edge-bus-application' and combined digital twin and BIM technologies. The system has also completed engineering certification: in accordance with the IEC 61850-9-2 specification, 4 kHz synchronous sampling is implemented on the device side, and the edge gateway implements Kalman filtering and Δ-compression optimization. Data is uploaded to the 5G gNodeB via the MQTT-TLS protocol. The data flows through 25 Gbps optical fiber and converges to the data lake and partitioned Kafka bus, achieving a 1 -second update rate for twin-BIM. At the application level, rigid body registration and least squares correction are used to achieve the unification of the twin state and BIM-IFC 3D posture, maintaining the spatial error value below 2 cm. With the help of Forge-API WebSocket and OPC UA technology, a closed-loop structure of 'physical-virtual-decision-making' is formed. Relying on the SoCal 28-Bus measured data set, functional performance testing and analysis were carried out: the average response time was less than 300 milliseconds, the end-to-end data delay was 87.5 milliseconds, the throughput reached 9,230 messages per second, the system reliability was 99.87 %, the digital twin synchronization frequency was 1.12 Hz, and the BIM refresh frequency was 0.98 Hz; the fault warning system used convolutional neural networks and bidirectional long short-term memory networks, and adopted a dynamic threshold control method. The accuracy of the warning 48 hours ago was 96.4 %, the missed alarm rate was 1.8 %, the false alarm rate was 3.5 %, and the consistency error between BIM and physical mapping did not exceed 0.6 %. The operating stability of the equipment was improved from 97.2 % to 99.1 %, and the full life cycle cost was reduced by 11.4 percentage points. This architecture is in line with the current intelligent operation and maintenance specifications of the power industry and adapts to the scalable capabilities of AI diagnosis and energy consumption forecasting.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Determination of Indicators Level of Service (LoS) for Building Asset Management
resumo: Building asset management in Indonesia has seen significant advancements as awareness of the importance of efficient management increases. This discipline focuses on the management, maintenance, and operation of buildings to ensure they function optimally, sustainably, and in accordance with community needs. The Level of Service (LoS) assessment serves as an indicator of the quality of service provided by building infrastructure to its users. LoS is essential for evaluating operational performance and making investment priority decisions throughout the infrastructure lifecycle, from construction to operation, maintenance, and rehabilitation. Therefore, research on determining LoS is crucial. This study employs the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) method to determine the weight of LoS assessment for buildings. Respondents were selected based on relevant expertise and experience to provide in-depth and accurate evaluations. The research results indicate that the application of the LoS model in the case study yields results consistent with the recorded condition reports of the observed buildings. The scope of this study is limited to the classroom assets of the Faculty of Engineering at Jember University and does not consider other assets such as roads or water structures. Additionally, this research solely involves the perspectives of building users without exploring other technical or financial aspects. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2025.

titulo: Grid-Based Spatial Encoding for Multimodal LLMs in Facility Management
fonte_periodico: Proceedings 2025 Artificial Intelligence for Business Aixb 2025
resumo: This paper presents ongoing research on a spatial analysis framework designed to improve the performance of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in real-time facility management, with parking lot monitoring as a representative use case. Although MLLMs perform well in object recognition, they often fail to capture precise spatial relationships, limiting localization accuracy. Existing methods address this issue but typically depend on specialized sensors, prebuilt maps, or complex embodied systems, which hinder deployment in resourceconstrained environments. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a grid-based spatial encoding method that embeds structured layouts directly into prompts, anchoring visual elements to explicit reference zones. This improves localization, obstruction detection, and reasoning in occluded or ambiguous scenes. In real-world parking scenarios, our approach increased space identification accuracy from 29% to 86% and obstruction detection from 15% to 85%. The system transforms ordinary surveillance into actionable spatial insights, supporting frontline workers and advancing safe, efficient, and sustainable operations in line with Japan's Society 5.0 vision. These preliminary findings demonstrate that prompt-based spatial grounding can significantly improve the spatial reasoning capabilities of MLLMs without retraining or additional sensors, and future work will extend validation to broader facility contexts. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: GEOSPATIAL MODELLING-THE NEXUS FOR CLIMATE INDUCED HAZARD ASSESSMENT AND INFORMED DECISION MAKING FOR DISASTER RISK REDUCTION
fonte_periodico: Proceedings of the IAHR World Congress
resumo: According to the Sustainable Development Goals Report 2024 the world is severely off track to realise the 2030 Agenda of the adopted SDGs. To put the SDGs on course, accurate, timely and disaggregated information is required. Given that disaster events are spatial phenomena, the application of geospatial based information systems has been proven to be a reliable tool for disaster risk reduction. Effective use of these technologies is context-specific and requires constant research and innovative development. Advances in web based geospatial information technology, and the integration thereof in infrastructure facilities management and asset management are providing opportunities to mainstream concepts of sustainable development, in particular climate resilience, into infrastructure design, operation and maintenance. These are investigated with reference to the Cities Infrastructure Delivery Management System (CIDMS) which is a fully compliant ISO 55000 asset management system. This paper further explores the importance of information sharing in the context of critical infrastructure delivery by showcasing an integrated web-based visualisation platform which is designed to model flood risk and provide instant statistics for analysing risk reduction possibilities. © 2025 IAHR.

titulo: An LCA–BIM integrated framework for life cycle carbon emissions assessment of bridges
autores: Chen, XH; Wang, HY; Khant, TT; Li, Q
resumo: Building information modelling (BIM) facilitates data collection throughout the life cycle of infrastructure, yet its implementation in life cycle assessment (LCA) for bridges poses challenges. This article presents a model that integrates BIM and LCA to assess the life cycle carbon emissions (LCCE) of bridges efficiently and accurately. The bridge’s life cycle is divided into four stages: material production, construction, operation and maintenance and demolition. Clearly defined boundaries for carbon emissions are established, and BIM generates the necessary data. A case study bridge evaluates this method, analysing factors like steel, cement and transportation using Monte Carlo simulation and sensitivity analysis. The total carbon emissions for the case bridge are 2.44 × 10^7 kg, primarily from material production and transportation (75.7%) and operation (17.6%). The study shows that integrating LCA and BIM improves carbon emission assessments, guiding low-carbon bridge choices and enhancing sustainability efforts towards carbon neutrality. © 2025 Informa UK Limited, trading as Taylor & Francis Group.

titulo: Applications and challenge of digital twin in life cycle of municipal pipe networks
resumo: Digital twin is the key technology to promote the life cycle digitalization and intelligent management of municipal pipe networks. To achieve intelligent closed-loop management for the life cycle of municipal pipe networks, this paper first analyzed the meanings of “process-oriented” and “object-oriented” of digital twin and gave the connotation for the life cycle management of the digital-twin-driven municipal pipe networks. Second, on the basis of the application paradigms in typical scenarios of design, construction, operation, and maintenance of the life cycle management of the municipal pipe networks, this paper proposed the technical framework of digital twin-driven municipal pipe networks. Finally, the existing challenges were discussed for the digital twin in the life cycle management of municipal pipe networks. The research shows that digital twin is the technical guarantee for the life cycle management of municipal pipe networks, and high-fidelity digital “twinning” is an important prerequisite for realizing the function of digital twin. © 2024 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

titulo: Bibliometric analysis of innovative technology use in sustainable facilities management for smart city development
resumo: Purpose In Africa, technological adoption in facility management (FM) is hindered by knowledge gaps, high costs and outdated infrastructure. This study aims to examine the role of innovative technology in sustainable FM (SFM) for Smart Cities through a bibliometric analysis to identify trends, themes and gaps. Design/methodology/approach A bibliometric analysis was conducted using Scopus as the primary data source, covering publications from 2014 to 2024. Data was analysed using VOSviewer to visualise publication networks, keyword clusters and citation relationships. A systematic search and content analysis were applied to ensure relevant document inclusion and thematic exploration. Findings Research interest in this field has grown significantly since 2021, with the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, digital twin and building information modelling emerging as dominant technologies. China leads in publications, while Spain has the highest citation impact. However, international collaboration remains weak, particularly in Africa highlighting the need for stronger interdisciplinary research networks. Originality/value This study contributes to the discourse on digital transformation in FM and smart cities by mapping technological advancements and their impact. It outlines future research and suggestions for SFM development in Africa. © 2025 Emerald Publishing Limited

titulo: Multi-Criteria Evaluation and Selection of Investment Schemes for Transmission and Transformation Projects Considering Life-cycle Cost and Carbon Emissions
fonte_periodico: 2025 5th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Control Science Ic2ecs 2025
resumo: Under China's dual-carbon targets and the agenda of high-quality power grid development, investment decisions for transmission and transformation projects need to jointly account for life-cycle costs and carbon emissions. In practice, however, scheme comparison still emphasizes upfront construction costs and a narrow set of technical indicators, while operation and maintenance costs, energy loss costs, and carbon costs over the life cycle are often underrepresented. This study analyzes the cost and carbon-emission components of transmission and transformation projects across the planning and design, construction, operation and maintenance, and end-of-life phases, and develops a multidimensional evaluation index system covering technical and safety performance, economic and life-cycle cost performance, environmental and carbon performance, and social and comprehensive benefits. Indicator weights are derived using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), and the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) is applied to evaluate and rank three alternative schemes for a 220 kV transmission and transformation project. The results show that, after incorporating loss-related costs and carbon costs into the lifecycle cost assessment, a scheme with slightly higher initial investment achieves better performance in both life-cycle economic efficiency and environmental impact, and becomes the overall preferred option. The proposed AHP-TOPSIS-based 'lifecycle + carbon' multi-criteria evaluation framework provides a concise and practical decision-support tool for investment scheme selection in transmission and transformation projects. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Toward a systematic integration of digital technologies in facility management organizations and services
resumo: Purpose – This article focuses on the complex relationship between digital technologies (DTs) and Facility Management (FM), aiming to develop frameworks to systematically integrate DTs into FM organizations and services. Design/methodology/approach – We conducted workshops with academics and industry representatives, focusing on (i) the classification and conceptualization of DT applications in FM, (ii) the effects of DT on FM, and (iii) the standardization and scaling of DTs within organizations and across the industry. Findings – This article, classifies DTs from the perspectives of information systems, business development, and the value chain. This article identifies key technology considerations, including positive and negative effects, risks and myths, barriers and enablers, and coping strategies. This article addresses opportunities and challenges related to the standardization and scaling of DTs. Practical implications – The conceptualizations co-created by industry and academia help establish a relevant research agenda and support the implementation of DTs. Originality/value – These categorizations advance the understanding of DTs in FM and lay a foundation for further research. © 2025 Olli Vigren, Chiara Tagliaro, Toomaj Ghalandar and Tin Phan

titulo: Life cycle environmental impact assessment of bridges based on comparison of different construction schemes
autores: Chen, XH; Shi, PY; Wang, HY
resumo: The full life cycle environmental assessment method is widely applied in infrastructure projects such as buildings and highways. However, its application to bridge life cycle assessments remains challenging. This paper addresses this gap by conducting a comprehensive environmental impact study throughout the entire life cycle of bridges. A foundational framework is proposed for evaluating the environmental impacts of bridge life cycles, dividing the process into four phases: raw material production, construction, operation and maintenance, and demolition and recycling. The evaluation system is applied to a newly constructed bridge, comparing two distinct construction methods—prefabricated small box girder and cast-in-place large box girder—to provide data for life cycle impact analysis. Four key factors—transportation distance, maintenance frequency, recycling coefficient, and material usage—are incorporated into the analysis. Sensitivity analysis, with a 10% fluctuation range for each variable, reveals that the initial phase (raw material production and processing) has the most significant environmental impact, particularly on human health, followed by resources and energy, and finally ecosystems. Among the variables, material usage during the initial phase shows the greatest sensitivity, followed by recycling efficiency in the demolition phase, repair frequency during operation, and transportation distance during construction. Regarding construction methods, the prefabricated method results in a higher level of pollution compared to the cast-in-place method. Based on these findings, a carbon emission reduction strategy is proposed to support green and sustainable development, aiming for carbon neutrality. The study highlights the importance of selecting low-carbon, sustainable materials in the design phase to minimize environmental impacts over the life cycle. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature B.V. 2025.

titulo: Application of Life-Cycle Assessment Approach to Zero Energy Buildings: Case Study of an Office Building in South Korea
resumo: This study evaluates the life-cycle carbon footprint of buildings, addressing a key limitation of zero-energy buildings (ZEBs), which primarily focus on operational energy use. This study identified the optimal conditions for structure type and window-to-wall ratio (WWR) of ZEB implementation to evaluate carbon emissions from a life-cycle perspective. Building energy simulations and life-cycle assessment (LCA) analyses were conducted to examine variations in the operational energy consumption and building life-cycle carbon emissions based on different structural materials and WWR configurations. The building selected for this analysis featured a combination of concrete and wood structures, with a WWR of 40% in the north–south direction and 30% in the east–west direction, each increasing by 20%. The findings indicated that increased WWR for both concrete and wood structures increases energy consumption. Moreover, the carbon emissions followed a similar pattern, rising as WWR increases. Regarding life-cycle carbon emissions, the findings suggest transitioning from the current concrete structure to a wood structure while maintaining a low WWR as an effective strategy to achieve carbon neutrality in building operations. titulo: Revolutionizing Facilities Management Outsourcing: AI Applications and Case Studies in Sustainable Outsourcing Relationships

resumo: Facility Management (FM) outsourcing is increasingly focusing on sustainability by adopting the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals in business decisions. This chapter aims to validate the published Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based FM outsourcing relationship system using real-world business cases related to sustainability. It begins with an introduction to the theory of the FM outsourcing relationship system, highlighting how it can assist FM strategists and leaders in designing their routine practices to enhance business effectiveness and productivity. The chapter also outlines the practical aspects of the research being conducted at the case study stage for testing and verification. In conclusion, categorizing FM outsourcing can assist in clarifying the relationships between providers and clients. Therefore, a methodological approach to assess new battery technologies has to be clearly identified and followed to maximize the opportunities of technology adaptation success. This paper aims to provide a high-level framework for oil and gas engineers to consider several important aspects prior to full acceptance and adoption of emerging battery technologies. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Research on Procurement Strategy of 500kV Transformers and Gas Insulated Switchgear Based on LCC
autores: Li, N; Li, CQ; Han, JQ; Zhang, WW
fonte_periodico: 2025 10TH INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON POWER AND RENEWABLE ENERGY, ICPRE
resumo: Taking the 500kV transformers and gas insulated switchgear (GIS) of a regional power grid as the research objects, a quantitative model including initial investment cost, operation and maintenance cost, repair cost, failure cost, and decommissioning disposal cost was constructed based on the Life Cycle Cost (LCC) theory of asset management. By collecting more than 320,000 business data records of 391 transformers and 817 GIS units from 2016 to 2023, the entropy weight method was adopted for cost correction and deviation standardization processing, and a supplier evaluation system was established. The research results show that considering the full life cycle cost expenditure of suppliers can more accurately evaluate the equipment quality of suppliers. This study provides data-driven decision support for power grid equipment procurement, which is helpful to improve the management level of equipment life cycle and the performance of asset operation.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Research on the Algorithm of Intelligent Management of the Whole Life Cycle of Buildings Based on the Integration of BIM and Internet of Things (IoT)
fonte_periodico: Proceedings 2025 2nd International Conference on Telecommunications and Power Electronics Telepe 2025
resumo: With the deepening of digital transformation in the construction industry, the integration of Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Internet of Things (IoT) is increasingly widely used in the whole life cycle management of buildings. How to give full play to the advantages of both to realize intelligent and refined building management is still an urgent problem to be solved. This study focuses on the core requirements of the whole life cycle of construction, and proposes a set of intelligent management algorithm framework based on the fusion of BIM and IoT. The construction organization designer based on BIM can provide a more scientific and controllable project progress management, and the effective fusion of BIM technology, intelligent algorithms, and construction can intuitively and imaginatively show the virtual construction process of the project, and analyze and decide on the optimal construction organization solution from the construction plan to the completion of construction. Organization scheme. The complementary characteristics of BIM and Internet of Things in data acquisition, storage and processing are analyzed, and the theoretical basis and realization framework of the integration technology are designed. Multi-level algorithms including data acquisition and pre-processing, data fusion and analysis, and decision support and optimization are developed for different phases of the whole building life cycle. The effectiveness of the algorithms is verified through actual cases, and an intelligent management platform integrating BIM and IoT technologies is constructed. The algorithmic framework significantly improves the efficiency of building energy management, resource utilization and the intelligent level of operation and maintenance, providing a new technical path and theoretical support for intelligent building management. ©2025 IEEE.

titulo: APPLICATION OF GREEN LEAN SIX SIGMA FOR MAINTENANCE MANAGEMENT OF ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT IN TRANSMISSION SUBSTATIONS
fonte_periodico: UPB Scientific Bulletin Series C Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
resumo: The new legislative requirements lead to changes in life cycle costs and implicitly to the reduction of the life span of electrical equipment. The most efficient maintenance methods are also the most expensive, for this reason it’s necessary to introduce a new method. Green Lean Six Sigma (GLSS) is a technique used in asset management, which offers the necessary tools to decide, implement and support improvements that have a positive impact on the environment. The purpose of this paper is to highlight the necessity and opportunity to implement the concept of Green Lean Six Sigma for asset management in high voltage electrical substations, as well as the feasibility of this goal. The aim is to expand the reliability centered maintenance method from a 2D analysis to a 3D one. A solution to improve substation maintenance is proposed by generating a global priority index of maintenance activities. © 2025, Politechnica University of Bucharest. All rights reserved.

titulo: Built to Suit Contracts for Brazilian Public Institutions: A Case Study of a Performance-Based Approach to Durable, Accessible and Sustainable Facility Occupation
autores: Gondim, IA; Calvetti, D; Sousa, H
resumo: In many public institutions across Brazil, there is a recurring need to occupy buildings in multiple municipalities within the same federative state. In the State of Ceará, there are institutions operating in over 100 municipalities, often in ceded, owned, or rented facilities. Occupation of ceded or leased premises has led to significant challenges in building maintenance and insufficient alignment with service needs. Acquiring property comes up against challenges related to acquisition costs and some slowness in the contracting process. In contrast, Built to Suit (BTS) contracts offer a faster, tailor-made construction process that aligns with specific client requirements. This study presents design parameters of a BTS project, incorporating strategies aimed at improving durability, internal layout, and service quality, while reducing maintenance and life cycle costs (LCC) compared to traditional solutions. The adopted solutions are described within the regional context, resulting in a project designed to meet functional, accessibility, and performance standards. Examples include the elimination of gutters over internal spaces—to prevent leaks—and contractual clauses that provide for mandatory preventive maintenance by the lessor. These measures contribute to a design with strong potential to meet the expected performance requirements. As a contribution, it is suggested that the BTS model, combined with a project flow guided by technical-operational diagnosis, can offer a fast and replicable solution for public institutions with high territorial dispersion. The proposed approach supports reducing corrective failures, improves operational performance and contributes to the building’s sustainability throughout its life cycle. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

titulo: Research on Material Life Cycle Management Method Based on Big Data Technology
fonte_periodico: Proceedings 2nd International Conference on Computer Communication Networks and Information Science Ccnis 2025
resumo: In order to cope with the challenges of process fragmentation, information lag and insufficient decision-making basis in the traditional power material management mode, and to achieve cost reduction, efficiency increase and accurate operation and maintenance, this paper studies a material life cycle management method based on big data technology. A hybrid prediction model combining Transformer deep learning model and HOLT smoothing algorithm is proposed to accurately predict the remaining useful life of the core components of substation equipment. The model gives full play to the advantages of Transformer in capturing the long-Term dependence and complex nonlinear characteristics of monitoring data, and combines the HOLT method to smooth the dominant trend, thus significantly improving the prediction accuracy. Through example verification, the model is superior to traditional prediction models such as LSTM and ARMA in key indicators such as RMSE (root mean square error) and MAE (mean absolute error). It provides a highly feasible theoretical model and practical path for power supply enterprises to implement the digital and intelligent life cycle management of substation materials. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Intelligent Operation and Maintenance in the Digital Transformation of Power Grid Production Project Management Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
fonte_periodico: 2025 International Conference on Energy Technology and Electrical Engineering Etee 2025
resumo: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, digital transformation has opened up a new path for intelligent operation and maintenance of power grid production project management. Aiming at the problem that traditional operation and maintenance mode is difficult to dynamically adapt to real-time changes of equipment status, complex task scheduling and emergency response, this study proposes a new intelligent operation and maintenance decision-making optimization model based on deep reinforcement learning. The core adopts deep double-Q network algorithm. Through reinforcement learning framework, the model takes equipment operating parameters (temperature, current, voltage, etc.) as inputs, combines experience playback and target network mechanism, and dynamically generates operation and maintenance policies. Experiments show that compared with CNN, LSTM and the original DQN algorithm, the deep double-Q network performs best on cumulative reward (1,643.2) and discounted cumulative reward (2,198.5), and the convergence speed is improved by about 25%. The actual deployment in the regional power grid verifies its effectiveness in minute-level fault response and resource optimization, with an operation and maintenance cost reduction rate of 21.3%. This study provides a reusable methodological framework for grid intelligent operation and maintenance, and helps to improve the efficiency of life cycle management. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Optimization Model of Interior Lighting Layout Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
fonte_periodico: 2025 6th International Conference on Intelligent Design ICID 2025
resumo: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, digital transformation has opened up a new path for intelligent operation and maintenance of power grid production project management. Traditional operation and maintenance modes struggle to dynamically adapt to real-time changes in equipment status, complex task scheduling, and emergency response. To address this issue, this study proposes a new intelligent operation and maintenance optimization model based on deep reinforcement learning. The core adopts the deep double-Q network algorithm. The model takes equipment parameters (temperature, current, voltage) as inputs, combines experience replay and target network mechanism, and dynamically generates operation and maintenance policies. Experiments show that compared with CNN, LSTM and the original DQN algorithm, the deep double-Q network performs best on cumulative reward $(1,628.6)$ and discounted cumulative reward $(2,198.5)$, and the convergence speed is improved by about 25%. The actual deployment in the regional power grid verifies its effectiveness in minute-level fault response and resource optimization, with an operation and maintenance cost reduction rate of 21.3%. This study provides a reusable methodological framework for grid intelligent operation and maintenance, and helps to improve the efficiency of life cycle management. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Multi-Objective Optimal Design of an Off-Grid Hybrid Renewable Energy System Ensuring Reliability and Minimizing Life Cycle Costs
fonte_periodico: Proceedings 2025 6th International Conference on Power Electronics and their Applications Icpea 2025
resumo: Hybrid energy generation systems based on renewable energies are designed to reliably supply energy to the load under various climatic conditions, guaranteeing high reliability and minimal energy cost. This paper proposes an optimal off-grid hybrid renewable energy system combining solar, wind, battery storage, and diesel generators. The system is designed using the multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO) method, considering the technical and economic performances over a 24 -year life cycle. The main objectives of the adopted multi-objective optimization process are to enhance reliability and reduce total life cycle costs, including investment, replacement, operation, and maintenance. Simulation results achieved an optimal reliability value of 99.07 % and an energy cost of 0.36 US/kWh over the system's lifecycle, with renewable energy sources contributing 97 % across different configurations of the hybrid PV/Wind/Battery/Diesel system. The proposed approach effectively succeeded in the optimal sizing of hybrid systems, ensuring the highest reliability and lowest cost. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Reliability analysis and life cycle costing of rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) system operating in a composite environment
autores: Pimpalkar, R; Sahu, A; Yadao, A; Patil, RB; Roy, A
fonte_periodico: Science and Technology for Energy Transition Stet
resumo: Solar PhotoVoltaic (PV) systems are becoming increasingly common, so it is critical to understand how system or component failure impacts lifetime costs. Reliability analysis uses historical performance data to help identify equipment or systems that perform badly. A case study of solar PV systems- dependability and Life Cycle Cost (LCC) analysis is presented in this research. Manufacturers and consumers of solar PV systems provide the information needed for reliability study. This research incorporates reliability analysis into the assessment of rooftop solar PV systems- LCCs in a composite climate. Failure and maintenance costs are a major contributor to total LCC, as demonstrated by estimating failure rates using Weibull++ modeling. ReliaSoft's Weibull++ software is used to estimate the best-fit failure distribution. Initial expenses, failure, Operation and Maintenance (O&M), and net salvage value are the categories into which the lifetime costs are divided. According to the analysis, inverters and balance-of-system elements are important sources of cost. The Mean Time Between Failure (MTBF) of earthing and grounding, DC CB, IGBT, AC CB, Grid, AC converter, relay, inverter, cooling fan, and SMBUS communication components is lower; however, since they need only modest repairs, this expense is covered by routine inspection. Understanding how costs affect a product's whole life cycle is made easier with the use of the LCC study. The cost of O&M accounts for around 74% of the overall LCC. Thus, it may be inferred that the LCC of the solar PV system was driven by O&M and failure costs. It gives the user an idea that O&M expenses associated with panel cleaning can be substituted by manual cleaning for small solar PV systems like those examined in this paper. Since failure costs are lower than O&M costs, it is possible to lower this cost by scheduling an ideal technician visit for routine inspection. The results indicate that PV system sustainability can be improved by implementing cost-effective technologies and optimizing maintenance procedures. Long-term performance monitoring, battery storage integration, and circular economy methods for recycling PV components should be the main topics of future research. © The Author(s), published by EDP Sciences, 2025.

titulo: Externality Assessment of an Onshore Wind Farm
autores: Ibrahim, HA; Thopil, GA
fonte_periodico: HUMAN-CENTRED TECHNOLOGY MANAGEMENT FOR A SUSTAINABLE FUTURE, VOL 3, IAMOT 2024
resumo: Onshore wind power has immense potential to accelerate South Africa’s energy transition to a sustainable power mix, effectively addressing the rising demand for electricity and mitigating the adverse impacts of fossil fuels. However, the effects on human health, crops, biodiversity, and materials caused by the technology remain largely unexplored in the existing literature. This study addresses this gap by examining both the greenhouse gas (GHG) and non-GHG emissions, as well as the external costs associated with onshore wind power in South Africa. Specifically, we focus on the 138 MW Jeffreys Bay Wind Farm, analysing its entire life cycle from material extraction/manufacturing (M), transportation (T), operation and maintenance (O&M), to decommissioning and disposal (D). This approach, known as life cycle assessment (LCA), provides a comprehensive understanding of the environmental impact. Results show that GHG impact accounts for 26.062 gCO2 eq/kWh and human health is the most significant non-GHG impact at 0.638 g/kWh. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

titulo: Survey on Enhancing Product Lifecycle Sustainability with Reinforcement Learning for Optimal Decision Making
fonte_periodico: 16th International Conference on Advances in Computing Control and Telecommunication Technologies Act 2025
resumo: The use of AI is popular in almost every field, from robotics to automation, finance, or healthcare. But challenges are associated with its application in decision-making for sustainable product lifecycle management (PLM) due to data lack of integrability and uncertainties from different stages of the whole product life cycle. To devise a methodology for choosing suitable AI techniques to support decision making in sustainable operations at different lifecycle stages. Identifying important lifecycle stages for AI – particularly reinforcement learning (RL) Otherwise known as Decision enhanced by RL A generalized procedure for employing RL in decision support is presented with life cycle data, such as operation and maintenance records. A case study where this method was verified in a simulation environment with an international manufacturer of vehicles. The case study demonstrates the potential performance of this method when using a simple linear model and suggests that RL is likely to be appropriate as the primary approach for maintenance scheduling in MTRO with small amounts of lifecycle data. In this paper we share an industrial case where RL improved decision making resulting in product lifecycle sustainability by prolonging the life of one product and reducing environmental impact. © Grenze Scientific Society, 2025.
palavras_chave: Artificial intelligence (AI); Data scarcity; Data uncertainties; Decision-making; Product lifetime; Sustainability; Sustainable product lifecycle

titulo: Integrated Environmental and Economic Assessment for the Replacement of the Flooring System in a Public Educational Building
resumo: The sustainability of society is interrelated with improving the sustainability of the built environment. In this scenario, public buildings have a lasting influence on society throughout their life cycle, with significant environmental and economic impacts, particularly during the usage, operation, and maintenance phases. The objective of this study is to evaluate the potential environmental and economic impacts on the flooring system over the reference period of 30 years, taking into account three alternatives (wood, ceramic, and vinyl) applied in the replacement phase of a public educational building located in Porto Alegre, Brazil. In addition to encompassing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): (SDG 11) Sustainable cities and communities, (SDG 12) Responsible consumption and production; (SDG 13) Action against global climate change—referring to the United Nations (UN) 2030 Agenda, the research method includes applying the integration of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and Life Cycle Cost (LCC) tools following national and international regulations. Tools are used with the assistance of OpenLCA and Excel software. The results demonstrate disparities in the integrated LCA-LCC analysis among the different alternatives. Ceramic flooring achieves low costs but has the most significant environmental impact. While wooden flooring has the best environmental results, vinyl flooring has the highest economic costs. Thus, the discussion seeks to provide conscious and balanced choices in flooring alternatives for technical managers in the public sector to make decisions. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

titulo: Assessing the Greenhouse Gas Emissions of a Base Station
fonte_periodico: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Technology Europe ICCT Europe 2025
resumo: The increasing demand of mobile subscribers and data traffic, especially in 6G, requires the deployment of additional cellular base stations contributing to greenhouse gas emissions. In order to curb climate change, there is a pressing need to comprehensively assess these emissions and identify levers to reduce them. The currently widespread approaches for assessing environmental impacts rely on overall procurement and purchase flows, offering a generalized non precise perspective. This paper investigates the implementation of a physical methodology that relies on a component-specific breakdown of emissions associated with a cellular base station and needs the physical characteristics as well as full life cycle analyses of every equipment. The assessment of the greenhouse gas footprint of a radio access network site considers the three main phases of its life cycle. The build phase which mainly consists of manufacturing and deployment emissions, the run phase emissions resulting from energy consumption of active equipment and ongoing operation and maintenance activities, and the decommissioning phase emissions associated with the disposal of components at the end of their life. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: User, operation, and maintenance manual for residential buildings: integrating BIM into document preparation and data collection
fonte_periodico: Iop Conference Series Earth and Environmental Science
resumo: Efficient building management requires the implementation of processes that ensure proper use, operation, and maintenance throughout a building's life cycle. In this context, innovative technologies such as Building Information Modeling (BIM) have stood out in enhancing the creation and organization of technical documents in the construction sector. This study aims to develop a user, operation, and maintenance manual for a single-family residence, employing BIM and meeting the requirements established by NBR 14037 (ABNT, 2024). The research highlights the importance of this document in building management, providing users with clear and accurate information to ensure appropriate performance and durability. As a case study, a high-standard single-family residence located in Petrópolis - RJ was analyzed, with projects modeled and coordinated using Revit and Navisworks software to ensure system compliance for the development of the User Manual. The results indicate that, despite current challenges and limitations in integrating this methodology for document generation, its application can significantly reduce operational and maintenance errors and improve communication among stakeholders throughout the building's life cycle, reaffirming the importance of this approach to improving the quality and efficiency of technical documentation in the sector. © Published under licence by IOP Publishing Ltd.

titulo: Steam Generators for Nuclear Power Plants
fonte_periodico: Steam Generators for Nuclear Power Plants
resumo: Steam Generators for Nuclear Power Plants, Second Edition continues its legacy of examining all phases of the lifecycle of nuclear steam generators (NSGs), components which are essential for the efficient and safe operation of nuclear reactors. This book is broken into three sections: design and manufacturing, operation and maintenance, and emerging topics. This revised edition includes new chapters on fitness for service guidelines; VVER steam generators; leakage through cracked tubes; secondary side components; full bundle probabilistic analysis; maintenance of steam generators; probabilistic models for steam generator life cycle predictions; steam generators for small modular and advanced nuclear reactors, and much more. This timely revision serves as a resource for professionals involved in all phases of the NSG lifecycle, from design, manufacturing, operation and maintenance, to fitness-for-service and long-term operation. It is also intended as a valuable resource for students and researchers interested in a range of topics relating to NSG lifecycle management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. titulo: A Four-Layer Digital Framework for BIM and FM Integration in a Sustainable Urban Drainage System †
resumo: This paper introduces a digital framework that integrates Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Facility Management (FM) to enhance the lifecycle performance of Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems (SuDS). Addressing the limitations of traditional drainage such as poor resilience and fragmented maintenance, the framework consists of the following four layers: BIM-based 3D asset modeling, sensor-driven monitoring, FM-integrated operations, and climate-informed adaptive planning. Grounded in systems engineering and aligned with International Standard ISO 19650 standards, it enables a dynamic digital twin to support continuous feedback and predictive maintenance. Illustrated through diagrams and comparison, the framework promotes adaptability and long-term sustainability in urban water infrastructure. © 2025 by the authors.
palavras_chave: Building Information Modeling (BIM); Facility Management (FM); Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems (SuDS)

titulo: Study on the whole lifecycle energy consumption scenarios of expressway
fonte_periodico: Science and Technology for Energy Transition Stet
resumo: This paper constructs a set of energy consumption scenarios for typical expressway construction, operation and maintenance phases, and analyses the energy demand under each scenario. Firstly, a comprehensive lifecycle energy consumption framework for expressway is established, detailing the energy consumption scenarios during construction, operation, and maintenance phases. Secondly, based on literature review and scenario assumptions, the study examines the energy consumption levels under different scenarios and analyses the proportion of energy consumption in each scenario. The results show that the ratio of energy consumption during the construction, operation and maintenance phases of expressway is about 5:10:3. The energy consumption during the construction phase is the highest for the construction of expressway trunk lines, accounting for about 80.6% of the total energy consumption. During the operation phase, fuelling and refuelling stations consume the most energy, accounting for about 71.4%. The energy consumption of expressway trunk lines is the highest during maintenance phase, which accounting for about 70%. This analysis facilitates a deeper understanding of the characteristics of the integration between transportation and energy networks, and assists the transportation sector in achieving carbon peak and carbon neutrality goals in a scientifically sound manner.  © 2025 The Author(s), published by EDP Sciences.

titulo: Research on multi-dimensional cost co-optimization for entire life cycle damage resistance of tower-line systems based on an improved WOA
fonte_periodico: Proceedings of 2025 2nd International Conference on Energy Technology and Electrical Power Etep 2025
resumo: In recent years, extreme weather disasters have become increasingly frequent, highlighting the growing need for power grid resilience. The coordinated optimization of economic benefits under the damage-resistant coordination capability of tower-line systems has emerged as a critical issue. Therefore, this paper investigates the optimization of multi-dimensional damage-resistant costs throughout the entire life cycle of tower-line systems. First, the investment composition of tower-line systems across their entire life cycle is analyzed. Subsequently, a correlation analysis is conducted on construction investment, operation and maintenance costs, safety indicators, and environmental costs throughout the entire life cycle. A coupled model linking the engineering safety, economic viability, and environmental impact of transmission tower-line systems from a life cycle perspective is established. Based on the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) with an improved convergence factor, optimization of the coupled economic performance of transmission line tower-line systems over their entire life cycle is pursued. This study investigates the dynamic equilibrium relationship among the "economic-safety-environmental"costs of engineering projects when enhancing the anti-damage coordination capability of transmission lines. It derives optimal strategies for improving engineering design under extreme meteorological conditions. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: A Multi-Level Software Supply Chain Security Defense System for Cloud-Native and High-Performance Computing Environments
fonte_periodico: 2025 International Conference on Frontiers of Information Technology Fit 2025
resumo: With the acceleration of the digital process, the software supply chain has become a key target of cyber attacks, and its security defense is facing severe challenges. This paper proposes to build a full-chain and multi-level security defense system for the software supply chain. By analyzing the security risks in each link of the full life cycle of software (development, construction, distribution, deployment, operation and maintenance), the paper systematically expounds the construction path of the defense system from three dimensions: technical defense, management mechanism and external collaboration. The research shows that embedding security into all links of the full life cycle, combined with SBOM-based technical tools, standardized management processes and ecological collaboration mechanisms, can realize the transformation from "passive response"to "active defense", providing a comprehensive solution for resisting supply chain attacks. This framework is particularly applicable to cloud-native CI/CD pipelines and high-performance computing environments, where distributed software components and large-scale deployment increase the complexity and risk of supply chain attacks. © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: Cooperative defense; full life cycle defense; Management mechanism; software supply chain security; Technical defense system

titulo: Life Cycle Cost Modeling and Application of Electric Energy Metering Equipment Based on ADC-LCC
fonte_periodico: 2025 4th International Conference on Energy Power and Electrical Technology Icepet 2025
resumo: The procurement decisions of traditional metering equipment often focus excessively on short-term costs, thus ignoring the operation and maintenance costs over the entire lifecycle and the risks of reliability. This paper constructs a decision-making model that integrates the Life Cycle Cost (LCC) and the Effectiveness Evaluation (ADC). By quantifying the costs of the whole process of equipment from procurement to scrapping (covering 18 cost elements in 8 major stages), and combining it with the effectiveness evaluation system of Availability (A), Dependability (D), and Capability (C), a comprehensive indicator of the cost-effectiveness ratio (E/LCC) is formed, providing scientific support for the procurement decisions of power grid enterprises. Empirical analysis shows that this model can effectively identify and quantify the coupling relationship between the full-cycle costs and effectiveness of metering equipment, verifying its application value in optimizing procurement decisions and improving the economy and reliability of the power grid. © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: ADC (Availability-Dependability-Capacity) performance evaluation; cost-effectiveness ratio; cost-performance optimization; electricity meter procurement; Life Cycle Cost (LCC)

titulo: Research and Application of Full Lifecycle Management Strategies for Power Data
fonte_periodico: Proceedings 2025 International Conference on Electrical Drives Power Electronics and Engineering Edpee 2025
resumo: The research and application of electric power data full lifecycle management strategy aims to improve the data management efficiency and decision support capability of electric power enterprises. This paper first discusses the importance of full lifecycle management of electric power data, emphasizing the key role of data quality for electric power enterprise operations, report generation, compliance, and potential law mining. Then, the article elaborates the strategy of full life cycle management of electric power data, including the key phases of data planning and design, operation and maintenance, and protection, as well as the specific management content and methods of each phase. The study verifies through simulation experiments that the system in this paper shows excellent recognition efficiency in comparison with the traditional system, with a maximum accuracy of 1.00 and a minimum of 0.94.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Spatiotemporal Life Cycle Assessment of Solar Photovoltaic Power Systems in Brazil: A Dynamic Framework for Environmental Impact Analysis
fonte_periodico: Conference Record of the IEEE Photovoltaic Specialists Conference
resumo: The rapid expansion of photovoltaic (PV) deployment in Brazil has raised the cumulative installed capacity to 52.1 GW in 2025. It highlights the importance of comprehensive environmental assessment methods for renewable energy systems. This study conducted a spatiotemporal life cycle assessment (LCA) of a 50 MWp utility-scale PV power plant in Brazil, utilizing a novel LCA framework that addresses the inherent variability of solar energy systems across different geographical locations and periods. The analyzed system features monocrystalline silicon modules installed in a mounted configuration with trackers, a 30% capacity factor, and a generation profile of 118,114 MWh/year, over 25 years. The research methodology employs openLCA software combined with ecoinvent v.3.10 database and the ReCiPe 2016 method to perform a spatiotemporally explicit LCA across four life-cycle phases: component manufacturing, construction and installation, operation and maintenance, and decommissioning. Environmental impacts were assessed through key categories, including mineral human toxicity, land use, climate change, and water use. This comprehensive approach provides valuable contributions for policymakers and stakeholders by identifying critical life-cycle stages and their associated environmental impacts. The study demonstrates how emerging tools can facilitate the practical application of spatiotemporal LCA while maintaining robust analytical capabilities, supporting strategic decisions regarding PV deployment in Brazil's expanding solar energy sector. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Research on the Application of Artificial Intelligence in Landscape Design of Urban Parks
resumo: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, its application in urban park landscape design has gradually attracted attention. This paper systematically discusses the application of AI in the whole life cycle of urban park landscape design, including demand analysis and data-driven decision-making in the early stage of design, intelligent generation and optimization in the middle stage of design and intelligent operation and maintenance and ecological monitoring in the late stage of design. Through case study, the application path of AI technology in a smart park is analyzed, and the advantages of AI in improving the scientific design, optimizing resource allocation and enhancing ecological benefits are demonstrated. At the same time, in view of the technical, social, ecological and economic challenges, the corresponding countermeasures are put forward, which provide theoretical support and practical guidance for the deep integration of AI and landscape design and promote the improvement of the quality of urban public space. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.
palavras_chave: Artificial Intelligence; Landscape Design; Urban Parks

titulo: RESEARCH ON TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE AND APPLICATION OF POWER GRID DIGITAL DELIVERY BASED ON BIM+GIS
resumo: Building Information Model (BIM) technology supports the fine design and management of power grid with its 3D modeling, information integration and cooperative operation capabilities. Geographic Information System (GIS) technology shows its potential in power grid planning, resource allocation and emergency response with its spatial analysis, geographic positioning and data visualization functions. The technical framework proposed in this study takes data as the core, platform as the support and application as the guidance, and realizes the digital and intelligent management of the whole life cycle of power grid. The features of this architecture include data fusion, platform collaboration, comprehensive application and intelligent decision-making. Key technologies include data fusion technology of BIM and GIS, 3D modeling and visualization technology, and optimization of digital delivery process. Through the application research of a smart grid project in a city, the remarkable effect of BIM+GIS fusion technology in improving design efficiency, construction accuracy and operation and maintenance management level is verified. At the same time, this paper also analyzes the challenges encountered in technology implementation, and puts forward corresponding solutions, including formulating unified data standards, promoting platform standardization and talent training, so as to promote the development and application of BIM+GIS fusion technology in power grid digital delivery. © The Institution of Engineering & Technology 2025.

titulo: Multi-level Intelligent Operation and Maintenance Platform of Digital Station Based on Cloud Edge-End Architecture
resumo: With the need to build a new power system, the scale of power grid equipment is expanding day by day, and the existing substation operation and maintenance system is complex, which is responsible for the collection and control of different equipment information. The data between each system is separated, resulting in a large number of duplication and it is difficult to be effectively used. How to build an efficient and unified operation and maintenance platform has become a big problem. By combining the advantages of cloud computing and edge computing, and integrating the multi-source data collection with substation equip- ment, the substation intelligent multi-level operation and maintenance platform with cloud edge-end architecture is proposed. First, it explains how the platform combines cloud side collaboration, panoramic twin, multi-source data collection, cloud native life cycle management and other technologies. Then, the platform design scheme is explained through multi-level data, business architecture and station application architecture, and explains the data collection, business division and cloud-edge collaboration of the platform. Finally, the platform applications of the cloud and the station side are displayed respectively, reflecting the advan- tages of the cloud side side architecture platform in overall control and efficient response. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2025.
palavras_chave: Cloud Edge-end; Cloud Native; Digital Twin; Smart Substation

titulo: BIM-FM INTEGRATION THROUGH OPENBIM: SOLUTIONS FOR INTEROPERABILITY TOWARDS EFFICIENT OPERATIONS
fonte_periodico: Journal of Information Technology in Construction
resumo: Facility Management (FM) faces ongoing challenges related to data interoperability and information loss during the transition from construction to operation phases, compromising asset management efficiency. Although Building Information Modeling (BIM) can optimize the flow of information exchange by offering a single, centralized model, the lack of standardization and interoperability issues between BIM and FM limit the full exploitation of its advantages. This study aims to develop a solution that integrates BIM and FM, using open standards like IFC to mitigate data loss and ensure continuous updates of BIM models throughout the construction and commissioning phases. The proposal aims to provide the facilities team with a BIM model containing the minimum necessary and reliable common information for the start of operations. The methodology adopted is based on Design Science Research (DSR) and includes the development of an artefact composed of four components: (1) a compendium of minimum common information requirements for various assets, (2) a web platform for continuous management of this information, (3) a Representational State Transfer API (Application Programming Interface) that ensures interoperability between different systems, and (4) an add-on for the Blender system, utilizing Bonsai (previously known as BlenderBIM) as the IFC modeler, which guarantees bidirectional data exchange between the web platform and BIM models, ensuring continuous verification and updating. The results show that the proposed artifacts are effective in mitigating interoperability difficulties, centralizing critical information, and continuously verifying data. The use of IFC promoted greater flexibility and standardization, resulting in more efficient and integrated asset management. The proposed solution offered a practical and sustainable approach for the construction industry, significantly contributing to the improvement of operational processes and information management throughout the asset lifecycle by decoupling from the limitations imposed by proprietary software. © 2025 The author(s).

titulo: Future directions: practical challenges, human dimensions, and long-term impact in robotics and artificial intelligence in sports medicine and sports services
fonte_periodico: Robotics and Artificial Intelligence in Sports Medicine and Sports Services
resumo: This volume examines the transformative role of robotics and artificial intelligence (AI) in sports medicine and services. It highlights advanced technologies such as AI-integrated wearables, brain-computer interfaces, and virtual and augmented reality in rehabilitation. The text also addresses the application of robotic exoskeletons in recovery and athletic performance enhancement. Additionally, it explores the evolving functions of robots in sports, from humanoid coaching to stadium logistics. By mapping the research landscape and addressing ethical considerations, this comprehensive guide presents new opportunities for professionals in sports medicine, rehabilitation, and facility operations. The volume concludes with a strategic roadmap for future developments, directing professionals toward sustainable, human-centered innovation. This book is essential for healthcare professionals, sports scientists, AI researchers, engineers, industry leaders, and policymakers keen on the latest advancements in sports medicine. It also appeals to athletes, coaches, fans, and sports communities interested in innovative technologies, featuring clear language and striking visuals. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

titulo: A Modular Ontology Stack for Integrating OpenBIM and Bayesian Structural Health Monitoring and Prediction
resumo: The Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry faces persistent challenges in integrating heterogeneous data for structural health monitoring (SHM) and facility management, specifically in capturing time-dependent degradation, probabilistic models reflecting uncertainty, and damage semantics. This paper proposes a Linked Data framework that extends Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) with semantic web technologies to address these gaps. By converting IFC data into a Resource Description Framework (RDF) graph via modular ontologies-including BOT, SOSA/SSN, OPM, DOT, and a custom LifeMACS Ontology (LFM)-The framework enables rich semantic queries, provides inputs for probabilistic analyses, and cross-domain interoperability. A Python-based conversion pipeline automates the translation of IFC geometry, sensor data, and inspection records into an RDF knowledge graph, while SPARQL queries demonstrate advanced capabilities, such as probabilistic crack-length or sensor value assessments and realtime data integration. A case study on a deteriorating reinforced concrete bridge validates the approach, showcasing its potential for improved statistical parsing directly using the RDF graph. Results highlight the framework's potential to connect static infrastructure data with dynamic lifecycle parameters. The work highlights the potential of semantic web technologies in advancing digital twin capabilities for the AEC industry.  © 2025 Copyright for this paper by its authors. titulo: Sustainability and Profitability in Social Housing: Evaluation of a Bioclimatic Envelope for Warm Tropical Climates
resumo: This article assesses the environmental and economic feasibility of a bioclimatic envelope prototype designed for social housing in warm, dry tropical climates. The assessment is based on a case study conducted in Cali, Colombia. An integrated methodology combining Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA) was applied to quantify cumulative CO2 equivalent emissions and operation and maintenance costs over a 60-year horizon. The evaluation used energy simulations, the adaptive thermal comfort model (ASHRAE 55), and projected climate scenarios for 2020, 2050, and 2080. The results suggest that the prototype studied proves the lowest cumulative cost (COP $16.14 million, approximately USD $4,000) and the lowest estimated emissions among the five options analyzed. Furthermore, it was the only option that yielded a positive cost-benefit ratio in the long term, reaching a value of 3.05 by 2080. This finding supports the benefits of integrating LCA and CBA as a combined analytical tool for decision-making in passive design for social housing, particularly in urban contexts vulnerable to climate change and subject to significant budgetary constraints. © (2025), (American Meteorological Society). All rights reserved.

titulo: Integrating artificial intelligence, building information modeling, and augmented reality to enhance facility maintenance
resumo: Lack of sufficient experience and easy access to previous historical and technical information on maintenance operations, along with various changes in maintenance staff, increase cost and decrease life cycle of building facilities. This study addresses this problem by presenting a framework to (1) use historical experience for a location-aware maintenance solution recommendation and (2) improve access to building facilities’ technical and historical information on-site. For this purpose, the framework integrates three digital technologies: Augmented Reality (AR), Building Information Model (BIM), and Artificial Intelligence (AI). The framework enables communication with facility managers and staff by natural language with the aid of the AI module. This module also employs case-based reasoning to recommend appropriate solutions using previous successful maintenance operations. The BIM module includes facility information and its maintenance history. The AR module recognizes elements on-site with electronic mobile devices and represents information about facilities. A University building case study is employed to evaluate the practicality and effectiveness of the proposed framework. Facility managers and staff of this building used the implemented framework and indicated that this framework is easy to use and suggests appropriate maintenance solutions. © 2025 Informa UK Limited, trading as Taylor & Francis Group.

titulo: Integrating interdependency effects into coastal bridge resilience against hurricane-induced waves within a life-cycle context
autores: Zhu, DM; Dong, Y; Chan, PW; Bastidas-Arteaga, E
resumo: The life-cycle hurricane resilience assessment of coastal bridges plays an important role in guiding decisions for their long-term operation and maintenance. Although some studies focused on bridge resilience under other disasters, there remains a paucity of resilience assessment methods associated with hurricanes and extreme waves. To address this issue, this study proposes a three-step resilience assessment framework to evaluate structural performance under hurricane hazards. Such a framework improves the existing method from the following aspects: (a) characterization of structural responses under extreme waves using a numerical-based Pseudo-Fluid-Structure-Interaction (PFSI) scheme, (b) consideration of the restoration of interdependent infrastructure systems at the pre-recovery phase, and (c) multiple resilience indices that integrate the effects of resources and recovery time. The developed framework is illustrated using a high-risk coastal bridge. A multi-criteria optimization problem is formulated to examine the practical value of the proposed resilience indices. The results of the developed framework are compared with the method without considering the effects of time delay, which shows that the bias could reach 15% under extreme cases. The proposed approach could facilitate decision-making by integrating multiple performance indices of coastal bridges into the decision-making process, thereby aiding decision-makers in optimizing their objectives. © 2025 Informa UK Limited, trading as Taylor & Francis Group.

titulo: Research on the Conceptual Model and Technical Reference Architecture of the Digital Twin Equipment System
fonte_periodico: 2025 IEEE 7th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence Computer Science and Information Processing Aicsip 2025
resumo: As an essential tool for digital transformation and a typical representative of new quality productivity, the application of digital twin technology in the full life cycle of equipment has significant advantages. In other words, digital twin can significantly improve design efficiency, optimize manufacturing processes, enhance operation and maintenance levels, enhance decision support capabilities, and help to achieve digital empowerment, networked interconnection, intelligent upgrading of equipment. In this paper, a conceptual model of digital twin equipment system which consists of target equipment, twin interaction, and digital entities is defined. Finally, the technical reference architecture of the digital twin equipment system including target equipment layer, twin interactive layer, digital entity layer and twin service layer is described. In conclusion, we analyzed the application ideas and effects of digital twin technology in equipment design simulation, status monitoring, fault diagnosis, and status prediction.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Case study on analysing whole carbon emissions based on actual energy consumption in existing buildings
resumo: The recent IPCC 6th Assessment Report (AR6) introduced for the first time the concept of calculating carbon emissions over the entire life cycle of a building, i.e. including the embodied carbon (EC) emissions generated in the material production, construction, operation and maintenance, and decommissioning/ disposal phases of a building. In this study, operational carbon emissions (OC) were calculated for existing buildings based on actual energy consumption, and embodied emissions (EC) were also calculated for the amount of construction materials initially used at the time of completion. The Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) method was used to calculate total carbon emissions. The target building is a three-story mixed-use building (residential and commercial), and energy consumption data such as electricity and city gas consumption by use were collected. In addition, since mixed-use buildings have inconsistent occupancy schedules, the results of the separation of baseline energy use were used to calculate OC emissions in order to accurately predict the cooling and heating energy saving effect of specific facility improvements in consideration of the seasonal use characteristics of cooling and heating energy. As a result, the largest part of the life cycle carbon emissions of the building is the operation phase, which accounts for 84.47% of the total carbon emissions. The materials production phase was the second largest contributor with 15.12% of the total carbon emissions. Finally, we concluded that carbon emissions can be controlled not only by energy source, but also by whether a building is occupied or unoccupied. © 2025 Building Simulation Conference Proceedings. All rights reserved.

titulo: Research on the Whole Life Cycle Management of Water Conservancy Project Based on K-means Algorithm
resumo: Research on full life cycle management in water conservancy engineering is currently limited, resulting in issues like improper project siting, high construction costs, and insufficient risk management capabilities. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an innovative management approach using the K-means clustering algorithm. This method leverages the K-means algorithm’s simplicity and fast convergence to cluster and analyze diverse data from different stages of water conservancy projects. It then presents these clustering results visually to assist project managers in making informed decisions. Using the K-means algorithm in the planning and design stage of water conservancy projects as an example, we demonstrate its feasibility, efficiency, and scientific rigor in managing the entire project life cycle. The research findings indicate the following: The research results show that (1) In the planning and design stage, the K-means algorithm aids in making informed decisions about engineering construction sites by clustering and analyzing relevant data. (2) The improved K-means clustering algorithm exhibits high processing efficiency and accuracy when handling various types of water conservancy project data. (3) The Kmeans algorithm’s application can span the construction, operation, and maintenance stages. It can cluster and analyze data related to material consumption, equipment usage, construction efficiency, and quality, ensuring compliance with quality standards, cost control, and project optimization. Additionally, it can be used to cluster and analyze data akin to water conservancy projects, like historical risk factors, aiding in risk evaluation and prediction. © The Author(s) 2025.
