titulo: Advancing Sustainable Infrastructure Management: Insights from System Dynamics
autores: Juarez-Quispe, J; Rojas-Chura, E; Vigil, AJE; Malaga, MS; Yabar-Ardiles, O; Anco-Valdivia, J; Valencia-Félix, S
resumo: Rapid infrastructure growth in developing countries has intensified environmental challenges due to cost-prioritizing practices over sustainability. This study evaluates 21 identified sustainable-driving tools to improve the management of infrastructure throughout its life cycle, by interacting with 20 out of 36 key infrastructure system management variables (ISMVs). Using a systems thinking approach, a Sustainable Systems Dynamic Model (SSDM) is developed, comprising a nucleus representing the interconnected stages of the life cycle: planning and design (S1), procurement (S2), construction (S3), operation and maintenance (S4), and renewal and disposal (S5). The model incorporates a total of 12 balance (B) and 25 reinforcement (R) loops, enabling the visualization of critical interdependencies that influence the sustainability of the system. In addition, its analysis shows the interdependencies between variables and stages, demonstrating, for example, how the implementation of tools such as LCA, BIM, and Circular Economy principles in S1, or IoT and SHM in S4, significantly improve sustainability. A gap between theory and practice in the adoption of sustainable practices is identified, which is aggravated by the lack of knowledge in specific developing countries’ context. Hence, this study contributes to its closure by offering a model that facilitates the understanding of key interactions in infrastructure systems. © 2025 by the authors.

titulo: Case Study: Developing a Methodology to Quantify Benefit-Cost Ratio Associated with a Complete Road Closure
fonte_periodico: Airfield and Highway Pavements 2025 Design Construction Condition Evaluation and Management of Pavements Selected Papers from the International Airfield and Highway Pavements Conference 2025
resumo: Benefit-cost analysis (BCA) is a well-established method for assessing the economic effectiveness of a roadway construction project (the “Build” scenario) in comparison to a “NoBuild” scenario. The primary components of this analysis are costs and benefits. Costs associated with the Build option are evaluated against those of the No-Build option to estimate the overall benefits and costs of the construction scenario. The costs of a roadway alternative primarily include agency costs and user costs over a specified analysis period. Agency costs encompass pre-engineering expenses, initial construction costs, and ongoing operation and maintenance (O&M) costs, while user costs cover travel time, vehicle operating costs, safety, emissions, and health impacts. In this study, a methodology was developed to estimate these costs and benefits, allowing for an assessment of economic effectiveness relative to the No-Build case. The methodology was successfully applied to a construction project, and sensitivity analyses were performed on factors such as traffic growth rate, discount rate, and detour length. Notably, at a projected traffic growth rate of 0%, the project yielded a favorable benefit-cost ratio (BCR) of 3.66 and a net present value (NPV) of $5,063,753. These results demonstrate that the proposed construction project is a valuable and cost-effective investment, underscoring the necessity for timely infrastructure improvements to enhance overall transportation efficiency and safety. © ASCE.

titulo: Physics-informed Remaining Useful Life Prediction for Rotating Machinery
resumo: Rotating machinery often experiences fatigue and degradation under complex loads and extreme conditions. Accurately predicting their remaining useful life (RUL) is thus essential for system safety and efficient maintenance. At the same time, the rotating machinery degradation trend is nonlinear with significant individual differences, and it is difficult to accurately learn the physical degradation mechanism by relying only on the original sample data, which can easily lead to a lack of generalization and physical consistency in the prediction results. To address the above problems, this paper proposes an enhanced Transformer architecture that incorporates prior physical knowledge, referred to as the Physics-informed Transformer (PI-Transformer). The model employs a multi-layer self-attention mechanism in the encoder to deeply extract degradation-related temporal features. It innovatively incorporates prior knowledge of crack propagation by constructing a physical neuron module, and further integrates physical features with data-driven features through nonlinear fusion using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN). Experiments on real rotating machinery full life cycle data show that the method in this paper excels in accuracy, stability and interpretability, providing a new methodology support for intelligent operation and maintenance of industrial equipment. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Research on Carbon Reduction Potential of the SMA Asphalt Mixture in Life Cycle
resumo: To research the carbon emissions of SMA asphalt mixture, SMA-13 and AC-13 asphalt mixtures were selected for comparative analysis, and the carbon emission amounts during the construction period and operation maintenance period were calculated. The research results indicated that the carbon emissions of SMA-13 during the construction period increased by 20.63% compared to AC-13; however, due to the improved performance, SMA-13 could reduce one preventive maintenance and one repair maintenance project compared to AC-13 within the design life. Therefore, the carbon emissions during the operation and maintenance period of SMA-13 could be reduced by 21.26% compared to AC-13, meanwhile with better performance. Based on the life cycle theory, SMA-13 could reduce comprehensive carbon emissions by 11.40% compared to AC-13. Therefore, SMA has better long-term carbon reduction capabilities and is an ideal durable green low-carbon technology for roads. It should be widely promoted and applied in national roads construction. © Published under licence by IOP Publishing Ltd.

titulo: Comprehensive Evaluation of Economic Efficiency and Environmental Impact of Airport Water Surface Photovoltaic System Based on Particle Swarm Algorithm
fonte_periodico: International Conference on Intelligent Communication Networks and Computational Techniques Icicnct 2025
resumo: This study aims to construct a multi-objective comprehensive evaluation model for airport water surface photovoltaic systems, optimizing both the levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) and carbon reduction benefits. First, an economic model incorporating PV module efficiency degradation, water surface reflection gain, and operation and maintenance costs, and an environmental model accounting for carbon emissions over the entire life cycle, were established. Second, a multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm was employed, with the objective functions of minimizing LCOE and maximizing carbon reduction benefits. Particle positions were dynamically adjusted using a velocity update formula, and the Pareto frontier was used to screen nondominated solutions. For an airport water surface with an annual irradiation of 1600 kWh/m2, the algorithm optimized the LCOE to 0.21 yuan/kWh, reducing annual carbon emissions by 250,000 tons of CO2. The optimal solution set demonstrates a balance between economic and environmental benefits when the module tilt angle is 35° and the installation density is 0.8MW/ha. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Research on the Application of Digital Twin Technology in Intelligent Maintenance of Steel Equipment
fonte_periodico: Safeprocess 2025 14th Caa Symposium on Fault Detection Supervision and Safety for Technical Processes
resumo: In the field of iron and steel industry, the equipment maintenance support system is crucial to maintaining the operational efficiency and reliability of equipment. However, the traditional maintenance mode based on historical data has time lag and analytical limitations, making it difficult to meet the real-time and accurate guarantee needs of modern complex equipment. With the characteristics of bidirectional mapping between virtual and physical entities and dynamic collaboration, digital twin technology brings innovation to the whole life cycle management of equipment, and can significantly improve the efficiency of visual management and control, condition monitoring, fault diagnosis and maintenance decision-making. This paper focuses on the equipment maintenance support system in the iron and steel industry. It first clarifies the scope of guarantee and core elements, then constructs a digital twin theoretical model and analyzes its architectural composition. Based on the bidirectional flow of twin data, it designs a technical operation and maintenance framework and overcomes the key technical problems in platform construction, providing theoretical and practical solutions for the intelligent upgrading of the industry.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: The Importance of Collaboration Throughout Transition into New Phases in Facility Lifecycles
fonte_periodico: Proceedings of the Nuclear Criticality Safety Division 2025 Conference Ncsd 2025
resumo: Two spent fuel reprocessing facilities at Sellafield Ltd have ceased operations in the last decade, with the associated Plutonium Finishing Lines also being rundown recently. Upon cessation of operations, these facilities transitioned to the ‘remediation’ phase of their lifecycle. Remediation may be defined as ‘the process of improving or correcting a situation’. In this instance, remediating these reprocessing facilities and associated Plutonium Finishing Lines involves conducting a post-operational clean out (POCO) followed by decommissioning. Entering this new phase resulted in several plutonium bearing liquor streams being generated that required appropriate treatment and/or disposal. The remaining effluent produced from the final Finishing Line operations required an alternative disposal route, as the effluent recycle route between the Finishing Lines and reprocessing facilities was no longer available. In addition, the washout of the facilities resulted in generation of some plutonium bearing wash liquors that also needed to be disposed of via this alternative route. The alternative route(s) identified for the treatment and disposal of these liquors involves them being returned to their respective upstream reprocessing facility from the Finishing Line, through which they must be transferred, via routes which have historically handled liquors with only trace quantities of plutonium, to reach the Highly Active Liquor (HAL) treatment facilities for blending with HAL and disposal via Vitrification. Executing this operation required collaboration and innovative thinking on various fronts. This was fundamentally because an existing engineered route was going to be used for a different purpose. It needed to be ensured that it was viable to do so operationally, programmatically, and safely. Hence, criticality safety assessors had to consult and liaise with various disciplines to problem solve and develop robust criticality hazard management strategies to enable the operation. Engineering expertise had to be sought to ensure that plant equipment could fulfil its function, from both an operational and safety perspective. Help from technical experts was required to develop chemistry-based arguments that underpinned criticality safety arguments. Close working with human factors specialists was needed to ensure that there was adequate confidence in novel operator instructions and the ability to implement criticality hazard management strategies. Furthermore, multiple facilities were affected by the totality of operations. There was an obvious need for coordination and communication between these facilities to ensure integration of work planning and to mitigate programmatic impacts. This was difficult at times due to differing priorities and experience amongst the impacted facilities management teams, and the constraints within the individual facilities that had broader impacts. This paper details the successes and challenges encountered throughout this process, where there was a requirement for multiple disciplines and facilities to collaborate in new ways to develop a fit for purpose safety case and enable high hazard risk reduction. © Proceedings of the Nuclear Criticality Safety Division 2025 Conference, NCSD 2025. All rights reserved.

titulo: Research Progress and Prospects of Carbon Emission Calculation and Low-Carbon Performance Evaluation of Bridge Engineering
resumo: To bolster China s bridge engineering in realizing low-carbon development, the research progress of carbon emission calculation and low-carbon Performance evaluation of bridge engineering is studied. The research on carbon emission calculation of bridge engineering mainly involves two categorics; the calculation of carbon emission of a specific bridge and the comparison of carbon emissions of different bridges. For the calculation of carbon emission of a specific bridge, the emission factor method is generally used to calculate the carbon emission of bridges. The carbon emissions of bridges mainly come from the material produetion, Operation, and maintenance. The carbon emissions during the material produetion stage mainly come from concrete and stccl. For the comparison of carbon emissions of different bridges, the influence of critical Parameters, such as material type and structural form, on the life-cycle carbon emissions of bridges is clarified. The research on low-carbon Performance evaluation of bridge engineering mainly includes two categories: the evaluation method of low-carbon Performance and the comprehensive evaluation System of bridges. For the evaluation method of low-carbon Performance, various low-carbon Performance rating and scoring methods based on the weight System are proposed. For the comprehensive evaluation System of bridges, the relationship between the low-carbon Performance and other Performances, such as economy and reliability, is preliminarily established. Suggestions and prospects are put forward for the insufficiencies in these four categories of research in the following aspects: the bridgc emission factor database and the impact of construction methods on bridge life-cycle carbon emissions need to be further studied; the bridge low-carbon Performance evaluation method based on big data should bc adopted to avoid subjective bias caused by the weight System; the bridge comprehensivc evaluation System should takc the coneepts of carbon emission index, environmental cost, and life-cycle cost into consideration in the bridge scheme design and education thoughts, which should also be the ultimate goal of carbon emission research of bridge engineering. © 2025 Wuhan Bridge Media Co., Ltd., MBEC. titulo: A State Evaluation Method for Distribution Network Secondary Equipment Based on Whole Process Integration and Deep Learning
fonte_periodico: 2025 7th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology Icpet 2025
resumo: Aiming at the problem of state evaluation of distribution network secondary equipment, a method integrating whole process integration and deep learning is proposed. Firstly, the whole process integration technology breaks the data barriers in all stages of the equipment life cycle, collects multi-source heterogeneous data including operation parameters, environmental data, maintenance records, etc., and transmits them to the processing center. The Transformer model is used for data fusion processing. Through operations such as local and global feature extraction and multi-head self-attention mechanism, combined with combined pooling and attention layer, effective features are obtained. Then, the trained and optimized model is applied to actual evaluation, and the equipment state results are output to provide decision support for operation and maintenance. In the case analysis, monitoring data from multiple regions in China are selected, and the data set is divided according to 7:2:1. The experimental results show that the proposed method has the shortest training time and the highest evaluation accuracy under different data volumes, effectively improving the accuracy and reliability of the state evaluation of distribution network secondary equipment.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: A Systematic Causality-Based Model for Risk Assessment and Management of Change in Chemical Plant Lifecycle
resumo: The lifecycle of a chemical plant includes development, design, construction, operation, maintenance, and decommissioning phases. When changes are proposed, primarily during the operation and maintenance phases, risk assessments are conducted to evaluate both implementing and not implementing the changes. When implementing a change leads to risk reduction, the process returns to the development and/or design phases for redevelopment and/or redesign. Among the risk assessment methods, HAZOP is widely used. When modifications qualify as Replacement In Kind (RIK), redevelopment and/or redesign efforts are reduced, making RIK determination essential. On the other hand, the business process model (BPM) structures engineering activities and information flows but lacks an explicit design rationale representation. This study proposes a systematic causality-based model to systematically represent the design rationale, aiding a logical and efficient RIK determination. A case study examined risk assessment, focusing on reactor minimum flow conditions and their impact on a downstream distillation column. The proposed model identified potential hazards and was cross-referenced with HAZOP results, confirming comprehensive identification of key examination points, including control system considerations beyond HAZOP's scope. Therefore, the proposed model enhances the consistency between PHA results and design rationale, ensuring a structured and transparent approach to change management. © 2025 Elsevier B.V.. All rights reserved.

titulo: Lifetime Modeling of IGBT Devices Based on Micro-Defect Topography Inversion
fonte_periodico: 2025 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Asia Wipda Asia 2025
resumo: As a key component of traction transmission system, the reliability of power electronic devices is an important guarantee of system safety. However, the existing studies mainly focus on the life assessment of the bathtub curve failure loss period, and lack the state characterization and remaining life prediction methods of the bathtub curve random failure period. In this paper, the solder layer CT scanning results of IGBT devices are combined with the finite element simulation model to invert the fatigue degree of the alive mesh through the stress relation between the dead and alive mesh and the microscopic representation of the Coffin-Manson model. The health state of the device is evaluated according to the void distribution in the solder layer during the random failure period, and the corresponding residual life model of the IGBT device is established to realize the life cycle evaluation of the IGBT device in service. The expected results of this paper enrich the life prediction and reliability evaluation of power devices, provide data basis for the continuous use of replaced IGBT modules, and thus reduce system operation and maintenance costs, which has important strategic value and economic significance. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Design and Application of an Intelligent Air-Conditioning Energy Consumption Monitoring System
fonte_periodico: 2025 6th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Electromechanical Automation Aiea 2025
resumo: Under the background of energy crisis and 'double carbon' target, the energy consumption problem of air conditioning system needs to be solved urgently. The article introduces an intelligent monitoring system for air conditioning energy consumption based on GD32F303RCT6 microcontroller, which integrates WiFi, 4 G dual-mode communication, power metering, and infrared control to realize fine control of air conditioning equipments and full life cycle management of energy consumption data. The system is equipped with core functions such as remote control, energy consumption data collection and uploading, dual-network redundant communication, and lowpower operation, and supports the integrated design of 'end-end-management-cloud', which can significantly reduce the ineffective energy consumption of air conditioners, improve the efficiency of operation and maintenance, and is widely compatible with a variety of application scenarios. Future improvements include the introduction of infrared human body sensors, temperature and humidity and air quality monitoring sensors, and the addition of real-time data visualization, energy efficiency prediction and energy-saving strategy optimization functions to further enhance the system's level of intelligence and user experience. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: MinePCR: A Novel Lifecycle Management Approach for 3D Point Cloud Maps in Intelligent Mining Systems
resumo: The full lifecycle management of mine point cloud maps is a fundamental basis for efficient operation and maintenance as well as safety monitoring in intelligent mining. However, due to the sparse structural features and strong repetitiveness of underground roadways, point cloud data often exhibits high redundancy, and the accuracy of multi-source temporal map registration is insufficient, constraining the long-term consistency maintenance of the maps. To address this issue, this paper proposes a full lifecycle management framework for mine point cloud maps, named MinePCR (Mine Point Cloud Registration and Refinement), which is based on adaptive feature extraction and robust spatiotemporal registration. Experimental results demonstrate that this framework can achieve high-precision and high-efficiency point cloud map management in complex mine environments, providing a highly reliable 3D geoinformation foundation for safety control tasks such as roadway deformation monitoring and vehicle path planning. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Research and Practice of Digital and Intelligent Technologies for UHVDC Projects Driven by Beidou Centimeter-Level Spatiotemporal Reference
fonte_periodico: 2025 IEEE Pes Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Asia Isgt Asia 2025
resumo: Aiming at the core challenges of UHVDC (Ultra-High Voltage Direct Current) projects, such as the urgent need for precise management in complex geographical environments and prominent barriers in full-life-cycle data integration, this paper proposes and practices a digital twin technology system driven by Beidou centimeter-level spatiotemporal reference. With the goal of 'full-element collaboration among physical power grid, digital power grid, and business systems', the system constructs a '12345' technical architecture: relying on two pillars, namely the Beidou + 5G centimeter-level spatiotemporal reference network (with a positioning accuracy of ± 5 cm under strong electromagnetic interference) and the 'BIM + GIS + SCADA' full-chain modeling technology (with a point cloud classification accuracy of ≫ 98%); a three-level verification system is established covering macro transmission corridors (error ≪ 0.3 m), meso-scale devices (error ≪ 8 mm), and micro components (error ≪ 2 cm). Focusing on the optimization of four-dimensional performance indicators (accuracy, efficiency, reliability, and scalability), and through key technologies such as air-ground collaborative 3D data acquisition, terrain-adaptive modeling engine, and streaming data governance mechanism (Kafka + Flink engine with a throughput of 100,000 points/second), it realizes high-precision air-space-ground integrated modeling (global error ± 5 cm) and millisecond-level full-life-cycle data fusion (topological accuracy ≫ 99.97%). Verified by the Kunliulong DC project, this technology has successfully compressed fault response time to ≪ 30 minutes in five application scenarios, including active defense for personnel safety (zero near-electrical accident rate), intelligent equipment diagnosis (defect recognition rate 98.7%), and network-free emergency collaboration, significantly improving the intelligent operation and maintenance level and safety management capabilities of UHV projects. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Transforming Parking Facilities for Electric Vehicles: An Optimal Design
resumo: Electric vehicle (EV) adoption is growing rapidly across Canada and around the world. The federal government has committed to achieving 100% zero-emission car sales by 2035; however, challenges persist, particularly in the form of limited charging infrastructure and the resulting frustration among EV users. This paper addresses the issue with inadequate charging stations by emphasizing the significance of accurate prediction and strategic planning for meeting future charging station needs. In particular, this research provides an analysis for estimation of the number of required charging stations and aims at identifying optimum location selection strategies for EV charging stations in commercial buildings in Quebec. The research adopts an owner-centric approach, recognizing the importance of considering owners needs and frustrations in the planning process. The selection of the charging station locations is guided through minimization of the life cycle costs associated with EV charging infrastructure from an owner's perspective. In doing so, the proposed EV-MathOpt model incorporates factors such as equipment, operation, and maintenance costs. The findings of this study are expected to contribute valuable insights that not only address the immediate challenges faced by EV users but also align with broader goals of promoting sustainable transportation and meeting government mandates. In conclusion, this research serves as a critical step toward fostering a seamless and cost-effective transition to an electrified future in Quebec's and in broader spectrum North America commercial buildings. © Canadian Society for Civil Engineering 2025.

titulo: ADNOC Offshore Digital Factory: Advanced Decision-Making via System Performance and Risk Quantification
resumo: Leveraging the innovative ADNOC Offshore Digital Factory's concept of Reality Based Prescriptive Predictive Maintenance (RB-PsM/PdM) High-Fidelity models to predict future availability and throughput for each production stream, as well as the revenue and costs, and to identify those units which are the main contributors to loss of performance (culpabilities), in addition to generate additional 18+ Key Performance Indication represents the efficiency and reliability for the production stream as well as individual areas/sites. This approach aims to evaluate the impact of changes at the equipment, operations, and maintenance levels to enhance availability and throughput, assesses strategic and operational scenarios based on cost-benefit analysis, hence provides a digital solution for supporting business decision-making processes. ADNOC Business Outcomes: • Informed Standard Decision-Making Process: quantify the benefits and costs of options to modify asset operation & maintenance strategy or system design, as well as the probability of achieving an outcome. • Improve Reliability: identify and address the elements in the system that contribute the most to nonperformance and the root causes of downtime, leading to significant improvements in reliability and performance. • Improve Availability: assists in improving the availability of assets, units, and systems, supporting assessment of changes to operating and maintenance strategies, spare's philosophy, design and/or logistics. • Elevate Predictability: enhances the ability to predict and foresee system behavior, helping you better prepare for potential scenarios and outcomes. • Decrease Life Cycle Cost: help in reducing the overall life cycle costs associated with assets and systems by identifying areas for optimization and cost reduction. • Optimized Operations Strategy: helps in streamlining operations strategies for optimum performance and maximum profitability. • Improve Maintenance Strategy: enhance maintenance strategies and procedures for prolonged asset life and minimal downtime. • Optimize CapEx and OpEx: enable quantification and comparison of the benefits and costs of different alternatives. titulo: Lifecycle Data Archiving and Intelligent Analysis of Nuclear Power Plant Equipment Based on Digital Twin
resumo: The operation and maintenance of nuclear power plant equipment generate massive amounts of heterogeneous data. Effectively archiving and utilizing lifecycle data of such equipment is a key challenge in the ongoing digital transformation of the nuclear industry. As a virtual replica of physical assets, the digital twin enables real-time integration of data across the design, manufacturing, operation, and maintenance stages, providing a comprehensive view of equipment performance and intelligent analytical capabilities. This study proposes a digital twin-based framework for lifecycle data management and intelligent analysis of key nuclear power plant equipment. The framework includes data archiving structure design, intelligent fault diagnosis, and maintenance optimization methods. By synthesizing data from authoritative public sources, the study compares traditional methods with digital twin-driven intelligent analysis in terms of fault diagnosis accuracy, equipment reliability, and maintenance efficiency. Results show that digital twin technology can significantly improve fault diagnosis accuracy (from approximately 90% to over 99%), reduce unplanned outages and failure rates (by about 70%), and substantially lower operation and maintenance costs. These findings provide a valuable reference for the digitalized maintenance of nuclear power equipment and contribute to enhancing the safety and economic efficiency of nuclear power plants. Finally, the study discusses the challenges in standardization, data quality, and security during digital twin implementation and outlines future research directions. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2025.

titulo: Prospective Directions in the Computer Systems Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) Shaping Data Exchange for Cities Sustainability and Resilience
fonte_periodico: Eai Springer Innovations in Communication and Computing
resumo: Sustainability and resilience in addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges within construction rely on interoperability. In architecture, engineering, and facilities management, a model-centered approach using standardized information structures like industry foundation classes (IFC) is essential for data sharing. Achieving complete interoperability across domains requires further research, especially in modularizing IFC, normalizing tree structures, and ensuring language independence. This chapter focuses on IFC schema, highlighting upcoming developments like IFC 5 and “IFC x,” with a core emphasis on modularization to enhance domain interoperability. Improved links between building information modeling (BIM) and geographic information systems (GIS), along with Internet of Things (IoT) integration into BIM, are also discussed. The three functions of model view definitions (MVDs) play a crucial role in defining subsets of IFC, imposing limitations, and establishing software implementation levels. Anticipated refinements in IFC 5 will coordinate these functions into distinct projects, establishing a shared interoperability layer within the schema. Modularization in IFC 5 is expected to streamline module creation, enhance upkeep, ensure consistent implementations, predict release cycles, and reduce the time gap between release and tool availability. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

titulo: Indoor Voxel Visualisation For Tenant Occupants’ Environment, Health, And Safety
fonte_periodico: Proceedings of the International Conference on Computer Aided Architectural Design Research in Asia
resumo: This study developed the Indoor Voxel Visualisation (IVV) system to help building occupants comply with Environment, Health, and Safety (EHS) requirements by addressing their challenges in understanding regulatory requirements, design intent, and building performance in tenancy spaces. Following the Design Science Research Methodology, we conducted a proof of concept (PoC) to evaluate IVV’s effectiveness. The IVV system uses Building Information Modelling (BIM) and voxel-based representation to transform critical design intent into clear, actionable instructions for tenants, making it easier for them to follow EHS guidelines. Additionally, the system enhances long-term sustainability by archiving the design intent history, such as layout modifications. In a case study, IVV was shown to dynamically record and communicate tenant feedback, enabling designers to keep accessible, up-to-date records of changes and intent in a user-friendly interpretation. IVV also has potential applications in HVAC monitoring, fire equipment inspections, and evacuation route visualisation, with future integration of augmented reality (AR) anticipated to enhance spatial understanding for tenants further. This approach supports sustainable, human-centric management, contributing to an ideal framework for reducing incidents in facility management and promoting effective EHS compliance. © 2025 and published by the Association for Computer-Aided Architectural Design Research in Asia (CAADRIA), Hong Kong.

titulo: Economic analysis of integrated wind-power-fire-storage system during operation period
fonte_periodico: 2025 4th International Conference on Energy and Electrical Power Systems Iceeps 2025
resumo: Under the strategic background of China's "dual-carbon"goal, new energy will usher in a larger-scale development. Large-scale integration of new energy into the grid will cause a huge impact on the power system, and new energy consumption will face great pressure. This paper constructs a comprehensive economic evaluation model for the integrated wind, fire and storage system, and systematically analyzes the cost and benefit characteristics during the operation period. The cost composition adopts the whole life cycle cost method, including equipment investment cost, operation and maintenance cost, fuel dynamic cost and carbon emission environmental cost. Based on the multi-market coupling pricing model, it covers a variety of benefits. The design of the economic evaluation index system includes static payback period, dynamic payback period, kWh cost and other basic indicators. The empirical study takes the Kubuqi Desert New Energy Base Project in Inner Mongolia as an example to analyze the cost structure and revenue pattern under the integration of 16 million kilowatts of "wind, fire and storage". The study shows that the policy environment and market environment have a significant impact on the system economy, and the related technological progress and market mechanism improvement will continue to improve the system economic performance. © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: economic analysis; multi-energy complementation; new energy; wind-fire-storage system

titulo: Linking BrIM to BMS for bridges - Recommendations for integration into existing bridge management practice
fonte_periodico: IABSE Symposium Tokyo 2025 Environmentally Friendly Technologies and Structures Focusing on Sustainable Approaches Report
resumo: Bridge Information Model (BrIM) is nowadays still being understood as 3D geometric model only and its benefit mainly in replacing drawings as main deliverable in new bridge projects. Many bridge owners across the world anticipate that the value of BrIM is in the entire process, so it could be used throughout the structure's entire life cycle, from the initial design to being recycled at the end of its lifespan. Operation and maintenance data is currently collected in various forms and stored in different repositories as part of a Bridge Management Systems (BMS). To optimize maintenance of the individual structural asset and manage the portfolio, it is beneficial if BrIM and BMS are linked such that information can be exchanged seamlessly, also for existing structures that currently do not have a BrIM model. In our vision, the establishment of a universally accepted standardized framework for data exchange between disparate systems empowers bridge owners. This paper analyses the 28 responses collected from bridge authorities from 15 different countries across five continents and shows that bridge managers recognize the potential of BrIM to enhance their operations, the path to widespread adoption requires addressing data standardization, improving visualization tools, and ensuring compatibility with existing management systems. © 2025 IABSE Symposium Tokyo 2025: Environmentally Friendly Technologies and Structures: Focusing on Sustainable Approaches - Report All rights reserved.

titulo: Digital Twin Enabling Technologies for Advancing Road Engineering and Lifecycle Applications
resumo: Road infrastructure is facing significant digitalization challenges within the context of new infrastructure construction in China and worldwide. Among the advanced digital technologies, digital twin (DT) has gained prominence across various engineering sectors, including the manufacturing and construction industries. Specifically, road engineering has demonstrated a growing interest in DT and has achieved promising results in DT-related applications over the past several years. This paper systematically introduces the development of DT and examines its current state in road engineering by reviewing research articles on DT-enabling technologies, such as model creation, condition sensing, data processing, and interaction, as well as its applications throughout the lifecycle of road infrastructure. The findings indicate that research has primarily focused on data perception and virtual model creation, while real-time data processing and interaction between physical and virtual models remain underexplored. DT in road engineering has been predominantly applied during the operation and maintenance phases, with limited attention given to the construction and demolition phases. Future efforts should focus on establishing uniform standards, developing innovative perception and data interaction techniques, optimizing development costs, and expanding the scope of lifecycle applications to facilitate the digital transformation of road engineering. This review provides a comprehensive overview of state-of-the-art advancements in this field and paves the way for leveraging DT in road infrastructure lifecycle management. © 2024 THE AUTHORS

titulo: Application of BIM (Building Information Modelling) and Digital Twins (DTs) in the Lifecycle Management of Bridges and Viaducts
resumo: The growing adoption of the Building Information Modelling (BIM) in Brazil, based on the Decree N0 11,888 of January 22, 2024, has reached multiple segments of the construction industry, including Special Works of Art (SWA). While the design and structural analysis of bridges and viaducts are widely addressed in academic and technical forums, their operation and maintenance remain underexplored, especially due to the industry’s slow technological advancement. This gap has contributed to severe outcomes, including structural collapses and service interruptions. This way, this research work aims to explore how the Digital Twins (DT), derived from BIM-based models, can serve as strategic tools for the operation and maintenance of SWAs. Considering the Brazilian standards such as NBR 9452 and the information management principles from ISO 19650, this study proposes a framework that integrates sensor data into digital environments for real-time asset monitoring. A statistical survey of SWA inoperability in Brazil, along with the analysis of management inefficiencies and enabling technologies such as Autodesk Tandem, supports the discussion. The findings highlight the urgent need for digitization in infrastructure asset management and propose DT as a feasible solution for improving performance, safety, and longevity of bridges and viaducts. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

titulo: Integrated Physical Modeling with Live Data Base to Develop Exception Base Surveillance Engine for Deep Tight Gas Fields
fonte_periodico: Society of Petroleum Engineers SPE Conference at Oman Petroleum and Energy Show Opes 2025
resumo: This paper details the transformative journey of the Oman Shell Well Reservoir and Facility Management (WRFM) team in designing and deploying an advanced, automated, and engineering-based monitoring system. The initiative was driven by the need to enhance operational efficiency, ensure safety, and optimize resource utilization across oil and gas facilities. The team achieved this by developing an integrated digital solution that seamlessly connects real-time field data with an Integrated Visual Management (IVM) platform. By embedding engineering logic and physics-based models into the IVM system, the solution enables Exception-Based Surveillance (EBS) alarms to be triggered automatically. This innovation has revolutionized the monitoring process, reducing reliance on manual interventions and enabling faster, more accurate decision-making. The primary objective of the project was to streamline the tracking of safety and business-critical performance indicators by automating the surveillance of wells and surface facilities. This automation not only minimized the need for manual data monitoring but also established clear roles and responsibilities for various teams, including WRFM and Operations. By leveraging engineering calculations rooted in physics models and data-driven logic, the team developed a robust system capable of detecting critical issues such as well exceeding erosional velocity, tubing leaks, and other operational anomalies. To enhance usability, the system incorporates diagnostic plots for intuitive visualization and a consolidated event view that includes features such as user acknowledgment and automated email notifications. These functionalities ensure that issues are promptly identified, communicated, and addressed. The EBS engine, a core component of the system, delivers direct value by generating live, accurate, and instantaneous data-driven alarms. These alarms, when acted upon in a timely manner by the field and subsurface teams, have yielded significant operational and financial benefits. Key outcomes include: 1. 100% Well Integrity Compliance: The system ensures that all wells adhere to stringent integrity standards, mitigating potential hazards and safeguarding operational safety. This proactive approach has significantly reduced the risk of well failures and environmental incidents. 2. Reduction in Deferment reaction time: Since its implementation in May 2024, the deferment reaction time have successfully reduced 15%. This reduction has contributed to uninterrupted production, maximizing revenue generation and minimizing operational disruptions. 3. Reduction in Daily Well Review Process time: The automation of the daily well review process has led to a 20% improvement in Full-Time Equivalent (FTE) efficiency. This optimization has allowed for better resource allocation, reduced operational costs, and enhanced productivity. The integration of the IVM platform as a physical modeling tool for system performance, combined with real-time data from surface facilities and wells, represents a groundbreaking achievement in the oil and gas industry. This first-of-its-kind implementation involved hardwiring an operating envelope database with the IVM prediction engine, creating a robust, real-time, and fully automated data surveillance system that is linked to a physical gas field model. The system's ability to predict and monitor operational performance in real-time has set a new benchmark for efficiency and reliability in the sector. Beyond the immediate operational benefits, this innovation has broader implications for the industry. It demonstrates the potential of digital transformation to enhance safety, reduce costs, and improve decision-making processes. The success of this project underscores the importance of collaboration between engineering, data science, and operations teams in driving technological advancements. Furthermore, it highlights the value of leveraging real-time data and predictive analytics to address complex challenges in oil and gas operations. Through development of this automated monitoring system, a significant milestone is achieved in the evolution of well and facility management. By combining advanced engineering models, real-time data integration, and user-friendly visualization tools, the team has created a solution that not only addresses current operational challenges but also paves the way for future innovations in the industry. This project serves as a testament to the power of digital transformation in achieving operational excellence and driving sustainable growth. Copyright 2025, Society of Petroleum Engineers.

titulo: Virtual Exchange for Intercultural Education: A Powerful Combination for Transforming the Food Value Chain
resumo: Addressing climate change and promoting corporate social responsibility (CSR) in the food value chain (FVC) is a defining challenge of the twenty-first century, in order to achieve a more interconnected and sustainable world. This necessitates global collaboration and cross-cultural perspectives to generate innovative solutions to global challenges. Collaboration is highlighted as crucial for making systemic changes in society and business to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The World Economic Forum (WEF) and various organizations are prioritizing CSR and engaging in efforts to identify and address interconnected global issues. The virtual exchange (VE) model included interdisciplinary courses in hospitality management from the Netherlands, facilities management from Switzerland, English as a second language from Japan, and Climate Change/Resilience: Impact & Responses for a Sustainable Future from the US. The VE aimed to equip future leaders with the skills to undertake global initiatives by fostering collaborative teamwork among international universities and diverse disciplines. The primary challenges addressed in the FVC include finding solutions that span various industries, countries, regions, and cultures, as well as enhancing collaboration and analytical thinking skills. Sustainability is seen as empowering students to take accountability for their actions and contribute ideas for a sustainable future. However, it is acknowledged that their viewpoints may be shaped by their specific urban or national context. The experience of collaborating on sustainability initiatives is expected to enhance students’ knowledge, skills, understanding of values, and motivation for action. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

titulo: Industrial Archaeologies of Complex Palimpsests. Application of Semantic Web Technologies to Digitalise the Knowledge Path from Data to Interpretation
autores: Cui, CD; Cursi, S; Simeone, D; Fioravanti, A; Currà, E
fonte_periodico: PROCEEDINGS OF THE 11TH INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE OF AR.TEC. (SCIENTIFIC SOCIETY OF ARCHITECTURAL ENGINEERING), VOL 1, COLLOQUI.AT.E 2024
resumo: Semantic web technologies are today widely used across the Architecture, Engineering and Construction (AEC) sector for different scopes and activities during the building life cycle and the operation and maintenance phase. In the heritage field, the development of several methods to facilitate information exchange and interoperability between stakeholders represents a crucial issue in the current research scenario. Building information modelling and related technologies can address some of these challenges and limitations through relational database structure. However, there are still some open questions related to knowledge representation and management of complex heritage sites. This paper outlines the use of semantic web technologies and standards, such as Web Ontology Language and existing domain ontologies, to digitalize the knowledge path from data collection to interpretation for the documentation of heritage assets. Firstly, it briefly defines the methodologies, data structure, exchange formats, and relations of the different technology databases with their application in the digital interpretative processes. Then, the proposed framework is evaluated through an example of industrial archaeology application in a multi-layered historical site. The aim is to propose a framework to manage different information classes, inconsistencies and uncertainties, from preliminary data gathering and structuring to ontologies instantiation activity by representing the logical levels of connection. The final intent is to highlight the possibility of overcoming the limitations in the different heritage study and management approaches to give proper support during the decision-making process performed by multiple stakeholders. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

titulo: Digital and AI-Empowered Maintaining of Regional Infrastructures Integrally
resumo: The infrastructure digitalization was mainly focused on identifying the operational state of a single facility via varied types of data collected. The overall spatial land system on which the infrastructures are located is insufficiently modeled and investigated. Therefore, the systematic digital management of the life cycle of the infrastructures, including the planning, construction, operation, and management phases, is limited. These facts result in three main issues in infrastructure operation and maintenance: (1) It is difficult to integrate spatial, operational, maintenance, and management data in an integrated manner; (2) The information barriers between multiple management entities lead to the misalignment between the risk identification and subsequent management response; (3) The uncertainty of the management process exacerbates public distrust of infrastructure security. In this study, a national spatial management framework is developed to overcome the mentioned issues, where the infrastructure information is incorporated. The theory of holistic management is adopted to systematically summarize the problems in intelligent management throughout the entire lifecycle of infrastructure from three aspects: integration mechanism, coordination mechanism, and trust mechanism. On this basis, the key issues of how digital information in infrastructure can be integrated into the national spatial management system are addressed. The emerging artificial intelligence techniques, including multi-source data fusion, application-driven perception, and digital collaborative management, are integrated to develop digital empowerment of infrastructure a comprehensive management. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2025.
palavras_chave: heterogeneous data fusion; holistic management; infrastructure digitalization; Territorial space management

titulo: Digital Twins for Intelligent Operation and Maintenance of Floating Offshore Wind Turbine Infrastructure on MODENERLANDS
resumo: This study proposes a pioneering approach to the operation and maintenance (O&M) of floating offshore wind turbine (FOWT) infrastructure on MODENERLANDS through the application of digital twins, boosted by advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques. The escalating challenges of maintaining FOWT structures, exacerbated by harsh marine environments and dynamic forces, demands a shift towards more intelligent and predictive O&M strategies. AI-enhanced digital twins are used, creating a dynamic and responsive model that copies the real-time state of FOWT infrastructure, thereby facilitating a proactive approach to O&M. By synthesising real-time data acquisition, advanced analytics, and predictive modelling, the AI-enhanced digital twins offer a substantial improvement over traditional corrective maintenance method. The digital twins allow for the identification of potential failure modes, prediction of deterioration progression, and recommendation of timely maintenance actions. The case study focuses on the MODENERLANDS project, employing the DTU 10MW reference turbine as a prototype to demonstrate the effectiveness of digital twins in optimizing the lifecycle management of FOWT infrastructure. Multi-physics simulations, informed by site-specific environmental data and material test results, are utilised to predict structural responses and assess corrosion fatigue (CF) deterioration states. The integration of these simulations with a probabilistic CF model enables a comprehensive evaluation of the structural health of FOWT towers and supports the development of refined adaptive control strategies aimed at minimising O&M costs while maximising operational durability and reliability. The research output not only highlights the potential for significant advancements in FOWT O&M but also sets a new benchmark for intelligent infrastructure management in the civil engineering sector. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2025.
palavras_chave: Artificial Intelligence (AI); Deterioration; Digital Twins; Floating Offshore Wind Turbine (FOWT); MODENERLANDS; Operation and Maintenance (O&M)

titulo: A Unified Graph Data Model and Storage Method for Temporal Variations in Power Grids
fonte_periodico: 2025 IEEE 9th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration Ei2 2025
resumo: With the continuous development of the new power system, the scale of power system topology nodes is constantly expanding, and local state changes are becoming more frequent. Based on relational database and static graph data modeling methods, there are significant efficiency bottlenecks in the fusion expression, integrated storage, and analysis and calculation of grid data across multiple time scales. This paper analyzes the time characteristics of the grid and proposes a method for expressing incremental data of multi-time-scale grid sections based on dynamic graphs. This method constructs a unified graph data model of grid time changes, innovatively adds time attributes to nodes and time series nodes, and realizes the expression and incremental maintenance management of multi-time-scale information such as grid topology structure, life cycle, and operating status. It has been verified that this model has certain advantages in the storage and management of large-scale grid time series topology data and dynamic grid graph calculations such as cross-time period topology analysis, and can provide efficient data support for power system analysis and calculation and business integration. © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: dynamic graph model; graph data storage; multi-temporal power grid; power grid topology construction

titulo: Digital Twin driven Nuclear Power Plant Health Monitoring, Diagnostics and Prognostics
fonte_periodico: Proceedings of Nuclear Plant Instrumentation and Control and Human Machine Interface Technology Npic and Hmit 2025
resumo: Nuclear Energy has the potential to significantly change the energy production landscape in the United States, meeting the nation's energy demands in a sustainable and environmentally responsible manner. However, the economics associated with operating the aging nuclear power plants (NPPs) require improvement while maintaining their high availability. The United States Department of Energy (DoE)'s Office of Nuclear Energy has been focusing on key research and development initiatives for the advancement of nuclear energy such as technologies and solutions to improve the reliability, sustain the safety, and extend the life of current reactors. This paper highlights the research to deliver an integrated decision support system for NPPs to provide improvements in the Operations and Maintenance (O&M) costs across the complete lifecycle of a Light Weight Power Reactor - from design and deployment to operations and maintenance. The underlying driver of the improved O&M costs is our hybrid approach with data-driven analysis and model-based systems engineering (MBSE) approach that utilizes a common model for all sustainment phases. The outcome of this research is expected to be of commercial value to related sectors and to contractors/suppliers who are involved with the development and maintenance of oil and natural gas offshore platforms. Owing to the drive for continuous design improvement and requirements of fault tolerance and low downtime, smart grids, building and facility controls (Heating, Ventilation And Cooling (HVAC), etc.), and various industrial control systems (ICS) could become the customers of developed solution suite upon incorporation of the capabilities. © 2025 AMERICAN NUCLEAR SOCIETY, INCORPORATED, WESTMONT, ILLINOIS 60559.
palavras_chave: Complete lifecycle coverage; Digital Twin; Explainable Artificial Intelligence (AI); Integrated Diagnostics and Prognostics; Real-time Health Monitoring

titulo: BUILDABILITY MOMENTUM ACROSS PROJECT STAGES: EMPIRICAL INSIGHTS FROM RIBA PLAN OF WORK TOWARDS SUSTAINABLE CONSTRUCTION
resumo: Buildability deals with the optimal integration of construction knowledge at various project stages to achieve the overall project objectives. Incorporation of buildability improves the construction project performance in terms of its cost, quality, productivity, safety, and results in early completion. This study investigates how buildability considerations manifest throughout the RIBA Plan of Work stages, from Strategic Definition-Stage to In Use-Stage7. Using a qualitative methodology, this research draws on semi-structured interviews with a cross-section of industry stakeholders, including designers, contractors, project managers, consultants, and specialists, to uncover how knowledge, stakeholder input, and decision-making practices influence buildability at each stage. Thematic analysis embedded in phenomenological research philosophy was adopted as the data analysis method. The findings show that buildability is often underdeveloped in early design due to limited contractor involvement but becomes more prominent in Spatial Coordination and Technical Design stages through logistics, sequencing, and specialist input. Handover and Use Stages underscore the overlooked importance of commissioning, handover, and facilities management for ensuring project continuity and usability. The study introduces the Buildability Momentum Curve, a visual framework mapping the rising and falling influence of buildability insights across all RIBA stages. This curve underscores the importance of early integration and sustained knowledge flow to mitigate fragmentation and performance inefficiencies. The findings have practical implications for procurement strategies, project governance, and knowledge management systems. By conceptualising buildability as a dynamic and evolving construct, the paper advocates for a more integrated and anticipatory approach to design and delivery that spans the entirety of the project lifecycle. © 2025, Ceylon Institute of Builders. All rights reserved.

titulo: NO MORE HUNGER GAMES: From Olympic legacy to livability Olympics
fonte_periodico: Events and Economic Development Bridging Theory and Practice
resumo: Mega-sporting events like the Olympics often burden host cities with high costs and long-term facility maintenance challenges while delivering mixed local benefits. The 2012 London and 2020 Tokyo Games, for example, show limited community impact amid soaring expenses. With declining bids, the International Olympic Committee’s sustainability initiatives aim to attract hosts, but questions persist about whether such events truly enhance urban life. Alternative approaches, such as a ‘Livability Olympics Ranking’ focused on housing, poverty, and wellbeing, could refocus global competition toward quality of life. © 2025 selection and editorial matter, Mike Duignan; individual chapters, the contributors.

titulo: Biological Safety Evaluation of Eco-Friendly Insulating Gas C4F7N/Air Decomposition Products
resumo: Because of its excellent insulating properties and environmental per-formance, the perfluoroisobutyronitrile (C4F7N) gas mixture is the most promising alternative to greenhouse insulating gas sulfur hexafluoride (SF6). However, after multiple arc extinguishing processes, various decomposition residual products will be produced, and the impact on the safety of maintenance personnel is still unknown. Therefore, this paper systematically evaluated the biological safety of C4F7N/Air decomposition residual products. The results demonstrated that the decomposed C4F7N/Air gas exhibits substantial acute toxicity when inhaled with an LC50 value of 31.21 parts per million for male lab mice (four hours), significantly lower than that of pure C4F7N gas. As a result, personnel involved in the operation and maintenance of electrical equipment must strictly adhere to safety precautions. © Beijing Paike Culture Commu. Co., Ltd. 2025.

titulo: Design and Implementation of a Full-Lifecycle Intelligent Management System for Emergency Mobile Seismic Monitoring Equipment Based on RFID and Embedded Technology
fonte_periodico: Proceedings of the 13th Academic Conference of Geology Resource Management and Sustainable Development Grmsd 2025
resumo: Aiming at the issues of low manual efficiency and fragmented lifecycle data in the management of emergency mobile seismic monitoring equipment, this study proposes a full-lifecycle intelligent management system for emergency mobile seismic monitoring equipment based on Radio Frequency Identification and QR code technologies. The system covers subsystems such as asset management, warehouse management, and equipment maintenance management, achieving unified management of the entire process from procurement and warehousing, issuance and return, maintenance and transfer, to scrapping and disposal of emergency mobile seismic monitoring equipment. © (2026) by Aussino Academic Publishing House All rights reserved.

titulo: Adaptive Security for Facilities in High-Risk Cities: A Case Study Approach
resumo: Establishing a facility in a high-crime urban area with complex security challenges necessitates strategic foresight and innovative approaches. This study investigates the range of risks confronting such facilities, including criminal activity, civil unrest, and cyber threats, and presents practical, evidence-based solutions to mitigate them. A central focus is placed on the collaborative engagement of key stakeholders-such as local authorities, community leaders, and law enforcement-to develop a resilient and cohesive security strategy. Additionally, this approach involves the design of an intuitive, community-oriented application to streamline the reporting of crimes and suspicious activities to law enforcement. By integrating physical security measures with a nuanced understanding of the unique social and cultural dynamics at play, this study proposes a comprehensive framework to safeguard the facility and its workforce, ultimately supporting sustainable, long-term operations within a complex urban context. © 2025 Puya Pakshad. titulo: DISCUSSION ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF DIGITAL TWIN STANDARD IN CHINA
fonte_periodico: American Society of Mechanical Engineers Pressure Vessels and Piping Division Publication PVP
resumo: Digital twin is an emerging new technology that has received significant attentions from standard organizations, industry, and academia. Industries such as manufacturing, architecture, hydraulics, electricity et al. have started using digital twin in operation, it can help with resources management, fault detection, smart maintenance management, et al., which increases working efficiency, as well as reducing budget. High-risk equipment such as pressure vessels, pipeline, and storage tanks typically operate at extreme operating conditions, problems may occasionally occur that forces the equipment shut down for maintenance, which would affect the operating efficiency of the equipment and raising up the cost. Therefore, a suitable digital twin method should be selected for evaluation. As a new technology used in industry, a conceptual system, and the definition of related terms in that field are the foundation for all subsequent work, they should be properly defined in the standard. The standardization progress of digital twin is discussed, digital twin models of high-risk equipment are introduced, and digital twin standardization of high-risk equipment are introduced in the present article. titulo: Operation and Maintenance of Safety Instrumented System (SIS)
fonte_periodico: 2025 Spring Meeting and 21st Global Congress on Process Safety Gcps 2025
resumo: The Safety Instrumented Function (SIF) in Safety Instrumented Systems (SIS) and Burner Management Systems (BMS) is a crucial protection layer that helps to reduce process risk in ethylene plants to acceptable levels. SIS follows ISA61511 which is a lifecycle standard. The operation and maintenance is the longest phase of the SIS lifecycle, and it is the responsibility of the owner/operator to demonstrate compliance with ISA61511 to satisfy OSHA PSM requirement. Each SIF must be tested at an interval determined during the SIL calculation. This test interval usually matches the Turnaround interval as most SIFs cannot be tested while the plant is running. Many users inadvertently ignore the useful life of devices specified by manufacturers. A device in safety service must be replaced or refurbished at the end of its mission time. Management of Change, documentation, training, validating device failure rates in SIL certificates against the field failure rates, developing decommissioning plan are examples of the tasks every operating company must perform as part of the SIS maintenance stage of the lifecycle. This paper seeks to raise awareness among ethylene producers about ISA61511 requirements to ensure compliance with OSHA PSM during operate phase of SIS lifecycle. © 2025 GCPS. All Rights Reserved.

titulo: User Side Energy Storage Capacity Configuration And Optimal Operation Strategy Analysis Based on Two-Layer Planning
fonte_periodico: 2025 International Conference on Electronics and Computing Communication Networking Automation Technologies Icec2nt 2025
resumo: This paper proposes an integrated decision-making model based on two-layer programming for the collaborative optimization of capacity configuration and operation strategy of user side energy storage systems. The upper level aims to maximize the net profit throughout the entire lifecycle, optimize the rated power and capacity of energy storage, integrate initial investment, operation and maintenance, and retirement costs, while incorporating income items such as peak valley arbitrage and demand electricity bill reduction; The lower level aims to minimize daily operating costs, predict controllable load schedulable capacity through Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and optimize energy storage charging and discharging strategies through dynamic programming. The model achieves bidirectional coupling between the upper and lower layers through state of charge (SOC) constraints and power balance conditions, and introduces a virtual energy storage equivalent mechanism to handle controllable loads, synchronously integrating the comprehensive power flow analysis of the heating network and power grid. The simulation results show that in the scenario of 40% renewable energy penetration rate, the generalized energy storage capacity reaches 1.25 MWh, the annual net income is 2.06 million yuan, the investment payback period is 4.5 years, and the peak load reduction rate is 13.2%, which verifies the advantages of the model in terms of economy and load balancing ability. Engineering verification shows that the calculation error of the full life cycle cost does not exceed 7%, indicating good engineering applicability. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Research on Maintenance-Free Technology System for UHVDC Transmission Lines in High-Altitude Uninhabited Areas
fonte_periodico: 2025 2nd International Conference on Dc Technologies and Systems Dcts 2025
resumo: This paper aims to construct a maintenance-free technology system for UHVDC (Ultra-High Voltage Direct Current) transmission lines in high-altitude uninhabited areas, breaking through the three bottlenecks of low operation and maintenance (O&M) efficiency, high response delay, and strong ecological constraints in harsh environments. By integrating a multi-source heterogeneous sensor network (with fiber optic vibration accuracy of ± 0.1 mm, infrared thermography temperature measurement error ≪ 1C, and LiDAR point cloud density of 200 pt / m2), an LSTM-ResNet fusion algorithm is developed to achieve edge intelligent diagnosis. Relying on the DTformer model driven by digital twin, a closed-loop architecture of 'perception-decision-execution' is built. The application results show that: the state prediction accuracy is ≫ 92.7%, the diagnosis response time is ≪ 200 ms, the investment cost per unit length is reduced to 1.082 million yuan per tower (a decrease of 42.8%), the surface disturbance area is reduced by 83.1%, and the carbon footprint is reduced by 64.3%. This system realizes the full-life-cycle autonomous operation of UHVDC transmission lines, provides an efficient, reliable, and green technical paradigm for the construction of external transmission channels of clean energy bases, and promotes the strategic transformation of power grid O&M towards minimal human involvement and intelligence. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Diagnostic and Prognostic Health Management in Autonomous Electric Vehicles: The Convergence of Intelligent Digital Twins and Generative AI
fonte_periodico: International Conference on Electrical Computer and Energy Technologies Icecet 2025
resumo: The advancement of electric autonomous vehicles (AEVs) introduces new challenges in ensuring reliability, efficiency, and safety. Diagnostic and Prognostic Health Management (DPHM), supported by Intelligent Digital Twin (IDT) technology, plays a critical role in real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, and lifecycle management. This paper explores the transformative impact of integrating Generative AI (GAI) with IDT, enhancing DPHM through synthetic data generation, failure scenario simulations, and self-learning models that adapt to real-world conditions. The synergy between IDT and GAI strengthens fault detection, optimizes maintenance strategies, and supports proactive health management. Additionally, this paper examines key enabling technologies, existing challenges, and future opportunities, highlighting how this integration can revolutionize health management systems and drive safer, more efficient, and sustainable autonomous electric mobility. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Research progress on updating of finite element model for hydraulic structures based on vibration response
fonte_periodico: Advances in Science and Technology of Water Resources
resumo: Due to the importance of accurate finite element models in assessing and analyzing the safety performance of hydraulic structures and on the basis of in-depth analysis of relevant research results at home and abroad, this paper systematically reviews the development and latest research progress of finite element model updating technology for hydraulic structures based on vibration response, with reference to both matrix-based and parameter-based updating approaches. Key issues of current finite element model updating technology for hydraulic structure are discussed and summarized. It is pointed out that future research can be carried out by combining artificial intelligence technology, from the aspects of high-efficiency sampling strategy and high-precision surrogate model development, multi-source information fusion and accurate extraction of vibration characteristics, and real-time dynamic model updating for the whole life cycle, so as to improve the practicability of vibration response-based finite element model updating technology and provide technical support for intelligent operation and maintenance of hydraulic structures. © 2025, Editorial Board of Journal of Hohai University (Natural Sciences). titulo: The influence of sustainability risk management on supply chain sustainability and profitability of medical technology firms
fonte_periodico: International Journal of Services and Operations Management
resumo: The primary objective of this study is to determine how sustainability spending can help build sustainable supply chains. This study also assesses the sustainability of five firms with respect to four dimensions; profitability, sustainability spending, risk rating, and sustainability risk management. Data was collected through unstructured interviews with biotechnology and medical technology industry personnel. Key sustainability risk factors that created a ripple effect along the supply chain were identified. The supply chain surplus and risk management strategies were evaluated. Technique for order of preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS) was used to rank the firms on their sustainability and risk management practices. The critical sustainability risks identified are inventory management, logistics/ transportation, waste management, energy consumption, supplier sustainability, material handling, and plant or facility management. Findings reveal that firms investing in sustainability risk management face better prospects of developing supply chain sustainability and profitability. titulo: Exploring The Physical Activity in Camping Tourism: A Confirmatory Factor Analysis of Tourist Experiences
resumo: Background. Research on camping tourism, especially tourist experiences, remains limited, offering valuable insights for facility management. Objectives. This study aims to identify the dominant factors shaping the camping experience and WOM and examine the impact of the camping experience on WOM. Methods. The research uses confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and structural equation modeling (SEM) to analyze data from 400 respondents who visited camping sites in Bandung Regency. Measurement indicators based on camping experience and WOM constructs were used to assess the strength and influence of each factor. Results. The findings show that "personal growth and renewal" and "WOM intensity" are the most influential factors in shaping the camping experience and WOM. Additionally, the camping experience has a significant positive effect on WOM. Conclusions. The results suggest that service providers should enhance engaging experiences to encourage positive WOM, attract more visitors, and ensure long-term sustainability in the camping tourism sector. © 2025, Society of Aging and Physical Activity (SAPA). titulo: Bibliometric Web of Science and Google Trends analysis of multi-criteria decision analysis within the built environment
autores: Smith, KA; Mostafiz, RB; Friedland, C; Nahmens, I
resumo: This research aims to leverage existing data sources to provide new insights into the usage of Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) in the built environment without creating a new data collection process. The study is focused upon built environment vocations, spanning the disciplines of architecture, construction management, urban planning, real estate, facilities management, and the numerous engineering domains that support capital projects. The method of the study utilized Google search engine data from Google Trends and academic literature metadata from Web of Science, which was analyzed using Bibliometrix via the Biblioshiny interface. These datasets were cross-referenced with original data collected from a Qualtrics delivered industry questionnaire to develop a more comprehensive understanding of MCDA adoption within the built environment. The research presents a ranked list of MCDA methods used within built environment vocations in order of level of adoption, with the top five being PROMETHEE, House of Quality, Monte Carlo Simulations, TOPSIS, and Utility Theory. The results include Biblioshiny visualizations for MCDA methods studied within built environment academic papers and findings related to tool associations via key clusters, such as GIS and drone based data collection tool usage, in concert with MCDA methods. The paper presents evidence that MCDAs are more frequently used in environmental science, geography, management, and sustainability studies within the built environment relative to other design or construction oriented use cases. By integrating diverse data sources—academic publications, search engine trends, and industry responses—the research explores a multi-faceted perspective on the current state of MCDA usage, highlighting the gaps between academic focus, industry practices, and public interest. The research notes that MCDAs are often considered on an individual basis instead of approached broadly as a set of mathematical tools, possibly serving as a barrier to a more expansive understanding of the means and methods practitioners might employ.
