titulo: Effective Maintenance Management Framework Through a Health Index: A Case Study in the Oil and Gas Industry
resumo: The oil and gas sector is transforming rapidly, driven by global energy demand and the need to address climate change. Effective maintenance management is critical for ensuring asset reliability and operational safety in this sector, where predictive and proactive strategies replace traditional reactive maintenance practices. This paper introduces a comprehensive health maintenance management framework designed to enhance oil and gas industry maintenance practices. The proposed framework includes six essential stages: Asset registration, maintenance strategy selection, capability promotion, maintenance implementation, reporting, and continuous improvement. A key innovation of the framework is using a Health Index (HI), which provides a quantitative and scalable assessment of maintenance management health. This index and its subindices are a benchmarking tool, enabling organisations to compare their performance with their historical or industry standards, proactively prevent equipment failures, and minimise downtime. The framework also supports modern techniques such as condition monitoring, artifcial intelligence, and digital twins to optimise maintenance efficiency and sustainability. A case study conducted in a gas processing plant demonstrates the practical application of the HI, revealing trends in maintenance management health over time and highlighting areas for improvement. The findings underscore the value of the HI in guiding decision-making, improving asset management, and supporting predictive maintenance practices. Furthermore, the study outlines how to integrate predictive methods, optimising scheduling and planning for maintenance activities, ultimately boosting asset performance and reducing operational disruptions. This framework offers a structured and dynamic approach to maintenance management, promoting continuous improvement and operational excellence in the oil and gas sector. © 2025 Published by SQU Publication Board.

titulo: Contribution of Lean Maintenance Management to the Sustainability of Dental Clinic
resumo: Lean maintenance is essential for the proper functioning of any organization; its management in dental clinics takes on special significance because these are institutions whose mission is to restore the oral and general health of the population. The objective of the research is to design a procedure for lean maintenance management in these organizations where the lean tools and techniques that can be used at each step are explained. The research was carried out in the last quarter of 2023 at the “Dr. Mario Pozo Ochoa” Dental Clinic, in the municipality of Holguín, Cuba. The main problems that affect maintenance were identified through the analysis of the value chain of this activity, determining the gaps for their subsequent elimination. The following results are worth highlighting: maintenance was managed following lean principles with the application of techniques and tools to facilitate its analysis, evaluation and control, which allowed the creation of the action plan for continuous improvement. It contributed to the improvement of process performance, obtaining favorable results in terms of time, productivity, quality and availability of medical equipment, thereby promoting the sustainability of these organizations. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

titulo: Optimizing Maintenance Management System: Identification of Critical Risk and Safety Factors in Human Error Based Corrective Maintenance in the SMEs using Fuzzy DEMATEL Approach
resumo: A better and optimal maintenance management system is a key source of a sustainable manufacturing environment in the competitive world. In response to improving drastic and competitive manufacturing working environments, many Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) wish for an optimal maintenance management system for business success and customer satisfaction. For the purpose of organizing optimal Corrective Maintenance Management (CMM) effectively, some literature and direct industrial surveys have suggested several critical factors of Human Error-Based (HEB) CMM in the working environment of SMEs. HEB accidents and machine breakdowns have always been a major concern in this type of maintenance management system in SMEs, especially in the 3D printing technology applied automotive industries. Such undesirable problems are more prevalent in SMEs of developing countries, especially in the SMEs of southern Tamil Nadu, India. Moreover, ranking the most significant critical factors in HEB maintenance inevitably involves the vagueness of human judgment in the traditional way of approach. This research objective is to predict, analyze, and evaluate the HEB maintenance factors that trigger undesirable machine accidents and corrective maintenance activities of Sensors and switches manufacturing operations in SMEs. Hence, this real-time case study research presents a favorable method for combining fuzzy set theory and the Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) method to rank the critical factors for optimal CMM implementation in the working environment of SMEs. According to this analysis identified the most critical factors (Meshing around - 0.205, Poorly written procedures and manuals, and work instructions – 0.163) were identified under two major sub-categories, such as environmental and organizational factors generally influenced in the SMEs. Also, an empirical case study is illustrated by presenting the proposed hybrid MCDM technique and demonstrating the application of implications. Copyright © 2025 Reports in Mechanical Engineering. titulo: Barrier Engineering: Models and Methods for Technical Safety
fonte_periodico: Barrier Engineering Models and Methods for Technical Safety
resumo: This book aims to provide a systematic approach to the design, assessment, operation, and maintenance of safety barriers that are used for preventing accidents and protecting humans, equipment, and the environment. Barrier Engineering: Models and Methods for Technical Safety is based on the philosophy of risk management, providing a thorough guide on identifying, analyzing, designing, operating, and maintaining safety barriers. It presents general theories, models, and both qualitative and quantitative analysis approaches, addressing both design and operational challenges for technical and non-technical barriers. The focus is on analyzing and evaluating the effectiveness and performance of technical safety barriers to ensure the functional safety of complex systems. This book also introduces the concepts of barrier security, applications of artificial intelligence, resilience, and sustainability considerations in safety barrier engineering and management. PowerPoint slides and a solutions manual are available for facilitating teaching and self-learning. This book can be used as a textbook for master-level students in process and machinery safety, industrial and systems engineering, and management, and it is also an invaluable reference for risk analysts and engineers in complex system design, operation, and maintenance. © 2025 Yiliu Liu.

titulo: Exploring the Role of Human Factors and Organizational Culture in Maintenance Management Practice Within Large Processing Industries
resumo: This study examines the impact of human factors (HF) and organizational culture (OC) on maintenance management practices (MMP) in large processing industries. A mixed-method approach, including a systematic review, surveys, and interviews, analyzed using SPSS 26 and AMOS software, revealed a strong positive correlation between HF, OC, and MMP (beta coefficients: 0.95 and 0.01). The findings highlight the critical roles of HF and OC in shaping effective maintenance strategies, offering practical insights for improving operational efficiency and sustainability. Likewise, this research contributes to understanding the interplay of HF, OC, and MMP, providing a foundation for future studies in the field. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2025.

titulo: A Wireless Enabled IOT Nondestructive Fatigue Damage Sensor for Estimation of Remaining Useful Service (RUL) of Structures Through Artificial Intelligence-Machine Learning Algorithms
fonte_periodico: Structural Health Monitoring 2025 Ensuring Mobility and Autonomy with Sustainability Proceedings of the 15th International Workshop on Structural Health Monitoring Iwshm 2025
resumo: In this study, a wireless enabled novel non-destructive evaluation (NDE) fatigue damage sensor for the structural fatigue health monitoring and prediction of fatigue life of structural members of large engineering structures is presented. The smart predictive IOT (Internet of Things) fatigue damage sensor has special designed smart breakable sacrificial sensor beams for early fatigue damage detection and prediction of fatigue sensitive structural and mechanical parts of fatigue sensitive structures. The IOT non-destructive fatigue damage sensor can measure directly the state of fatigue damage accumulation levels and predict the remaining useful life (RUL) of structural components or locations for the life cycle management and predictive maintenance of structures without using any fatigue damage algorithm. The non-destructive evaluation (NDE) fatigue sensor consists of mechanical and electronic units. The mechanical part of the fatigue damage sensor has special designed smart and predictive sacrificial beams with different levels of lifetimes (10% N, 20% N, 30% N, 40% N, 50% N, 60% N, 70% N, 80% N, 90% N, 95-100% N) normalized to the total lifetime of a real structure. The mechanical sensor beams designed with special geometry using stress magnifying effects to measure the fatigue damage accumulating level and early fatigue damage detection and fatigue state health monitoring of structures. The smart fatigue damage sensors attached onto the surface on a real structure is expected to have the same cyclic stress-strain loading behaviour and the same cyclic stress-strain history for during the operational service life. The sensor having multiple parallel oriented and mini-micro non-destructive fatigue damage measurement sensing beams are designed to fail earlier than a real structure in the different predetermined fatigue lifetimes like a mechanical fatigue fusing system. Due to its predictive feature the fatigue sensor will extent not only the service life of fatigue sensitive mechanical components but also increase the safety and reliability of structures. Since the wireless enabled fatigue damage sensor network through Internet of Things (IOT) technologies collect the real operational fatigue data remotely, the statistical fatigue damage sensor network data can be used for the prediction of lifetimes of structural or mechanical members by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) Machine Learning (ML) Algorithms. The distributed fatigue sensor network also provides a real operational-experimental statistical data for condition based predictive maintenance, maintenance management, end of service life indicator (ESLI) and development of new fatigue design tools for fatigue sensitive parts or locations of fatigue critic metallic and composite structures. titulo: POST OCCUPANCY EVALUATION (POE) IN GOVERNMENT OFFICE BUILDINGS: A LITERATURE REVIEW
resumo: The construction industry is a vital sector in the global economy, with governments acting as one of its primary clients. Despite this significance, many public office buildings have recurring issues in operation and environment, which affect satisfaction, comfort, and productivity for users. Therefore, research aims to develop a framework for the adoption of post occupancy evaluation (POE) in government office buildings. A comprehensive literature review was conducted to recognize pertinent issues with government buildings and their effect on occupants. The research evaluates POE as a tool capable of addressing such issues by providing a systematic assessment of building performance from the user's perspective. A framework is built to explain the linkages between the identified issues, impact on the user, and the intervention function of the POE. Further, the framework presents how POEs act as an intervention device that leads to many advantages, such as improving building operation, evidence-based decision-making, and additional occupant satisfaction; however, the use of a POE in the public sector is hampered by many obstacles, such as institutional inertia, lack of awareness, and resource constraints. The framework also offered strategies to clear these barriers and enhance the use of POE as a building management staple where continuous improvement is prioritized for government office environments. © 2025, Ceylon Institute of Builders. titulo: H-BoostGBM: A Data-Driven Hybrid Boosting Framework for Multi-Source Building Energy Prediction
fonte_periodico: Proceeding of 2025 IEEE 6th International Conference on Computer Big Data and Artificial Intelligence Iccbd AI 2025
resumo: Accurate prediction of building energy consumption is essential for improving energy efficiency and supporting sustainable urban development. Traditional time-series forecasting methods encounter several issues when applied to building energy prediction, including difficulty capturing nonlinear relationships among environmental and operational variables, inconsistent data quality, and poor generalization across different building types and climates. To address these limitations, this study proposes an enhanced LightGBM-based model, termed H-BoostGBM (Hybrid Feature-Integrated Gradient Boosting Framework). The proposed framework incorporates systematic data preprocessing, feature selection, and temporal aggregation to improve data quality and model robustness. By integrating environmental, operational, and temporal features, H-BoostGBM effectively captures complex dependencies in energy consumption patterns. The model is trained and validated on real-world building datasets and compared with conventional regression models and other ensemble learning methods. Experimental results demonstrate that H-BoostGBM achieves higher prediction accuracy, lower error metrics, and improved generalization performance. These findings highlight the potential of advanced ensemble learning techniques to enhance intelligent energy management and promote energy-efficient building operations. © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: Building energy consumption prediction; Ensemble learning; Feature engineering; Machine learning; Sustainable building operation

titulo: Operation and Maintenance Essentials and Cost Estimation of the Tailwater Wetland Coupled with Wastewater Treatment Plant
resumo: Constructed wetlands are ecosystems consisting of water and plants. They serve multiple purposes, including sewage purification, biodiversity protection, microclimate regulation, and habitat preservation. Today, they are globally recognized as environmentally friendly “Green” sewage treatment technologies and are widely employed for industrial wastewater and domestic sewage treatment. While numerous studies have been conducted on plant and filler selection and decontamination capabilities of constructed wetlands, along with practical applications, challenges still persist in the field of constructed wetland wastewater treatment projects. However, in the field of constructed wetland sewage treatment projects, there is still the phenomenon of emphasizing construction while neglecting management, and the lack of a scientific and effective operation and management system result in problems such as blockage, decreased treatment efficiency, irregular operation, and subpar landscape aesthetics. To address these challenges, a tailwater wetland coupled with wastewater treatment plant in Yangtze River Basin was taken as a case, to propose specific requirements and measures for the operation and maintenance of constructed wetlands, focusing on water quantity, water level, vegetation, packing materials, aquatic animals, and thermal insulation. The objective is to maximize the multi functionality of constructed wetlands and provide theoretical and technical support for their sustainable operation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.
palavras_chave: fees and charges; operations; tailwater wetland

titulo: INDONESIAN PV POWER PLANT PERFORMANCE: FAILURE-MODE ALIGNMENT WITH AN OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE ENHANCEMENT STRATEGY
fonte_periodico: Association of Researchers in Construction Management Arcom 2025 Proceedings of the 41st Annual Conference
resumo: Towards a 2060 net-zero-emission target, Indonesia has had slow growth in its solar photovoltaic capacity; current installations are plagued by performance problems. Detecting failure modes and augmenting operation and maintenance strategies for reliability enhancement of solar power plants is this study's aim and, fills a regional research gap by identifying the local causes of underperformance of photovoltaic power plants, giving an O&M strategy to mitigate these problems. The methodology builds upon secondary research, low-yield case-study company reports, structured interviews with 4 key Indonesian solar industry experts and, a Pareto analysis to identify the 20% of components (invertor faults/battery drop-offs) responsible for 80% of energy-yield deficits. Failure mode effects analysis then populates a developed, structured maintenance framework for Indonesian PV plants. This work shows that improvement in the general energy-yield of Indonesian photovoltaic power plants is addressed by targeted O&M, which enhances solar power plant performance in rural Indonesia, towards helping attain the country's objectives on renewable energy, adding to the overall goal of sustainable energy development in the region. © Association of Researchers in Construction Management, ARCOM 2025 - Proceedings of the 41st Annual Conference.
palavras_chave: energy-yield; failure-modes; Indonesia; O&M-framework; PV-power

titulo: Differential maintenance decision-making method for distribution equipment based on risk assessment
fonte_periodico: Proceedings of SPIE the International Society for Optical Engineering
resumo: To improve the operation and maintenance efficiency of large-scale distribution equipment and reduce operation and maintenance costs, this paper proposes a differentiated maintenance decision-making method for distribution equipment based on risk assessment. Firstly, use the fault correlation matrix to calculate the impact of a single distribution equipment fault on the distribution network. Then, calculate the severity index of the consequences of power distribution equipment failures from two aspects: the losses caused by equipment failures and the impact of equipment failures on the distribution network. Secondly, utilizing real-time monitoring information from the device to calculate the real-time health index of the device overcomes the disadvantage of poor real-time health index performance. Utilize real-time health index and severity index of fault consequences to calculate the risk value of the equipment, and then obtain the relative risk value of the equipment. At the same time, based on the importance of the equipment, develop differentiated maintenance strategies for the equipment. Finally, based on the relative risk value and maintenance strategy of the equipment, a maintenance method for the equipment is formulated, and the effectiveness of the proposed model and method is verified through numerical examples. © 2025 SPIE.
palavras_chave: distribution equipment; maintenance; maintenance decision-making; operation; risk assessment

titulo: Research on Next Generation O&M Platform for urban Power and Energy Facilities Based on CIM
fonte_periodico: 2025 IEEE 9th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration Ei2 2025
resumo: The continuous healthy operation of power energy facilities is a crucial prerequisite for ensuring the safety and stability of the power system. In response to the characteristics of the new power system, such as a large number of devices, extensive distribution, and complex operating environments, traditional equipment operation and maintenance (O&M) methods face challenges like passive responses, insufficient auxiliary decision- making, and low maintenance efficiency. This article analyzes the new operational features of equipment in the new power system, elaborates on the new requirements for precise perception of equipment status, health assessment, and O&M support capabilities, and proposes and designs an O&M platform based on City Information Model technology. The article also explains the platform's architectural design and core business scenarios, and explores the application of technologies such as AI and large models within the platform. This platform aims to enhance the efficiency and reliability of equipment O&M in the new power system, reduce O&M costs, and provide new ideas and approaches for the maintenance of power energy facilities under the evolving context. © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: AI; City Information Modeling (CIM); New Power System; O&M Platform Architecture; Power and Energy Facilities

titulo: Maintenance and Refurbishment for Low Emissions in Buildings
resumo: As climate change poses significant challenges globally, the built environment’s contribution to greenhouse gas emissions is increasingly scrutinized. This chapter emphasizes the importance of effective building maintenance and refurbishment strategies to minimize environmental impact. In addition to exploring various maintenance strategies for reducing energy consumption and emissions, the chapter discusses the significance of building refurbishment and smart retrofits for sustainability. An examination of greenhouse gas emissions associated with the built environment is included, along with quantification and reporting methods based on the Greenhouse Gas Protocol. Further to addressing performance benchmarking on carbon emissions among buildings, the chapter outlines methods for conducting environmental and economic evaluations of energy retrofits, showcasing a credible procedure for assessing environmental benefits and related costs. Finally, an empirical case study illustrates practical applications of these evaluations, offering valuable insights for practitioners, decision-makers, and researchers striving for a more sustainable built environment. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2025.

titulo: Overview of Offshore Wind Power Technologies
resumo: Optimizing offshore wind power technology and reducing the levelized cost of electricity throughout the lifecycle are key measures for the large-scale development of offshore wind power, contributing significantly to the transition toward sustainable energy systems. However, compared to onshore wind power, the internal flow dynamics of offshore wind farms are more complex, which poses challenges for operation and maintenance. Therefore, there is an urgent need for updated, smarter, more efficient, and economic offshore intelligent operation control technologies to facilitate the large-scale development and utilization of offshore wind power. This paper approaches the topic from two perspectives, offshore wind turbines and offshore wind farms, introducing popular research directions and technical bottlenecks in these two related fields. This includes offshore wind turbine capacity development and fundamental technologies, offshore wind power forecasting technology, and offshore wind power operation and control technology, offshore intelligent operation and maintenance technology, as well as offshore wind power and integrated marine area utilization technology. Firstly, the challenges faced by the intensive development of offshore wind resources and operational environments are analyzed. Secondly, the challenges encountered in the aforementioned technological areas and their potential solutions are summarized. Finally, a systematic reflection and outlook on the large-scale development of offshore wind power are provided, reinforcing its critical role in achieving global sustainability goals. © 2025 by the authors.
palavras_chave: offshore wind power; operation and maintenance technology; operation control; sustainable energy system; wind power forecasting

titulo: Research on Structural Safety Monitoring and Motion Response Prediction of Floating Offshore Wind Turbines
fonte_periodico: Proceedings of the International Offshore and Polar Engineering Conference
resumo: Safety monitoring and early warning systems are critical for the operation and maintenance of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs), particularly in terms of accurately and promptly predicting their motion responses. To address this challenge, a comprehensive, multidimensional monitoring and early warning system has been developed, focusing on tower, floating body, mooring, and environmental condition monitoring. Additionally, an LSTM model is employed to predict the short-term motion responses of FOWT, with the goal of providing early warnings for potential structural failures and contributing to the long-term sustainability and safety of offshore wind energy systems. © 2025 by the International Society of Offshore and Polar Engineers (ISOPE).
palavras_chave: Deep neural networks; FOWT; Motion prediction; Structural safety monitoring

titulo: Analysis of Levelized Cost of Energy for Wind Power
fonte_periodico: 2025 4th International Conference on Green Energy and Power Systems Icgeps 2025
resumo: This article analyzes and calculates the Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) for wind power projects, outlining the cost structure which includes investment and operation maintenance costs. Using the LCOE model, the article examines the factors influencing costs and calculates the cost per kilowatt-hour through a case study. The study finds that investment costs mainly consist of turbine purchase, construction, and loan interest, while operation maintenance costs increase with the turbine's age. Reasonable returns are key to sustainable development. The final LCOE for wind power is calculated to be 0.3482 yuan/kWh, providing a theoretical basis for project pricing.  © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: LCOE; Levelized Cost of Electricity; Operation And Maintenance Costs

titulo: Subcluster Operating Model in Managing Large Assets: Driving Efficiency Through People Empowerment
resumo: M asset is the largest producing asset in South the Sultanate of Oman with over 30 producing fields, and faced operational complexities due to the high number of producing and injecting wells that need to be managed, the active drilling program, the diverse development types, and multiple production and injection stations. To address these challenges and enhance efficiency and performance, the asset transitioned from a functionally segmented, value stream-based model, where disciplines like the drilling team (New Oil), planning, and Well, Reservoir & Facility Management (WRFM) teams operated in silos, to an area-focused Subcluster Operating Model. This new model integrates all key activities within geographically defined zones, aiming to improve production performance, optimize costs, and empower teams through enhanced ownership, accountability, and cross-functional collaboration. The Subcluster Operating Model organized the large unit (asset)into integrated area-based units called subclusters, each given full responsibility for its production system, including planning, execution, and performance monitoring. Resources such as rigs, hoists, and different units were allocated per subcluster to ensure operational flexibility. A centralized opportunity funnel was developed to mature development options and feed prioritized projects into execution systematically. Regular performance reviews, knowledge-sharing sessions, and cross-disciplinary collaborations were embedded to support the alignment and decision-making. Moreover, the model significantly enhanced collaboration not only within subclusters but also among key stakeholders from other departments such as concept engineering, operations, and other supporting functions. This stakeholder engagement helps an integrated system approach to asset management, enabling smoother handovers and collective problem-solving. In addition to operational benefits, the Subcluster Model promotes talent development and leadership growth by empowering multidisciplinary teams to take ownership, build capabilities, and prepare future leaders. To maintain strategic coherence and ensure that all subclusters pursue common goals, the overall operating model remains under the leadership and guidance of the Asset Manager and senior leadership team. The implementation of the Subcluster Operating Model delivered substantial results across key performance areas. In terms of production growth, Asset M surpassed its production target ahead of schedule, achieving the highest production levels since inception while reducing deferment by 15%. Additionally, the model accelerated the maturation of strategic future growth projects, ensuring the sustainable development of this large asset. Regarding cost leadership, subclusters operated with autonomy over allocated resources, such as hoists and standalone units, driving optimization and lean execution, which resulted in achieving the lowest Unit Operating Cost (UOC) in the past four years. Furthermore, the model promoted people empowerment and improved decision-making by embedding a culture of accountability, enabling teams to lead development planning and execution with enhanced technical and leadership capabilities. Decision making became faster and more effective due to improved visibility and alignment with long-term asset strategies. The Subcluster Operating Model introduces a novel area-based operational structure within a complex & active asset environment. This approach decentralizes ownership and empowers multidisciplinary teams to manage full-cycle operations within defined geographies. It integrates planning, execution, and opportunity maturation within localized units, enhancing agility, resource optimization, and decision quality. This innovative model not only redefines operational efficiency but also sets a benchmark for a scalable, people-centric asset management system for large-scale assets. Copyright © 2025, Society of Petroleum Engineers.

titulo: Achieving Greenhouse Gas Emission Reduction Through OperationExcellence Program in Mature Offshore Oil Fields
fonte_periodico: Society of Petroleum Engineers SPE Asia Pacific Ccus Conference Apcc 2025
resumo: Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from mature oil and gas fields constitute a significant portion ofthe industry's overall emissions. While these mature fields possess substantial reduction potential,implementation of improvement action is often challenging due to various constraints related to aging assetsas well as complexity in production and operation management. This challenge is further amplified forremote offshore fields, where access to solutions is limited. This paper presents a case study on how alocal oil company's operating mature offshore oil fields in Vietnam successfully reduced its GHG emissionsagainst its annual target while maintaining stable operations and production through a unique OperationalExcellence (OE) program. It also aims to share lessons and insights to support similar operators of matureoil fields in overcoming challenges related to GHG emission reduction. Driven by the Corporate's 2040 net-zero emissions target, the Company proactively conducted theOperational Excellence Benchmarking Program [1]. This work aimed at finding opportunities forenhancement of production sustainability and operations' efficiency, of which GHG emission is a greatsignificance. As a result of the benchmarking, a number of improvement opportunities were identifiedand ranked based on the company's business goals and its strategic priorities. Regarding GHG emissionreduction, the key initiatives, which have been being implemented, include (1) centralizing operationdata for visualization and analysis, (2) improving facility maintenance with risk-based inspection andprescriptive maintenance approaches, (3) optimizing compressor gas volumes through surface networkmodeling and field trials, and (4) conducting routine flare and leakage assessments. These initiativeseffectively contributed to the achievement of the GHG emission reduction along with stable oil productionin the Company's mature offshore oil fields. Copyright 2025, Society of Petroleum Engineers.

titulo: Integrated decision support framework architecture for rolling stock maintenance management - sustainable software perspective
fonte_periodico: 2025 4th International Conference on Power Control and Computing Technologies Icpc2t 2025
resumo: This paper proposes a decision support framework architecture designed to optimize fleet management, particularly focusing on minimizing total maintenance costs. The framework includes a planning optimization module, which integrates input data, a mathematical model, and optimization methods to develop cost-effective schedules for locomotives assigned to transport tasks. Through the application of various optimization algorithms, including simulated annealing, genetic algorithms, and their cost versions, the case study demonstrates substantial cost reductions on average by more than thirty percent compared to basic approaches. The results highlight the framework's capability to support strategic decision-making in fleet composition, contract evaluation, and maintenance planning. Energy-saving algorithms, modular structure and optimization of resources make the framework sustainable software. © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: decision support; enterprise performance management; framework architecture; maintenance management; rolling stock schedule; simulation support systems

titulo: Economic and Environmental Dispatch of Hybrid Microgrids Using a Genetic Slime Mould Algorithm under Time-of-Use Pricing
fonte_periodico: 2025 5th IEEE International Conference on Energy Engineering and Power Systems Eeps 2025
resumo: With the rapid growth of renewable energy integration, microgrid economic dispatch is facing increasing challenges due to the stochastic and intermittent nature of distributed energy resources (DERs). To address these challenges, this paper establishes a multi-objective optimization framework embedded in a Markov Decision Process (MDP) for microgrid intraday scheduling. The objective function jointly considers fuel costs, power exchange costs, operation and maintenance (O&M) expenses, and environmental penalty costs from pollutant emissions of diesel engines (DEs) and microturbines (MTs). To solve the high-dimensional and nonlinear optimization problem, a Genetic Slime Mould Algorithm (GSMA) is developed by integrating the global search capability of the Genetic Algorithm (GA) with the adaptive local exploitation ability of the Slime Mould Algorithm (SMA). A case study on a hybrid microgrid comprising PV, wind, MT, DE, and battery energy storage system (BESS) is conducted under time-of-use (TOU) pricing. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves reliable peak shaving and valley filling, reduces total operation costs, and effectively enhances both environmental performance and supply reliability in islanded mode. © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: Genetic Slime Mould Algorithm (GSMA); Markov Decision Process (MDP); Microgrid economic dispatch; Renewable energy integration

titulo: INTEGRATION OF IOT IN SMART BUILDING SYSTEMS FOR SUSTAINABLE URBAN DEVELOPMENT
resumo: The rapid growth of urban populations has exacerbated energy waste, resource inefficiency, and environmental degradation in contemporary cities, necessitating crucial, smart building solutions. This paper examines the incorporation of the Internet of Things (IoT) in intelligent buildings to facilitate sustainable urban development. The study helps address inefficient building operations by proposing an IoT-based system built on distributed sensors, real-time data collection, cloud-based analytics, and automated control systems. The technology will be based on the implementation of environmental, occupancy, and energy-monitoring sensors within the building's subsystems, preliminary data processing, and predictive analytics to maximize energy efficiency, comfort, and work efficiency. The experimental analysis of a multi-zone smart building testbed has shown significant enhancements, including a reduction in yearly energy demand from 420 MWh to 338 MWh, a reduction in the HVAC system's peak load from 96 kW to 71 kW, and an increase in HVAC system efficiency to 0.82. Also, IAQ indicators, such as CO2 levels, remained below 900 ppm for more than 92% of the operating time, and automated lighting systems reduced unnecessary illumination by 3.1 hours per day. These findings support the claim that smart building systems powered by IoT can significantly improve energy efficiency, occupant comfort, and environmental performance. It is concluded that the mass implementation of IoT-integrated construction may be of utmost importance in ensuring the development of sustainable urban infrastructure by minimizing resource use, reducing operational expenses, and supporting data-driven city planning. © 2025, Technical institute of Bijeljina. All rights reserved.
palavras_chave: building automation; energy management systems; internet of things (IOT); real-time monitoring; smart buildings; sustainable urban development; urban sustainability

titulo: Toward Sustainable Built Environments: Leveraging Green Hydrogen in New Zealand
resumo: The requirement to decarbonize the built environment has intensified globally, with New Zealand aligning its objectives to ambitious climate goals. This study explores the potential of green hydrogen as a versatile energy carrier to revolutionize building operations and contribute to sustainable energy systems. The research objectives encompass developing public acceptance, analyzing energy out-comes, ensuring social and economic security, and formulating recommended policies for government consideration. This empirical study employed a multimethod approach, integrating literature review with qualitative interviews and a quantitative survey. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2025.
palavras_chave: Built Environment; Decarbonization; Green Hydrogen; Hydrogen Technologies; Sustainability

titulo: Optimization of Maintenance Management in Hydroelectric Plants Implementing Oil Steam, Brake Dust, and Slip Ring Dust Collector Extraction Systems
fonte_periodico: 2025 25th Conference of the Electric Power Supply Industry Cepsi 2025
resumo: This study evaluates the impact of implementing auxiliary extraction systems - oil vapor, brake dust, and slip ring carbon dust collectors - on the maintenance management of Francis turbine-generators at the Chaglla Hydroelectric Power Plant in Peru. Excessive contamination from oil vapors, brake dust, and carbon deposits on slip rings historically led to frequent maintenance stops, reduced availability (92.5% pre-implementation), and high operational costs. Through a quasi-experimental methodology, we analyzed data from 2019 to 2024, comparing performance before and after the 2022 installation of these systems. Results demonstrate significant improvements: availability increased to 95%, reliability rose from 82% to 96%, maintenance costs decreased by 52%, and preventive maintenance frequency was halved. The systems' integration with SCADA-enabled predictive protocols further optimized resource allocation. These findings highlight the effectiveness of targeted extraction technologies in enhancing hydropower plant sustainability, aligning with global trends toward cost-efficient and reliable renewable energy generation. © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: availability; cost reduction; dust extraction systems; Francis turbine; Hydroelectric power; maintenance optimization; reliability

titulo: Artificial Intelligence-Based Technologies and Approaches of Sustainable Entrepreneurship: Current Status and Perspectives
resumo: Entrepreneurship and sustainable development have come together to create a new field, “sustainable entrepreneurship.” Increasing the number of people starting their own businesses is critical to a country’s progress. In terms of job creation, boosting the economy, launching new businesses, and influencing social evolution, the success of entrepreneurship is critical for nations. Sustainable entrepreneurship (SE) is based on the acceptance that long-term environmental and social results and impact are as important as short-term economic ones. Recently, with advances in the field of artificial intelligence (AI), several researchers recommend AI-based techniques for sustainable development. The objective is to understand the current state of the subject by characterizing bibliographic records indexed in the Scopus and WoS databases. Microsoft Excel and VOSviewer were used for data analysis and visualization. The results indicate that the use of artificial intelligence and machine learning methods and algorithms for sustainable entrepreneurship is limited. Therefore, the development of a methodology for sustainable entrepreneurship that incorporates AI emerges as a promising avenue for research. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.
palavras_chave: continuous improvement; dental clinics; dental equipment; lean maintenance management; sustainability

titulo: Multi-Criteria Decision-Making for Selecting Key Performance Indicators in Bus Rapid Transit Fleet Maintenance
fonte_periodico: Proceedings of the 2025 IEEE 32nd International Conference on Electronics Electrical Engineering and Computing Intercon 2025
resumo: Effective maintenance management in urban transportation systems, such as Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) fleets, relies on selecting appropriate Key Performance Indicators (KPls) to monitor performance and align with organizational objectives. This study proposes a Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) framework to select maintenance KPls for a BRT fleet in Lima, Peru, addressing the region's challenges of high operational costs and reactive maintenance practices. Using the ELECTRE I method, supplemented by the Simos procedure for criteria weighting, 20 candidate KPls were evaluated based on five criteria: quality of maintenance, alignment with objectives, decision-making influence, ease of comprehension, and stakeholder engagement. The methodology, inspired by aerospace material selection techniques, incorporates expert input and validation to ensure practical applicability. Results identify six critical KPls, including reliability, availability, and corrective maintenance cost percentage, which enhance proactive maintenance strategies. This approach provides a replicable, mathematically robust framework for transportation maintenance management, adaptable to diverse operational contexts.  © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: BRT; ELECTRE I; Maintenance; MCDM

titulo: Immersive Analytics for Sustainable and Resilient Building Operations: Leveraging Immersive Space to Think (IST)
resumo: In the pursuit of sustainable and resilient building operations, integrating immersive analytics shows promise. This approach utilizes virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) to enhance sensemaking, revealing cognitive processes in the “space to think.” This paper introduces a novel conceptual framework that combines immersive analytics with Immersive Space To Think (IST) methodologies, leveraging advanced Holotable technology. The framework creates an immersive interface for facility managers and building owners to simulate scenarios, particularly focusing on energy consumption and carbon footprint reduction. Real-time data from IoT sensors embedded in building infrastructure enables visualization of impacts such as thermostat settings, lighting levels, and renewable energy integration. This approach fosters collaboration among stakeholders by providing a shared virtual space for interactive visualization and scenario exploration. By facilitating collective assessment of energy efficiency, cost effectiveness, and occupant comfort within the IST, stakeholders can make informed decisions. This transformative approach enhances building management by optimizing energy use in smart buildings, supported by immersive analytics and IST environments, promising improvements in sustainability, resilience, and occupant satisfaction across commercial and residential sectors. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2025.

titulo: Digitalization of District Heating: Transforming Heat Networks for a Sustainable Future
fonte_periodico: Lecture Notes in Computer Science Including Subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics
resumo: The district heating and cooling sector is experiencing new challenges with the current transformation of energy systems. The required decarbonization will result in a more complex heat energy system, as a few large plants which utilize fossil fuels will likely be replaced, mostly by smaller production plants distributed around the system, that use renewable or waste energy sources. Furthermore, district heating and cooling systems must be operated more efficiently and flexibly to ensure a consistent and cost-effective thermal energy supply, as well as effective participation in the power system balancing market. Because of the necessary changes in the energy system, district heating becomes increasingly beneficial to both end users as well as other energy sectors, and the number of connections is increasing in many countries in conjunction with the phase-out of fossil fuels such as oil and gas for space heating and hot water supply. In this changed environment, increased adoption of digital technology in the district heating and cooling sector provides a chance to make systems smarter, more flexible, efficient, and reliable, hence accelerating the necessary integration of additional renewable and waste energy sources into thermal supply systems. However, many existing systems still lack a high level of digitalization. With more complexity, flexibility, more powerful tools, and approaches (and hence increased digitalization) will be required. Aside from technology, the integration of new digital business processes will make deployment easier. However, new concerns, such as data security and privacy, as well as questions concerning data ownership, must be addressed. This paper reflects on the results of the research conducted as part of the IEA DHC Annex TS4 project and the depiction thereof in the “Digitalisation of District Heating Systems – Optimised Operation and Maintenance of District Heating and Cooling Systems via Digital Process Management” guidebook [1]. https://www.iea-dhc.org/the-research/annexes/2018-2024-annex-ts4 © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.
palavras_chave: business processes and models; Digitalization of district heating; operation and maintenance

titulo: A federated deep domain adaptation-based framework for nuclear power steam turbines considering privacy-preserving
resumo: With the increasing awareness of environmental protection, sustainable manufacturing has become an important component in various industries. As an essential foundation for sustainable strategy, safe and reliable operation and maintenance of nuclear power resources is crucial, requesting agile and precise response and diagnosis of equipment failure signals. Due to security requirements, nuclear power plants strictly isolate operating data and form an actual data island. Simultaneously, the insufficient amount of fault sample data makes it difficult to establish an accurate fault diagnosis model. How to establish a stable and reliable nuclear power steam turbine vibration fault diagnosis model across different nuclear power plants and nuclear equipment has become a big problem. To achieve secure model aggregation without violating client privacy, federated learning (FL) has become a research hot spot for model aggregation, but it ignores the differences between source clients and fails to capture domain-invariant features during local training, which hinders its further development. To address this challenge, a federated deep domain adaptation-based framework considering privacy-preserving (FL-DDA) is proposed for operations and maintenance in nuclear power plants. The framework performs feature extraction locally in source nuclear power plants and targets nuclear power plants, such that the features are shared securely without revealing data privacy. At the same time, domain adversarial training is integrated into the local model training to realise the transfer of vibration fault diagnosis knowledge. Furthermore, an adaptive weight mechanism is devised to facilitate the adaptive adjustment of model weights in federated aggregation. Finally, a desensitised vibration dataset in nuclear power steam turbines is applied for validation, and FL-DDA is compared with other existing methods. Under the premise of data privacy security, the proposed FL-DDA framework proves to outperform its peers in vibration fault diagnosis and domain adaptation. © 2025 The Author(s). IET Collaborative Intelligent Manufacturing published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd on behalf of The Institution of Engineering and Technology.

titulo: Risk evolution model construction and dynamic assessment for urban buried gas pipeline leakage
fonte_periodico: Qinghua Daxue Xuebao Journal of Tsinghua University
resumo: [Objective] Currently, the service life of buried gas pipelines in most Chinese cities has exceeded 20 a. Because of the combined effects of third-party damage, corrosion, and human error, the operational safety of these pipelines has decreased, leading to a high probability of accidents. Because gas pipelines are often buried Underground, the transported medium is flammable and explosive, and they are located in densely populated areas, they possess characteristics of concealment and high risk. A leaking gas pipeline can easily trigger secondary fire and explosion incidents, causing severe casualties, property damage, and gas supply interruptions. [Methods] To prevent buried gas pipeline leakages and associated accidents in urban areas, a method for assessing the cascading risk evolution of pipeline leakages is proposed. Based on the operational characteristics of urban buried gas pipelines, risk factors, such as human factors, physical elements, environmental factors, and pipeline conditions are comprehensively integrated. These risk factors are further refined into a threeTevel indicator System. The logical relationships among the development process of leakage accidents and these risk factors are examined, and an integrated risk evolution and assessment model is developed through the Grey decision-making trial and evaluation laboratory (DEMATEL) method, interpretive structural modeling (ISM), and the dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) approach. The Grey-DEMATELTSM method is utilized to analyze causal hierarchical relationships among risk factors and identify key risk factors. The introduction of Grey numbers compensates for the subjective uncertainty of expert evaluations in the DEMATELTSM method, making the assessment results more aligned with actual conditions. Different types of risk factors are quantified through methods such as expert opinions, historical data, and probability distributions, and a pipeline leakage risk evolution DBN model is established based on the logical relationships among the risk factors. Furthermore, the probability of accident consequences is calculated and updated in real time to predict the potential development paths of accidents, thereby assisting in the safety Operation and maintenance decision-making of buried gas pipelines. [Results] The results indicated that the corrosion and human factors exhibited high levels of causality, centrality, and sensitivity, making them critical risk factors for preventing pipeline leakages. A dynamic risk analysis model was conducted the use of the gas pipeline explosion accident in Shiyan, Hub ei Province, as a case study. The results showed that the posterior probabilities of corrosion-related nodes were significantly higher than those of other nodes. Based on the assessment results, targeted measures were proposed to prevent initial incidents and cut off the accident propagation paths throughout the entire life cycle during the design and manufacturing phase, laying phase, and operational phase of the buried gas pipeline. The case study verified the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method. [Conclusions] The Grey-DEMATELTSM-DBN model can comprehensively consider the characteristics and quantitative representation of risk factors relate to humans, machines, environment, and management, even in situations with limited data. Based on historical accident information, it establishes a multiTevel hierarchical structure model for the causes of buried gas pipeline leakage accidents. The model quantifies the degree of influence and sensitivity among various risk factors and provides an intuitive display of accident evolution scenarios. The proposed method enables the dynamic analysis of the risk evolution process of buried gas pipeline leakages, providing Support for decision-making in safety Operations, maintenance, and accident investigations involving urban buried gas pipelines. © 2025 Tsinghua University. All rights reserved.

titulo: Challenge and path of high-quality development of coal mine intelligent construction
fonte_periodico: Meitan Kexue Jishu Coal Science and Technology Peking
resumo: Coal mine intelligentization is a vital direction for promoting the high-quality development of the coal industry. Reviews advancements in the foundational theories, technological systems, and demonstration applications of coal mine intelligentization, comprehensively analyzes the current status of intelligent coal mine construction, identifies key technological bottlenecks, and proposes pathways to address these challenges. In terms of foundational theories, the study focuses on the theoretical framework of digital coal mines and intelligent mining. For technological system construction, the key technical modules of intelligent coal mines are summarized. Regarding demonstration applications, typical intelligent mines are used as case studies to evaluate the application effects of intelligent systems in actual production and to identify technical, managerial encountered during their promotion. Building upon in-depth research into the foundational theories and technological systems of coal mine intelligentization, as well as practical experiences from demonstration mines, the study systematically examines the current status and pressing issues in intelligent geological support, information and communication systems, excavation, mining, and intelligent safety control systems. Special attention is given to addressing technological bottlenecks in efficient excavation under complex geological conditions, high-efficiency mining of thin coal seams and seams prone to dynamic pressure, robotic collaborative operations, and system maintenance. The research highlights the development of efficient excavation technologies for complex conditions, high-performance mining techniques for thin coal seams and dynamic-pressure coal seams, critical technologies for coal mine robotics, and innovations in next-generation intelligent safety control systems. It further emphasizes accelerating the large-scale and intelligent transformation of open-pit coal mines, improving the standardization of intelligent mine operation and maintenance systems, and facilitating iterative upgrades to intelligent systems. Driven by industry needs and guided by technological innovation, the study advocates for the integration, advancement, and digitalization of coal mining equipment to provide reliable technological and equipment support for the high-quality and sustainable development of coal mine intelligentization. © 2025 China Coal Society. titulo: Impact of Building Maintenance and Rehabilitation on Urban Sustainability: SOS Call for Action–Algarve Case Study
resumo: Buildings are designed for a 50-year lifetime. However, they can stand out for more without major repairs, depending on materials quality, climate aggression, use, and maintenance, among other aspects. Considering that Algarve’s building boom occurred between the 60s and 80s, a significant quantity of buildings is achieving their lifetime. Consequently, the demand for rehabilitation is rapidly increasing. Buildings, like other infrastructures, deteriorate over time due to several factors. However, the lack of maintenance stands out, and a structural survey is essential to determine the load capacity and ensure the safety of the society. Corrosion of reinforcement and spalling of the concrete cover may lead to loss of strength and unserviceability. Corrosion is initiated mainly by chloride contamination or exposure to atmospheric CO2, and the presence of moisture accelerates this degradation processes. In this study, different types of buildings located along the Algarve coastline, suffering from serious structural pathologies resulting mainly from the carbonation of the concrete, are presented. This article describes the constructive pathologies observed and presents the campaign test results, including carbonation tests, the presence of chlorides, corrosion potential, and measurements of covers, among others. These real examples show a rather deteriorated state of the building constructions, which are more than 50 years old in this touristic region. Thus, a priority line on the path towards housing sustainability is urgent. The authors pretend to launch an SOS signal and a call for action, to implement maintenance and rehabilitation plans legally. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.
palavras_chave: Maintenance; Rehabilitation; Urban Sustainability

titulo: Research and Design of Multi-function Integrated Boom Transporter based on ANSYS
resumo: With the constant evolution of substation (converter) station towards high capacity, high voltage level, and high-efficiency operation, in the process of construction and operation and maintenance of substation (converter) station, in order to improve operation efficiency and ensure personnel safety, based on finite element analysis and calculation, a crawler-type multifunction integrated boom transport vehicle is designed and developed. The integrated boom adopts a four-stage retractable design, and implements multi-port matching planning at the end, which can adapt three kinds of mechanical modules, such as lifting, manned, and gripper. The design of the whole vehicle is described in detail from three dimensions: mechanical, electrical, and hydraulic. Finally, the functional test and practical application of the developed integrated boom transport vehicle were carried out in a substation (converter) station. The results show that the crawler body chassis can be turned in place, the mechanical gripper module can grasp the equipment support with a diameter of 300 mm, a weight of 200-300 kg, and a length of 4.5 m, and the minimum length of the steel pipe is 3800 mm. The manned platform has a maximum load of 200 kg and a maximum height of 6 m for installation. © Published under licence by IOP Publishing Ltd

titulo: Appraising sustainable and resilient physical infrastructure facilities in higher education institutions: the role of smart maintenance management
autores: Ebekozien, A; Aigbavboa, C; Hafez, M; Samsurijan, MS; Oke, AE
resumo: Purpose – Infrastructural facilities, including higher education institutions (HEIs), are capital-intensive and require inclusive maintenance. In many developing countries, the maintenance is underfunded. This creates a challenging situation and puts pressure on the HEIs’ insufficient facilities in Nigeria. A modernised (smart) maintenance operation with pervasive digital technologies may enhance HEIs’ physical infrastructure facilities. Studies regarding how the smart maintenance management (SMM) role can enhance sustainable and resilient HEIs physical infrastructure facilities are scarce. Thus, this study aims to investigate the role of SMM and proffered measures to improve its application in Nigeria’s HEIs physical infrastructure facilities. Design/methodology/approach – The researchers adopted a qualitative method and collected data using observation of existing infrastructure and oral interviews across Nigeria. At least two HEIs were chosen from each zone for a good representation. Saturation was accomplished at the 25th interviewee. Also, the researchers manually adopted a thematic analysis and presented the main findings in themes. Findings – Findings reveal that SMM is a key aspect of Industry 4.0, and its relevance to HEIs infrastructure facilities cannot be overemphasised regarding resilience and sustainability. The absence of regulation/ standards, maintenance expertise in smart infrastructure facilities, low maintenance budget, the fear of skill- biased technological change, the perceived maintenance cost and occupant behaviour/resistance to change emerged as the major challenges facing SMM implementation in public HEIs. The research proffers recommendations based on these results. Originality/value – This study intends to reawaken policymakers to appraise the use of Internet of Things embedded in buildings to improve predictive maintenance in HEI infrastructure facilities. If fully embraced, the outcome will enhance the resilience and sustainability of infrastructure systems, including HEIs. © Emerald Publishing Limited

titulo: Evolution from Industry 1.0 to Industry 5.0 in the Context of Machine and Plant Maintenance
resumo: The changing needs of modern manufacturing require a re-examination of the maintenance management role in achieving key cost and service benefits. The development of maintenance requirements is supported by the progress of information technology, which provides new opportunities for the implementation of maintenance processes. The aim of the article is to describe the latest trends in the field of maintenance management from the perspective of the challenges of the fourth and fifth industrial revolution as well as economic, environmental, and social challenges. The five stages of the machine maintenance approach, related to the five industrial revolutions, are characterized, along with the advantages and weaknesses of each machine maintenance approach. The operating data in different operating periods were characterized. Digitalization can empower machine maintenance services by using collected data and advanced technologies to monitor equipment health, diagnose faults, predict and prevent failures long before they occur and ensure performance optimization. © 2025 The Author(s).

titulo: Process Safety Management
resumo: Process Safety Management provides comprehensive, practical guidance for developing and implementing process safety programs in the design, operation, and maintenance of industrial facilities. Drawing on clear definitions, real-world examples, historical context, and case studies, the book explains how process safety management (PSM) principles can be applied across the process and energy industries. A successor to Sutton’s earlier work Process Risk and Reliability Management, this volume reflects current industry practice and incorporates new developments in regulations, technology, and operational risk management. Across twenty-one chapters, it addresses the core elements of process safety, including hazards analysis, incident investigation, operating procedures, training, and audits. The discussion highlights how process safety improves not only safety performance but also operational integrity, equipment reliability, and system availability. The book reviews major process safety regulations and standards and outlines proposed updates by agencies such as OSHA and the EPA. It also considers emerging topics, including the role of generative AI in PSM and the implications of net-zero initiatives for process safety programs and sustainable operations. Process Safety Management is intended for graduate students in chemical, industrial, and process engineering, as well as for practicing engineers in design firms, consultancies, and operating companies. It also serves as a reference for professionals in regulatory organizations such as the CSB, OSHA, API, NFPA, and the US EPA who evaluate or oversee industrial safety programs. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. titulo: TOWARDS A COMPUTERISED MAINTENANCE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM FOR HEALTHCARE FACILITIES IN SOUTH AFRICA
resumo: Healthcare facilities constitute one of the essential infrastructures in any community. It plays a critical role in achieving Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) No. 3, which aims to enhance the health and well-being of individuals. Nevertheless, the efficient upkeep of healthcare facilities in South Africa has encountered several obstacles, and one potential solution is the implementation of computerised maintenance management systems (CMMS). This study explored the benefits of the deployment of CMMS for healthcare facilities in South Africa. A quantitative methodology required data collection through a structured questionnaire distributed to professionals within the built environment. The collected data was analysed via exploratory factor analysis, utilising principal component analysis as the extraction method. The study’s outcome identified four components as the benefits of the deployment of CMMS for healthcare facilities in South Africa: maintenance efficiency and facilities uptime, asset and resource management, regulatory compliance and safety assurance, and sustainability adherence and strategic insights. In conclusion, the study offered suggestions that could facilitate the effective integration of computational systems like CMMS to maintain healthcare facilities in South Africa. © 2025, Ceylon Institute of Builders. titulo: Maintenance management of existing bridges: a brief comparison of some Western world strategies
fonte_periodico: IABSE Congress Ghent 2025 the Essence of Structural Engineering for Society Proceedings
resumo: Many countries of the Western world have made significant investments in infrastructure development in the'60s-'70s and before. The management of the existing bridges is complex and requires very articulated and dynamic activities, made even more complicated by the large number of authorities dealing with this issue. After some catastrophic collapses, these activities have been systematically launched in some countries, even if significant delays are recorded in others. A task group of the IABSE Italian Group (IABSE-IT) has been activated to analyze the Italian guidelines for the assessment of the existing bridges and suggest potential improvements. To this aim, a survey of guidelines used in other countries for the management of existing bridge stock has been carried out. In this paper, the several approaches identified through the survey are preliminarily discussed and compared with the Italian one. © 2025 IABSE Congress Ghent 2025: The Essence of Structural Engineering for Society, Proceedings. titulo: Sludge Drying Lagoon Design and Its Comparison with Sludge Drying Bed and Evaporation Lagoon
fonte_periodico: Industrial Water and Waste Treatment Pollution Control
resumo: This is one of many publications written to transfer simple and low-cost US sludge dewatering technologies, such as sludge drying lagoons, sludge drying beds, and evaporation lagoons, to developing countries. Special emphasis in this publication is placed on the following subjects: (a) sludge drying lagoon process description, comparisons, and general design criteria; (b) sludge drying lagoon design procedures; (c) sludge drying lagoon operation and maintenance; (d) analysis of a sludge drying lagoon system; (e) flow diagram of a sludge drying lagoon system; (f) summary of the US Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA) design criteria for sludge drying lagoons for reference by developing countries; (g) comparison between sludge drying lagoons and sludge drying beds; (h) comparison between sludge drying lagoons and evaporation lagoons; and (i) important terminologies. All design equations, criteria, case histories, and examples adopt both international metric units and US customary units. The first sister publication, “Drying Beds Design,” covers the subjects of traditional and modern sludge drying beds, technology status, applications, limitations, performance, established design criteria, environmental impact and restrictions, cost estimation, design examples, case histories, and terminologies. The second sister publication, “Scientific Sludge Drying Beds Design,” introduces the design equations and sample calculations for determining the sludge drying beds’ drying time, surface area, number of drying bed sections, solids produced per year, sludge cakes removed per year, and manpower estimation for operation and maintenance using US customary units. In the third sister publication, “Sludge Drying Beds Design Using International Metric Units,” the author discusses the laboratory investigations for obtaining design parameters, engineering steps for sizing the drying beds, sludge loading rate verification, alternative scientific methods for drying bed design, acceptance or modification of design criteria, and applications and verification of the manpower models. In the fourth sister publication, “Dissolved Oxygen Model, Vapor Pressure, Evaporation Lagoon, and Flotation Post Aeration,” the theory of evaporation and the evaporation lagoon technology are presented in detail. The fifth sister publication, “Understanding Evaporation, Transpiration, Evapotranspiration, Precipitation, and Runoff Volume for Agricultural Waste Management,” provides important technical information for determining the minimum depth of sludge drying lagoons and evaporation lagoons. The US technical information, charts, design examples, and case histories presented in this sludge dewatering technology series are for developing countries to follow, in order to avoid or reduce environmental pollution, and in turn, achieve the goal of sustainable industrial and agricultural development around the world as established by the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO). © 2026 selection and editorial matter, Lawrence K. Wang, Mu-Hao Sung Wang, and Yung-Tse Hung individual chapters, the contributors.

titulo: Optimizing techniques to support the development of Green IoT
fonte_periodico: Design and Analysis of Green and Sustainable Iot Technologies for Future Wireless Communications
resumo: The rapid proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT) in recent years has garnered significant attention from both industry and academia due to its transformative potential and capacity to enable innovative solutions. Central to the IoT paradigm is the creation of expansive, collaborative networks that necessitate efficient functioning for long-term operational sustainability. Green IoT has emerged as a critical framework prioritizing the sustainability and feasibility of these extensive IoT ecosystems. This chapter provides a systematic and comprehensive exploration of the role of optimization in the design, operation, and maintenance of green IoT networks. An introductory overview of optimization principles and the formal structure of optimization problems is presented as a foundation for the discussion. This is followed by an in-depth analysis of various optimization methodologies, including their application in addressing key challenges within IoT networks. To contextualize these techniques, the chapter delves into their integration within network architectures and examines pivotal resource allocation strategies such as power allocation, beamforming, time allocation, and channel access, etc. These resource management strategies are critically evaluated for their role in enhancing the performance, efficiency, and sustainability of IoT systems. Furthermore, the chapter investigates emerging enabling technologies required to support the increasing density of IoT deployments. Specifically, the potential of technologies such as Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) and Backscatter Communications is highlighted for their ability to extend network capabilities, improve energy efficiency, and facilitate innovative communication paradigms. The chapter concludes by identifying future research directions and outlining the prospective development trajectories of next-generation IoT networks. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

titulo: Implementation of Tpm and Rcm to Increase Service Level in a Maintenance Sector Company
fonte_periodico: Proceedings of the World Congress on Mechanical Chemical and Material Engineering
resumo: Industrial maintenance management plays a critical role in operational continuity and efficiency in key sectors such as construction and mining. This study analyzes the impact of the joint implementation of Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) and Reliability-Centered Maintenance (RCM) in an industrial services company. A structured methodology was adopted, including the classification of critical equipment through ABC analysis and risk matrices, the use of Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA), and the planning of preventive tasks. The results show significant improvements in key indicators: Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) increased by an average of 28%, Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) improved from 40% to 65%, and the service level increased from 38% to 63%. Additionally, operational costs were reduced by 20%, optimizing equipment availability and strengthening operational sustainability. This study validates the effectiveness of TPM and RCM as complementary tools for optimizing maintenance processes, reducing failures, and enhancing competitiveness. The findings highlight the importance of integrating preventive and predictive strategies to face the challenges of industrial maintenance in dynamic environments. © 2025, Avestia Publishing. All rights reserved.

titulo: Geospatial Semantics-Based Mapping of Digital Twin-Based Controls for Scalable Management of Targeted Fan-Assisted Cooling System
fonte_periodico: Computing in Civil Engineering 2025 Computational and Intelligent Technologies Selected Papers from the ASCE International Conference on Computing in Civil Engineering 2025
resumo: Digital twin (DT) technology offers promising advancements in building operations but faces scalability challenges due to the complexity of maintaining fixed control loops and semantic models. This study introduces a geospatial semantics-based DT framework for scalable and adaptive control loop management, demonstrated through its application to targeted fan-assisted cooling systems. By integrating geospatial data with logical reasoning, the framework automates control loop mapping for grid ceiling-embedded fans. Experimental validation with 120 participants in a shared office space tested three DT user interface designs (person-based, object-based, and suggestion-based controls) showing strong user satisfaction (p < 0.00) across all three interfaces. To ease the adoption our proposed approach, a plugin, geospatial semantics-BrickSchema integration, was developed to streamline geospatial data integration and semantic development through graphical programming. These findings highlight the framework's potential to overcome scalability challenges in traditional building management systems, offering a flexible and sustainable solution for dynamic real-world environments. © ASCE.

titulo: Study on Carbon Emission Data of Urban Buildings
resumo: In pursuit of global carbon peak and neutrality, precise carbon emission measurement using advanced management tools and technologies is crucial for effective urban carbon reduction and sustainable growth. We propose classifying building emissions into three distinct stages—construction, operation, and maintenance—by utilizing mathematical methods and Building Information Modeling (BIM) for separate calculation. Moreover, we recommend implementing an annual carbon emission management system tailored to each building. © The Author(s) 2025.

titulo: Expert method to support sustainable renovation decisions
resumo: The purpose of this article is to present a practical application of an expert method for setting renovation priorities for residential building maintenance when setting sustainability goals. The proposed method is based on an innovative approach that provides the techno-economic data necessary to perform a multi-stage optimization to achieve a long-term building renovation strategy. To conduct the study, a mixed-integer linear programming MILP was used that takes into account constraints and boundary conditions that are updated for each year of the time schedule horizon. The developed methodology makes it possible both to identify future renovation activities and to develop a program for their optimal combination, in which the activities are scheduled at the appropriate optimal stage of the time horizon. © 2025, Wydawnictwo SIGMA-NOT. titulo: Photovoltaic power prediction for smart energy monitoring systems based on digital twins
fonte_periodico: Proceedings of SPIE the International Society for Optical Engineering
resumo: Digital twin technology provides an innovative program for PV system monitoring, gradually replacing the traditional monitoring methods. By building a virtual model to link with the actual system, and collecting power generation parameters with sensors in real time, it realizes dynamic simulation of operation status and abnormal warning. Combining historical and real-time data, and through the corresponding algorithms, the technology can predict potential failures and initiate preventive maintenance, effectively reducing operation and maintenance costs, while improving system efficiency. © 2025 SPIE.
