titulo: Concrete with incorporation of polymeric recycled aggregate
autores: Carvalho, M; dos Santos, CP; Lima, EMS; de Oliveira, HA; De Melo, L; Almeida, VGD; de Melo, FMC
resumo: This study aims to evaluate the properties of a concrete with polymeric glue residue aggregate, through formulations by replacing natural coarse aggregate (NCA) with polymeric coarse aggregate (PCA). The gradual increase in the PCA content resulted in a reduction in consistency, specific gravity, compressive and flexural strength. However, there was an increase in the void ratio and water absorption. Regarding durability, the partial replacement of 40% of NCA by PCA showed the best performance. The conclusion is that it is possible to use polymer glue waste as aggregate in the production of concrete, helping to reduce the extraction of raw materials and the pollution of this waste in the environment. Its use in concrete production can increase the durability of this material, which will reduce building maintenance. © 2025 Pontificia Universidad Catolica de Chile. All rights reserved.

titulo: Technical Challenges of Transmission Equipment in a 230kV Underground Transmission Substation in Singapore
fonte_periodico: 2025 25th Conference of the Electric Power Supply Industry Cepsi 2025
resumo: Underground 230kV transmission substations present unique technical challenges, particularly in the deployment of high-voltage equipment such as switchgear, transformers, and reactors. This paper examines the critical challenges associated with the design, installation, operation, and maintenance of 230kV transmission equipment in underground environments, focusing on spatial constraints, thermal management, and environmental sustainability.The confined spatial footprint of underground substations necessitates innovative engineering solutions for the transportation, hoisting, and installation of heavy equipment, such as large power transformers and reactors. Advanced hoisting techniques, including modular assembly and the use of specialized machinery, are explored to address access limitations and ensure operational efficiency. The paper also highlights the importance of optimized substation layouts and room height configurations to accommodate equipment while minimizing escalation costsThermal management is a paramount concern in underground environments, where natural ventilation is absent. Power transformers and reactors generate significant heat, necessitating efficient cooling systems to ensure reliability and prevent overheating. This paper identifies water-cooling systems as the most effective solution for underground applications, detailing their design, integration, and redundancy measures to enhance system resilience. The selection of transformer types suitable for underground use is also discussed, emphasizing compact designs and advanced insulation materials.Maintenance and renewal of transmission equipment in underground settings pose additional challenges. The paper explores strategies for site testing, predictive maintenance, and equipment renewal, including the use of modular designs and real-time monitoring systems to minimize downtime and extend asset life. Environmental considerations are addressed through the development of SF6 gas containment systems, which mitigate the risk of gas leaks and reduce greenhouse gas emissions, aligning with Singapore's sustainability objectives.This paper provides valuable insights into addressing the technical, logistical, and environmental challenges associated with underground 230kV transmission substation. It offers solutions and mitigation strategies to achieve safe, reliable and sustainable power supply in Singapore. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: LLM-based Transformation of Electrical Distribution Grids: Gathering Requirements for Optimised Workforce Management in the Era of Renewable Energy Integration
fonte_periodico: Proceedings of the Conference on Production Systems and Logistics
resumo: The advancing climate change and the resulting need to restructure the energy supply industry mark the beginning of an era of significant upheavals, profoundly impacting energy distribution. The ongoing integration of renewable energy sources introduces new strains on power grids, as they are now confronted with bidirectional energy flows as well as significant fluctuations in energy generation and demand. These developments pose unprecedented challenges to the physical integrity and operational efficiency of distribution networks. Therefore, electrical distribution grid operators (DGOs) must balance these new challenges while ensuring supply security and sustainability, as well as considering economic efficiency. To meet these new challenges, the development of innovative maintenance strategies is essential. In this context, the digitalisation of power grids emerges as a key technology, offering solutions through the introduction of holistic assistance and prognosis systems (APS). This paper focuses on the collection and analysis of requirements leading to the development of an assistance system for maintenance workers in distribution networks based on Large Language Models (LLM). The LLM aims to support workforce management by providing maintenance workers with targeted information and real-time recommendations. The methodology involves conducting expert interviews to gather essential requirements, followed by a thorough analysis of the collected data. Based on this, the foundation for developing the LLM-based assistance system is established. The results demonstrate how LLMs can enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of maintenance management by optimising workflows and supporting personnel in decision-making processes. © Institute for Production and Logistics Research GbR Herberger, Hübner & Beus.

titulo: Investigation and analysis on the charging status and standard of pharmacy intravenous admixture service in China
resumo: Objectives: The charging policy of pharmacy intravenous admixture service (PIVAS) is not merely a minor “billing issue” confined to individual hospitals, but rather a critical component that impacts the safety, efficiency, equity, and long-term sustainability of the national healthcare system. Its implications extend across patients, medical institutions, the pharmaceutical industry, and even the broader public health landscape. To establish a foundation for the national charging standard of intravenous admixture service, this study comprehensively investigated and analyzed the operational costs and current charging policies of PIVAS across 30 provinces in China. Methods: Questionnaires were distributed through the “Wenjuan Xing” platform from May 6th to 1 July 2022. After data generation and export by the platform, statistical and descriptive analyses of the questionnaire results were conducted using statistical software, including EXCEL, SPSS. Results: A total of 761 PIVAS surveyed, 91.59% were affiliated with the pharmacy department, while 6.70% belonged to the hospital independent department. Most PIVAS strongly agreed with imposing fees, while most tertiary hospitals agreed that dispensing fees should be categorized based on hospital levels; however, most secondary hospitals disagreed. Approximately 60.58% of PIVAS have implemented a charging system which allows charges after inspection and evaluation. Regarding changes for different drugs nationwide, common drugs had an average charge standard of 4.39 yuan per bag while antibacterial drugs averaged 5.01 yuan per bag. Hazardous drugs had an average charge of 23.17 yuan per bag, whereas parenteral nutrition solutions averaged 38.75 yuan per bag. The annual operating cost of PIVAS in China was approximately RMB 2,098,100, with the integrated operating cost comprising 89.36% of the total, while dispensing cost accounted for only 10.64%. Human costs emerged as the highest annual consumption (74.20%), followed by facility maintenance (4.77%) and equipment acquisition costs (3.44%). Conclusion: The lack of a unified inspection and evaluation standard as well as charging standard in China is currently an urgent issue that needs to be addressed. The existing charging standard falls below the recommended level, thus it is necessary to develop a more reasonable and equitable charging standard that takes into account operational costs. This study can serve as an empirical reference for national medical insurance and health administration authorities in establishing unified regulatory standards and dynamic pricing adjustment mechanisms for PIVAS. It contributes to the transition of PIVAS from “regionally fragmented management” to “nationally standardized operations,” thereby supporting the dual objectives of enhancing healthcare service quality and optimizing the utilization efficiency of medical insurance funds. titulo: Cost Analysis of Various Flexible Resources in New Power Systems
resumo: To address climate change and achieve sustainable development, it is urgent for power systems to transition to low-carbon, clean renewable energy. A high proportion of renewable energy will significantly impact the cost structure of new power systems. This paper studies the costs of various flexible resources in the new power system, including generation, grid, and storage, calculating the Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE) according to investment construction costs fuel costs, and operation and maintenance costs. The economic analysis and evaluation of these flexible resources provide scientific guidance for the optimal allocation of resources in the power system, holding significant economic importance. © Beijing Paike Culture Commu. titulo: Digital Twin Application and Facilitation in the AEC Industry’s Operation and Maintenance Stage
fonte_periodico: Studies in Systems Decision and Control
resumo: Digital twins are transforming various industries by enabling data-driven decision-making and enabling efficient operations. However, research on digital twins often focuses on specific sectors, leaving untapped potential across a spectrum. This paper aims to address these challenges by highlighting the pivotal role of digital twins in converging cyber-physical data for sector-specific applications. Drawing on prior research on big data and digital twin technology, the paper presents a cross-sector perspective, introducing innovative applications in sectors like healthcare, energy, and transportation. The research encourages cross-sector collaboration, innovation, and unlocking the potential of digital twins in diverse domains. By exploring the possibilities of digital twins in diverse domains, this research encourages organisation to harness their power for enhanced efficiency, intelligence, and sustainability, shaping a brighter future for industries worldwide. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

titulo: Integration of BIM and GIS on web viewer environment for Tan Cang station asset management
resumo: This study presents the application of the BIM&GIS integration model on Web platform for asset management. From the literature review, three main types of BIM&GIS integration models are pointed out: BIM lead - GIS support, GIS lead - BIM support, and BIM and GIS equally role and are merged by a third platform. Thereby, the characteristics and features of each type are evaluated. Then, the BIM&GIS integration model is conducted under the third type for the case study of Tan Cang station, on Metro Line 1: Ben Thanh - Suoi Tien. The observations show the BIM&GIS integration model is a useful tool in which helping project stakeholders deliver optimized decisions for management, exploitation, operation, and maintenance of the project and gradually implementing sustainable development for a smart city. © 2025 Elsevier B.V.. titulo: SUSTAINING AIRLINKS THROUGH DESTINATION STAKEHOLDERS’ COLLABORATION
fonte_periodico: Strategies for Sustainable Air Services Development an Airline Destination Collaborative Approach
resumo: This chapter functions as a capstone delving into the critical role of destination stakeholder collaboration in developing sustainable and viable airlinks. It begins by examining the interdependencies between airlines and various destination stakeholders, including airports, tourism boards, local governments, and other pertinent destination stakeholders. In recognizing their roles, the chapter highlights how these relationships contribute to the successful operation and maintenance of airlinks. To do so, it explores strategies for effective collaboration, and addresses challenges such as aligning diverse interests and managing shared resources. As a core focus, the chapter hones-in on dissecting how value is created in developing airlinks through activities such as resources exchanges, and shared goal setting to foster cooperative relationships grounded in trust and reciprocity. It argues that robust stakeholder collaboration is essential for ensuring resilience and competitiveness of destinations and offers a processual roadmap to ensure stakeholder collaboration in air connectivity growth and strategic planning. © 2025 selection and editorial matter, Kareem Yarde and Chrystal Zhang; individual chapters, the contributors.

titulo: Where Commitment Meets Innovation: Transforming EJ Commitment into Tangible Impact
fonte_periodico: Proceedings Weftec 2025 98th Water Environment Federation Technical Exhibition and Conference
resumo: The Northeast Ohio Regional Sewer District (“the District”) provides wastewater and stormwater services to more than 1 million Northeast Ohioans every day. In 2022, the District published our Environmental Justice (EJ) Commitment Statement, clarifying how EJ has always resonated with our mission and establishing guideposts to help us reflect upon the effectiveness of our efforts. The “EJ in Action” and “Environmental Justice Resource Guide” tools have since been developed in-house to bring EJ to a tangible level and provide actionable guidance for each of the nearly 800 District employees. This paper offers an example of how a utility can activate employees at every level beyond commitment and discussion of Environmental Justice into a space of meaningful action and engagement that has tangible impact on their service area. The District defines EJ as follows: “through meaningful engagement, informed actions, and equitable treatment, the District will continue to provide equitable treatment and meaningful engagement of our residents—inclusive of all races, cultures, lifestyles, neighborhoods, and incomes—so we may advance our clean-water work without placing disproportionate environmental or fiscal burdens on those we serve.” Environmental Justice has always been inherent to and a part of District work. At the most basic level, we serve an EJ role by treating wastewater, reducing or eliminating combined sewer overflow (CSO) pollution, and addressing stormwater flooding and erosion. For example, on a recent Engineering & Construction Department (E&C) CSO Control project, the Kingsbury Run Consolidation Sewer, realignment of one of the tunnels will reduce impact to residents in a low-income neighborhood both during construction and future operation and maintenance, and also save costs through improved constructability of the tunnel. The realignment can be viewed solely as technical enhancement, but through the EJ lens this is a tangible example of informed action and equitable treatment at work to reduce potential environmental or fiscal burden. This example was discussed at an E&C All-Department meeting in an effort to bring EJ from a conceptual level to a practical one. E&C staff were eager to have additional examples highlighted to further their knowledge. From this feedback was born the “EJ in Action” database. This tool helps identify, track, and communicate EJ opportunities in the planning, design, and construction of E&C projects. Examples are submitted by employees, who are then given the opportunity to present about their example in future departmental meetings—a combination of ongoing departmental learning and professional development in one. After successful rollout to the E&C department, the tool will be expanded in 2025 to include District-wide examples as part of NEORSD’s 2025-27 Strategic Plan. Building familiarity with EJ is a first step for many employees, but soon deeper questions emerge. What tools or guidance exist that help employees ensure EJ is woven into their work in a more meaningful way than a simple “add-on” or check box? How can we ensure the core connection to EJ is being made across all facets of our work as a utility: project management, communication, operation and maintenance, field services, and finance…to name just a few. This deeper question and request for guidance is being answered by the District’s “Environmental Justice Resource Guide.” This comprehensive document, developed by staff across the District, provides brainstorming prompts, communication frameworks, a digital hub of geo-referenced data to visualize and measure EJ in project areas, and suggestions for best practices to help ensure EJ is a key component in every project. The document is currently being finalized by the Environmental Justice Committee and will be rolled out for District-wide use and reference by the end of 2025. titulo: A case for applications of machine-vision-Aided industrial robotics in pipeline bolting
fonte_periodico: American Society of Mechanical Engineers Pressure Vessels and Piping Division Publication PVP
resumo: This paper addresses the case for a practical application of AI by incorporating it into the process of installing and removing bolts from piping joints. The major cases identified are reducing human error and bridging the construction labor gap. This paper then discusses the application of AI by describing the 3 guiding objectives in tool-design identified by industry, safety, speed, and quality, and the various industries where this application is immediately relevant. The current process for industrial bolting is still heavily reliant on human labor, and thus prone to human error. As industrial assets age, they become less forgiving of human error and thus more prone to risk of incident. There is a direct correlation between the quality of bolting labor and bolting reliability. Bolting labor quality needs to improve to mitigate risk of industrial incidents. Emerging research and development has identified machine vision, a form of AI, as a key opportunity to improve bolting reliability by automating select components of bolting labor. In parallel, there is a continued increase in demand for bolting labor projected across industrial construction. It will be difficult for construction crews to meet industry needs at the current staffing levels. Continuing to pursue research and development of machine-vision enabled industrial robotics to improve the safety, speed, and quality of bolting labor is also a step in bridging the construction labor gap. After surveying over 75 industry leaders, it became apparent that bolting labor is analyzed by 3 major factors: safety, speed, and quality. These factors are significant in piping alignment, worker safety, flange seal integrity, equipment reliability, and worker efficiency. Not only is the quality of bolting labor important for the duration of the work, but the impact of the labor is in effect over the course of the equipment runtime until the next turnaround cycle (often 4+ years) long after the bolting crew has left the jobsite. In pursuit of delivering improved quality bolting labor to piping joints, emerging research and development has led to new designs of a hands-free bolting robot. This new approach has been intentionally designed following industry guidance along the same 3 criteria: safety, speed, and quality. The research and product development addressed in this paper is initially targeted towards industrial infrastructure in the following areas: facility maintenance, capital projects, facility retrofits, and new facility construction. This positions the emerging technology strategically across all types of energy infrastructure and in a variety of relevant industries: oil & gas, chemical/petrochemical, pharmaceuticals, food & beverage, water/wastewater/water treatment/sewage, agriculture, cosmetics, irrigation, nuclear, mining, and green/sustainable manufacturing. There is a strong case for improving bolting reliability and bridging the construction labor gap across all of these industries. Copyright © 2025 by ASME.

titulo: Using Linked Data Containers for BIM Based Structural Inspection Workflows
resumo: The proliferation of Building Information Modeling (BIM) in the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry has led to an increased amount of digital information. During design, construction, and operating phases of a structure, data in a diverse array of formats and versions is being produced and exchanged between actors involved. Solely in the operating phase with the growing prevalence of digital processes, the need for a robust and sustainable approach for integrating and storing data that spans a structure’s lifecycle has become vital. To this end, Linked Data containers may be employed to establish connections and relationships between different data sources and processes in a structured and standardized manner. This paper aims to explore the potential of applying a Linked Data approach to establish connections among heterogeneous data sources during the operating and maintenance phases of bridges. A case study of structural inspection data from material tests on a road bridge is employed, in which data integrated into the container ranges from test design to presentation of test results. The proposed implementation leverages the standardized Information Container for Linked Document Delivery (ICDD), capable of accommodating various data formats and enabling link creation through Resource Description Framework (RDF) triples. Consequently, a collection of RDF triples and various document formats form the Linked Data container was proposed for inspection data. Moreover, it is shown that the proposed framework has the potential to be extended by mapping additional ontologies related to various structural or material tests by demand. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential use cases of Linked Data containers within the AEC industry and their respective shortcomings at present. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.
palavras_chave: Building Information Modeling (BIM); Building operation; Linked data (LD)

titulo: Distribution Transformer Heavy Overload Classification Evaluation Method Based on Early Warning Domain Modeling
resumo: Aiming at the problem of early warning and evaluation of operation conditions of distribution transformers, a practical grade-warning method of operation risk in distribution area is proposed, which is based on the fusion analysis of overload rate, sustainable running time after overload and winding temperature after overload. The operating state of distribution transformer is described as the operating point of overload rate, sustainable running time and winding temperature. By analyzing the location of the operation area where the operation point belongs, the operation risk assessment of the distribution platform area is carried out, which is conducive to the operation and maintenance personnel's accurate grasp of the operating conditions of the distribution transformer in the platform area. The results of example analysis show the validity and reliability. © Beijing Paike Culture Commu. Co., Ltd. 2025.

titulo: Operational and Maintenance Challenges of Energy Storage Systems in Microgrid
fonte_periodico: IEEE Conference on Technologies for Sustainability Sustech
resumo: The integration of battery energy storage systems (BESS) in microgrids has gained significant attention in recent years due to their ability to improve the reliability, efficiency, and sustainability of power supply. However, the operational and maintenance challenges of BESS in microgrids are still a major concern. This paper reviews the current state of the art of BESS in microgrids and identifies the key operational and maintenance challenges. The challenges include battery degradation, state of charge management, power quality issues, and communication protocols. It also explores the potential solutions to these challenges, including advanced battery management systems, predictive maintenance, and standardized communication protocols. The results of this study can provide valuable insights for the design, operation, and maintenance of BESS in microgrids. © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: Battery Energy Storage Systems; Maintenance Challenges; Microgrids; Operational Challenges; Renewable Energy Sources

titulo: Development of a Sustainable Electrical Substation Design Using the Malaysian Carbon Reduction and Environmental Sustainability Tool (MyCREST)
fonte_periodico: Iop Conference Series Earth and Environmental Science
resumo: Although high-voltage electricity substations contribute less to the overall carbon footprint of an electricity company compared to other operations, converting them to eco-friendly designs is a more accessible option than larger interventions like shifting to renewable energy sources. This study presents the selection of suitable design elements for the redesign of a 132kV substation building for Malaysia, guided by the Malaysian Carbon Reduction and Sustainability Tool (MyCREST). The aim was achieved through improving project implementation, enhancing energy and water efficiency, sourcing sustainable materials, and incorporating green design elements. Through MyCREST evaluation, a typical 132kV substation has a baseline score of 42 points, and the redesign yields element sets that qualify for 1-star to 5-star ratings. Taking into account design, construction, operation, and maintenance, the maximum achievable MyCREST score is 123 points, qualifying for a 5-star rating. However, the feasibility of these improvements depend on site constraints, costs, and the need for additional simulations and environmentally efficient equipment.  © Published under licence by IOP Publishing Ltd.

titulo: Research on stability control of deep learning algorithms in soft fault diagnosis technology for photovoltaic inverters
fonte_periodico: Proceedings of SPIE the International Society for Optical Engineering
resumo: Aiming at the problems of complex circuits and short fault duration in photovoltaic (PV) inverters, a fault diagnosis algorithm based on Self-Organizing Map (SOM) and Back Propagation (BP) neural networks is proposed. Simulations are conducted using Simulink software to model the faults of PV inverters. Based on the collected relevant parameters, the SOM-BP neural network is employed for fault diagnosis. The simulation results show that the proposed SOM-BP neural network achieves high accuracy rates in both the training set and the test set, demonstrating a high accuracy in fault diagnosis.Effectively reduce operation and maintenance costs, ensure the stable operation of PV power plants, and help the sustainable development of PV power generation industry. © 2025 SPIE.
palavras_chave: BP neural network; deep learning; fault diagnosis; photovoltaic inverter; SOM Neural Network

titulo: Progressive Collapse Mitigation of Hospital Buildings Using Different Retrofit Strategies
resumo: Growing global concern about progressive collapse in building structures under abnormal loads has driven extensive research on enhancing resistance through advanced design and retrofit solutions. This paper introduces innovative retrofit strategies using steel bracing and rooftop outrigger-belt truss systems tailored for hospital buildings. These systems improve vertical stiffness and strength with minimal additional mass and sections, enabling rapid, low-impact, and reversible implementation while maintaining uninterrupted building operations during retrofitting. Nonlinear dynamic analyses of real hospital buildings highlight significant improvements in load redistribution and collapse resistance, offering an efficient and sustainable solution for critical infrastructures. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.
palavras_chave: Nonlinear analysis; Progressive Collapse Retrofit; Robustness

titulo: Sustainability and Resiliency in Airport Energy Infrastructure: A Multidisciplinary Methodology for Optimizing Building Operations
fonte_periodico: AIAA Science and Technology Forum and Exposition AIAA Scitech Forum 2025
resumo: There is a striking difference in the domain of environmental consciousness: a large amount of greenhouse gases is produced by commercial buildings compared to what is commonly perceived in the transportation sector. The International Panel on Climate Change has labelled buildings as the third largest contributor of greenhouse emissions with at least 17.5%, whereas the aviation industry merely contributes 2%. Hence, there is an urgent need to decarbonize buildings to enhance sustainability, a sound path towards mitigating effects of climate change. Moreover, continued power supply to critical buildings such as hospitals and airports, is important to ensure life safety of their users. Power outages in such buildings disrupt operations resulting to substantial financial losses. For instance, the 2017 outage at the Hartsfield Jackson Atlanta Airport in the United States demonstrated the result — a 11-hour period without power which brought Delta airlines about $50M estimated in loss. From a system-of-systems perspective, this paper investigates decarbonizing of buildings and infrastructure by considering aspects of sustainability, resiliency, and a ordability. A detailed account of scenarios involving power outages, building HVAC systems and the demand of electric vehicles is balanced against the amount of power from the main grid and distributed energy resources including photovoltaics, storage systems and power generators. The aim of this study is to provide a financially optimum combination of grid energy and DERs (Distributed Energy Resources). As such, this study utilizes a proposed methodology that employs use of multi-variate regression models to integrate a building HVAC system modeled using Simcenter Amesim in a representative thermal envelope with an optimization tool developed by the US National Renewable Energy Laboratory. These modeling tools are used to create a parametric and interactive tool that assists stakeholders in assessing tradeo’s for building energy sourcing to meet power demands even during power outages and assess its impacts financially and environmentally. © 2025, American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics Inc, AIAA. All rights reserved.

titulo: Controlling Airplane Crashing Using Multi-Agent Technology (MAT) Using Fuzzy Analytical Technique
fonte_periodico: Recent Advances in Smart Communication Technologies for A Sustainable Future
resumo: The rapid growth of air transportation has intensified global concerns regarding aviation safety, demanding the integration of advanced and intelligent technologies. This chapter investigates the role of Multi-Agent Technology (MAT) in enhancing safety across critical phases of aviation, including aircraft design, manufacturing, operations, and maintenance. Although prior studies have addressed isolated aspects, comprehensive research on the systemic impact of MAT on aviation safety remains limited. Employing the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), the study identifies and ranks the most influential MAT variables that contribute to effective crash prevention. The outcomes provide a structured decision-support model for aviation professionals, enabling targeted investments and strategies that strengthen safety performance both qualitatively and financially. By embedding smart communication technologies within the MAT framework, this research not only advances safety mechanisms but also contributes to building a more sustainable and resilient future for the aviation sector. © 2026 by IGI Global Scientific Publishing. All rights reserved.

titulo: Research on Multi - Objective Optimal Scheduling of Integrated Energy Systems Based on Distributed Neurodynamics
fonte_periodico: 2025 3rd International Conference on Cyber Energy Systems and Intelligent Energy Iccsie 2025
resumo: Under the impetus of the sustainable development concept, the construction of an integrated energy system containing renewable energy has become a research hotspot. Existing studies mostly adopt centralized algorithms for optimization scheduling, which have problems such as low efficiency and high pressure. This paper proposes a distributed neural dynamics optimization algorithm, combined with multi-objective optimization theory, to optimize the scheduling of an integrated energy system containing electricity, heat, gas and cold. By refining the load types, the electricity-gas and electricity-gas-heat transfer load models are constructed; the distributed neural dynamics algorithm is designed and its stability is verified; multi-objective optimization takes into account economic costs while gradually incorporating environmental protection and operation and maintenance factors. The Matlab simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has fast convergence speed and good stability, and has practical application value.  © 2025 IEEE.

The topics discussed include: sustainable harvest/collection optimization of residual agro-forestry biomass including wildfire risk; classifying forest supply chain traceability data with an ontological approach; maintenance management: a review on problems and solutions; towards a digital twin for production planning: combining discrete event simulation and ml for flexible job shops; subcontracting risk management in the Portuguese molds and plastics industry; the critical uncertainties method to enhance robustness in circularity; a physics-informed ai control system for enhanced safety and automation in hollow glass manufacturing; a digital twin architecture for monitoring and quality assessment for a composite filament extrusion pilot line; and fiber laser surface pre-treatment on steel substrate to investigate the influence of surface state on fabrication durable joints.

titulo: INVESTIGATION OF SUSPENDED SEDIMENT AND TURBINE EROSION FOR THE SUSTAINABLE OPERATION OF A PLANNED LOW-HEAD HYDROPOWER PLANT
fonte_periodico: Proceedings of the IAHR World Congress
resumo: Sediment-laden flow plays a crucial role in the design, operation, and maintenance of hydropower plants (HPPs) where sediment may cause turbine erosion as well as sedimentation. This study focuses on the sediment management at the planned low-head run-of-river HPP Massongex-Bex-Rhone (MBR) on the Rhone River, Switzerland. Historical sediment and discharge data were analyzed, a field measurement campaign was conducted during a flood in 2021, and the IEC 62364 erosion model was applied to estimate the expected turbine erosion. Mitigation measures such as turbine coatings and temporary shutdowns of the HPP during high sediment periods were evaluated. Results show that turbine shutdowns at river discharges above 400 m³/s reduce the average suspended sediment concentration in the turbine water by 31%, significantly decreasing abrasive erosion. Moreover, the headwater drawdowns during shutdowns allow for sediment passage. The findings highlight the importance of both effective sediment management and turbine design for sustainable hydropower. © 2025 IAHR.

titulo: Social acceptance of water quality through decentralized greywater treatment using green wall system
fonte_periodico: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
resumo: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Addressing water scarcity through innovative and sustainable solutions is crucial in regions like Jordan, where resources are limited, and community involvement plays a pivotal role in ensuring success. This study examines the social acceptance and readiness of university dormitory residents, specifically female students at Al-Zahra’a Dormitory, the University of Jordan, for implementing a decentralized greywater treatment system using green walls. This study seeks to examine the social factors influencing the deployment of decentralized greywater treatment systems, particularly focusing on enhancing public acceptance and ensuring their sustainable use in urban settings. METHODS: This study investigated the technical capabilities of the greywater treatment system by analyzing the quality of the treated effluent against Jordanian standards, thereby evaluating its potential for reuse in toilet flushing and irrigation applications. Additionally, a structured questionnaire with 24 questions was distributed to dormitory residents and staff to explore social acceptance. Responses were categorized into four thematic groups: 1) Awareness and Understanding, assessing participants’ familiarity with greywater treatment; 2) Perceptions and Attitudes, evaluating opinions and concerns regarding the system; 3) Environmental Impact, examining perceived benefits and potential drawbacks; and 4) Participation and Support, measuring willingness to engage in operation and maintenance activities. This mixed-methods strategy offered in-depth understanding of the technical viability and social interactions involved in the implementation of the system. FINDINGS: The findings indicate that 90 percent of respondents are aware of water scarcity, with the majority strongly supporting innovative solutions like the green wall system. The study emphasizes the critical role of community participation in the success of sustainable systems. Notably, 82 percent of respondents expressed interest in training programs on the operation and maintenance of the greywater system, demonstrating a proactive attitude toward its long-term sustainability. Morever, 87 percent favored the expansion of the system from the dormitory to other residential neighborhoods, reflecting a strong consensus and the potential for more extensive application. However, concerns regarding potential issues such as odor and health impacts were noted, with nearly 50 percent of participants expressing discomfort. CONCLUSION: Overall, strong community interest and readiness for green wall-based greywater systems highlight their potential to address water challenges. Continuous monitoring, system optimization, and stakeholder collaboration are essential for long-term success. By implementing well-defined protocols, offering thorough training, and optimizing management strategies, organizations can alleviate health and environmental concerns, which in turn cultivates trust among users. Expanding these systems to other areas with community involvement and outreach programs can amplify impact. Continued investigation into social acceptance will improve strategies and promote the broader implementation of decentralized greywater treatment solutions. © This is an open access article under the CC BY license (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

resumo: The proceedings contain 18 papers. The special focus in this conference is on Environmental Challenges in Civil Engineering. The topics include: Impact of Building Maintenance and Rehabilitation on Urban Sustainability: SOS Call for Action–Algarve Case Study; diagnostic and Assessing the Limit States of Prestressed Concrete Railway Bridge; Some Issues of the Kyiv TV Tower Renovation After the Missile Attack; the Influence of Global Warming on the Change of Climatic Loads on the Territory of Ukraine; holism and Reductionism in Determining Environmental Impacts; tool Development for Precast Concrete Elements in Robot-Assisted Flow Production; multi-functional Integration in Clay-Cardboard Sandwich Structure with Semi-automated Manufacturing; sustainable Production of Complex Precast Concrete Elements Without Demolding Drafts Using Concrete Extrusion and Processing; efficient Production of Precast Concrete Staircases Using Additive-Manufactured, Component-Integrated Formworks Systems; concrete Extrusion Using Sustainable Cement Alternatives; behavior of Half-Slab and Beam-and-Block Floor Supported on Four Edges: Short- and Long-Term Studies; the Sustainability of Minimum Space: Removable Off-Grid Architecture for Outdoor Tourism; design Public Space with Water for an Ecological City: Two International Design Summer Schools; urban Public Space Accessibility–A Literature Review; evolution of Architecture Integrated with Greenery in the Works of Marek Budzyński; sustainability in Emergency: Design Strategies and Waste Management for the Living Situation in the Refugee Camps.

titulo: A Digital Twin Framework for Real-time Energy Optimization: A Simulated Case Study of the Podium Office Building, New Cairo, Egypt
resumo: The growing demand for smarter and more energy-efficient buildings has led to increasing interest in digital twin (DT) technology for building operation and management. This paper presents a DT framework developed to improve the energy performance of the Podium Office Building in Cairo Festival City, New Cairo, Egypt. A detailed EnergyPlus model, supported by Python-based tools (eppy and pyEnergyPlus), was used to test three HVAC control strategies: a baseline fixed schedule, a real-time DT-informed strategy, and a predictive optimization approach. By integrating local climate data and realistic occupancy patterns, the study evaluates energy savings, CO2 reductions, and indoor comfort improvements. The results indicate that the DT framework can significantly enhance performance in commercial buildings, particularly in hot-arid climates, offering practical insights for future applications of DTs in energy management and sustainable design. © 2025 Faculty of Engineering, Mansoura University.
palavras_chave: Digital twin; Energy optimization; Office buildings

titulo: Optimizing Power Resilience Performance of Intelligent Solar Photovoltaic System for Smart Energy Management Considering Reliability and Cost
resumo: Due to being nonpolluting and renewable, intelligent solar photovoltaic (PV) technology is widely used to provide electricity and becomes a cornerstone to sustainable energy and smart energy management. Different from existing studies that improve the PV efficiency by changing cell materials, this article proposes a novel system reliability and cost model of enhancing the PV power resilience performance from the perspective of optimizing the number of PV panels. Specifically, a multiobjective planning model is proposed, which determines the optimum number of spare parts for PV panels maximizing the output power resilience while maximizing the system reliability and minimizing the cost. The reliability measures the probability of stable operation of a PV panel considering the no-power output state. The cost factor encompasses negative cost of environmental benefits, resource cost, operation and maintenance cost, and penalty cost. Experiments are performed on fifty sets of Pareto optimal solutions in summer and winter cases to illustrate effectiveness of the proposed method by using a ground-mounted PV project in Zhongwei City, China.  © 1963-2012 IEEE.
palavras_chave: Cost; multiobjective optimization; performance; photovoltaic (PV) system; system reliability

titulo: Developing An Anomaly Detection Model for Predictive Maintenance in Large-Scale PV Systems Using Temporal Convolutional Network
resumo: Large-scale photovoltaic (LSSPV) systems are vital for advancing sustainable energy production, yet their performance and availability are often compromised by faults, inefficiencies, and operational challenges, leading to increased maintenance costs and downtime. Predictive maintenance plays a crucial role in addressing these issues by enabling proactive measures to improve system reliability and efficiency. This study investigates the application of Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) for predictive maintenance, focusing on the prediction of DC output power and anomaly detection at the string level. Leveraging environmental datasets, including solar irradiation and PV panel temperature, the TCN model effectively captures temporal dependencies in sequential data, addressing challenges related to data abstraction and nonlinearity. The performance of the proposed model was validated to ensure its accuracy and reliability by means of a comparison with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). By replacing traditional scheduled operation and maintenance (O&M) methods, the TCN-based approach enhances monitoring, inspection, and maintenance processes, reduces operational costs, and improves the overall reliability of LSSPV systems, highlighting its potential as a robust solution for advancing predictive maintenance in photovoltaic energy systems. © 2025, IPMEDIA SDN BHD. All rights reserved.
palavras_chave: Anomaly detection; DC output power; Large-Scale Photovoltaic Systems (LSSPV); Predictive maintenance; Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN)

titulo: Optimization Method for Cross-Regional Scheduling of Retired Charging Pile Component Reuse
fonte_periodico: International Journal of Engineering and Technology Innovation
resumo: With the increasing number of decommissioned charging piles, efficient reuse of their components is essential for sustainable resource utilization and intelligent grid management. To address the challenges in recycling and scheduling retired charging pile components, this study proposes a cost-optimization approach for delivery planning in smart grid logistics. An Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (EDVRP-TW) model is formulated that considers vehicle capacity and time constraints. To solve it, an Improved Chicken Swarm Optimization Algorithm (ICOOT) is developed, integrating Circle chaotic mapping, spiral search strategy, and normal cloud mutation to enhance convergence speed and solution quality. Simulation experiments using real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly reduces operation and maintenance costs, achieving up to an 11.77% cost reduction. The results validate the effectiveness and applicability of the model and algorithm in intelligent recycling and scheduling of grid materials. © by the authors.
palavras_chave: EDVRP-TW; green technology; ICOOT; retired charging piles; smart grid logistics

titulo: Research on Optimal Capacity Allocation of ESS and STATCOM Based on Improved Sparrow Search Algorithm
fonte_periodico: Proceedings of 2025 IEEE 7th International Conference on Civil Aviation Safety and Information Technology Iccasit 2025
resumo: With the high popularization rate of renewable energy power stations, power systems is facing dual pressures of stability and economy. To address this challenge, this paper conducts research on the optimal capacity allocation of ESS and STATCOM in renewable energy power stations. Firstly, it establishes models of ESS and STATCOM, and analyzes the interaction process of ESS and STATCOM in high-penetration renewable energy power stations. Then, the optimal capacity allocation model for ESS and STATCOM with the goal of economy is further constructed, and it is solved by improved sparrow search algorithm (ISSA). Finally, the validity of the optimization model is verified by an example analysis. This research provides theoretical guidance and practical references for the active and reactive capacity allocation, operation, and maintenance of high-penetration renewable energy power stations, and helps promote the economic benefits and sustainable development of renewable energy power stations. © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: ESS; Optimal Allocation; Renewable Energy Power Stations; STATCOM

titulo: Research on Intelligent Monitoring and Fault Diagnosis Methods for Wind Turbines Based on Data Mining
fonte_periodico: Safeprocess 2025 14th Caa Symposium on Fault Detection Supervision and Safety for Technical Processes
resumo: Under the impetus of China's 14th Five-Year Plan, the renewable energy sector has experienced accelerated development, with wind power - a mature and commercially viable clean energy source - facing significant challenges in operation and maintenance (O&M) amid its large-scale deployment. Wind turbines, predominantly deployed in complex climatic environments, suffer accelerated fatigue degradation of critical components due to the coupling effects of dynamic meteorological parameters and mechanical loads. This study focuses on the application of data mining and artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in establishing intelligent monitoring and fault diagnosis systems for wind turbines. A data-driven methodology is proposed to enhance fault detection accuracy and predictive maintenance capabilities. Looking ahead, big data technologies are poised to drive intelligent upgrades within the wind power industry, achieving strategic breakthroughs in cross-system collaborative optimization and autonomous decision-making, thereby empowering the sustainable development of renewable energy.  © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: data-driven methodology; intelligent monitoring systems; wind power

titulo: Innovations for Sustainability of Environmental Sanitation Infrastructure and Safe Containment of Faeces in Maharashtra
fonte_periodico: Water and Energy Systems Building for Climate Resilience and Environmental Sustainability
resumo: Faecal sludge and septage management have garnered significant attention within various programs in India that are aimed at improving sanitation and public health. One such notable initiative is the Swachh Bharat Mission. The National Urban Sanitation Policy prioritizes the management of faecal sludge and septage. These initiatives focus on promoting the construction of septic tanks and the adoption of appropriate technologies for the safe handling and treatment of sludge. Furthermore, the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation and the Smart Cities Mission also have components related to faecal sludge and septage management. State governments have also tailor-made programs and policies to address these challenges. This chapter discusses the results of pilot projects implemented at multiple locations in Maharashtra to address the following three critical challenges: 1) sustaining the O&M of the existing FSTPs at urban centers; 2) non-availability of resources and infrastructure for safe FSSM in villages; and 3) optimum utilization of existing urban infrastructure and ensuring sustainable operation and maintenance. The focus is on institutional innovation. © 2025 selection and editorial matter, M. Dinesh Kumar and Yusuf Kabir; individual chapters, the contributors.

titulo: Workforce Assessment of Vietnam's Solar PV Industry
fonte_periodico: Eee Am 2025 IEEE 2nd Asia Meeting on Environment and Electrical Engineering
resumo: Vietnam's solar PV industry has grown rapidly, but now faces the challenge of building a skilled workforce amid emerging training gaps. To effectively address these gaps, it is crucial to conduct a comprehensive survey of solar-related job positions across the value chain. These findings from a 2025 survey of industry stakeholders, including project developers, engineers, operators, and educators, examined workforce structures, skill requirements, and training effectiveness. The results indicate that system designers, project managers, and operations and maintenance technicians are perceived as pivotal roles, yet remain undersupplied. Respondents also underscored the growing significance of emerging technologies, particularly energy storage and smart grid integration, which will reshape skill profiles over the coming decade. While transferable expertise from conventional power sectors contributes to the talent pool, a significant gap persists in solar-specific skills. The study concludes that coordinated interventions by industry, government, and training institutions are essential to address skills shortages, expand practical training, and embed emerging technology competencies, thereby supporting Vietnam's long-term renewable energy transition.  © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: job role; solar PV; Vietnam; workforce

titulo: Research on maintenance strategies and quality control for key components of electric train bogies
fonte_periodico: Proceedings of SPIE the International Society for Optical Engineering
resumo: The current maintenance plans for electric trains in China primarily follow a "preventive maintenance as the main strategy, with emergency maintenance as a supplement" approach. Fixed maintenance intervals often result in either "over-maintenance" or "under-maintenance" of components. As a crucial subsystem for ensuring the high-speed, safe, and stable operation of electric trains, research on the fault propagation patterns and optimization of maintenance modes for the bogie can provide decision support for the systematic operation and maintenance strategies of electric trains. In light of this, this paper establishes a comprehensive maintenance optimization method for multi-component systems in rail transit electric trains, based on real fault and maintenance records, and the correlation between key components. This aims to balance maintenance costs while ensuring the reliability and availability of the bogie system. © 2025 SPIE.
palavras_chave: Bogie; Maintenance strategy; Multi-objective optimization; PSO; Rail transit electric trains

titulo: Role of Data Analytics in Optimizing Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Operations in Smart Buildings
fonte_periodico: Proceedings of the 2025 IEEE International Conference on Computation Big Data and Engineering Iccbe 2025
resumo: This review article explores the role of data analytics in optimizing air conditioning and refrigeration in smart buildings. Data analytics are used to address inefficiency and to reduce high energy costs associated with traditional heating, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) management. Data analytics helps enhance energy efficiency and reduce operational costs through real-time monitoring and predictive maintenance. The feasibility of using data analytics is validated in case studies for significant energy savings and occupant comfort. The data-driven strategies are effective for sustainable building operations. Integrating advanced technologies such as the Internet of Things sensors and machine learning algorithms enables efficient HVAC management. © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: data analytics; energy efficiency; HVAC optimization; smart buildings; sustainability

titulo: An Interpretable Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Method Based on Temporal Embedding
fonte_periodico: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence Iceaai 2025
resumo: Photovoltaic power generation is a key driver of sustainable development, making real-time operation and maintenance of power generation equipment increasingly critical. Accurate forecasting of future power output can enhance the economic efficiency of power plants, optimize power dispatch, ensure grid stability, and prevent both power shortages and wastage, while enabling timely adjustments and maintenance. However, many remote photovoltaic power plants struggle to optimize resource utilization due to insufficient or unavailable sensor, cloud, and satellite data, often relying solely on limited historical information. This challenge is further exacerbated in regions where human intervention is costly or impractical due to accessibility issues. Traditional models, while reliable, often function as 'black box' systems, lacking interpretability, making it difficult to identify the root cause when predictions deviate from actual values. To address these challenges, this study proposes a low-cost, deployable model framework that relies only on historical data and calendar features to provide long-term trend forecasting for decision-making, offering a novel solution for effective predictions under resource constraints. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: LSTM-Driven Predictive Scheduling for Green Energy-Hydrogen-Methanol Integrated System
resumo: This study proposes an optimization scheduling model for the Green Energy-Hydrogen-Methanol Integrated System (GEHMIS) based on the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, aimed at achieving efficient, stable, and economical operation of renewable energy systems. In response to the fluctuations and uncertainties in the output of wind and solar energy, this paper introduces the LSTM network to accurately predict wind speed and temperature using historical data. The integrated system model developed in this study covers key processes such as wind and solar power generation, water electrolysis for hydrogen production, hydrogen storage and transportation, and methanol synthesis. The objective of this research is to maximize the overall system profit by developing a multi-constraint mathematical optimization model that takes into account multiple factors, including hydrogen and methanol production efficiencies, hydrogen consumption, operation and maintenance costs, electricity price fluctuations, grid interactions, and carbon dioxide costs. Compared to traditional random resource allocation strategies, the proposed optimization model demonstrates significant advantages in terms of economic benefits and energy utilization efficiency: the overall system profit increased by approximately 68.3 %, and the hydrogen utilization rate improved by 30 %. This provides important technical support and a practical pathway for the large-scale application of green energy and the global transition to sustainable energy. titulo: An Engineering Delivery Model for Cloud-Based Intelligent Computing Infrastructure
fonte_periodico: 2025 10th International Conference on Cloud Computing and Big Data Analytics Icccbda 2025
resumo: With the rapid advancement of new-quality productivity and artificial intelligence technologies, cloud computing has emerged as a critical enabler for intelligent transformation across various industries. This paper explores the evolving trends in intelligent computing infrastructure delivery services and proposes a cloud-based engineering delivery model for intelligent computing infrastructure. The model is designed to assess the full-stack technical service capabilities of cloud management service providers in delivering large-scale model engineering projects, specifically under scenarios involving 100card, 1,000-card, and 10,000-card intelligent computing clusters. The accuracy and generalizability of the model are validated through extensive enterprise data analysis. Furthermore, this paper examines the future development trajectory of intelligent computing infrastructure delivery services from five key perspectives: standardization and ecosystem collaboration, intelligent operation and maintenance with automated delivery, green computing and sustainable development, edge computing and distributed intelligent computing, and security and trusted delivery. These advancements are expected to foster the synergistic integration of cloud computing and AI technologies, thereby accelerating the intelligent transformation of diverse industries.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: A Comparison of Impact for Various Biomass Utilization in Indonesian Cofiring Coal-Fired Power Plants
fonte_periodico: IEEE Pes Gtd Conference and Exposition Asia 2025 Accelerating the Energy Transition Towards Carbon Neutrality A Sustainable Energy Future for all Gtd Asia 2025
resumo: Biomass is one of the largest sustainable energy potentials that impacts worldwide GHG emission reduction. Biomass cofiring has a potential energy alternative since it may produce net-balanced CO2 emissions. The Indonesian government has been committed to reducing emissions with several strategic programs and increasing a renewable energy mixed target of 23 % by utilizing biomass in the existing CFPP. This paper investigated the impact of various types of biomass in Indonesian CFPP, such as woodchips, sawdust, palm kernel shells, rice husks, and corn cobs. The characteristics of fly ash and exhaust gas emissions as a waste product of the boiler are analyzed to know the impacts on operation and maintenance. The result shows that rice husk has the lowest potential for slagging, indicated by SI of 0.07, FI of 0.3, and BAI of 2.9 in the comparison profile for various 5% biomass cofiring. In addition, the impacts of CO2 and NOx emissions have also been investigated, with a promising reduction in GHG emissions. © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: circular economy; cofiring; GHG emission; Renewable energy resources

titulo: User Perception and Behaviour Towards the Sustainability of Shared Sanitation Facilities in Poorer Peri-Urban Area (Case Study: Ciwalengke, Majalaya District)
fonte_periodico: Iop Conference Series Earth and Environmental Science
resumo: Access to safe sanitation is crucial for public health and sustainable development. The WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme recognizes the role of shared sanitation in achieving Sustainable Development Goal 6b. Shared sanitation facilities provide a practical solution in densely populated poorer areas and offer a cost-effective alternative to private facilities. However, their functional sustainability is often compromised by inadequate operation and maintenance. This study aims to identify psychosocial factors influencing the maintenance of shared sanitation facilities, focusing on a case study in Ciwalengke, Majalaya by employing the RANAS and IBM-WASH frameworks. The questionnaire components include behavioural, risk, attitude, norms, ability, self-regulation, contextual, psychosocial, and technology, which were reduced from several items within each variable using Principal Component Analysis (PCA). These components were used as predictor variables and analysed using multi-linear regression with the outcome variable as behaviour, resulting in an R2 value of 0.395 at p<0.01. Further analysis reveals that risks, attitude, and self-regulation components are significant predictors of behavioural outcomes. The sustainability analysis, based on questionnaire responses, indicates that sanitation facilities in the area are somewhat sustainable. These findings demonstrate that users' perceptions and behaviours provide valuable insights into assessing and enhancing the sustainability of shared sanitation facilities. © 2025 Institute of Physics Publishing. All rights reserved.

titulo: A Data-as-a-Product Approach for Smart Grid Data-Driven Optimization
fonte_periodico: 2025 IEEE 13th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering Sege 2025
resumo: The integration of renewable energy sources into smart grids presents challenges such as energy variability, grid reliability, and interoperability. This paper aims to present the Data-as-a-Product (DaaP) framework as a solution to these challenges by considering data as a strategically managed asset, thus promoting collaborative efforts between grid operators, renewable energy providers, and stakeholders. In addition, the concept of DaaP will leverage uniform interfaces as well as highly protected data-sustained platforms, thereby the framework adds more value to the smart grid by operational efficiency and crossentity analytics. Improvement of the way of operation such as grid flexibility, operation and maintenance, efficiency, and crossorganizational analytics can ensure higher operation efficiency, optimal energy use, and adequate resources. The presented framework potentially enables improved forecasting, optimization, and decision-making, leading to the be more resilient and sustainable smart grids. While implementation challenges exist, this scalable framework provides a blueprint for modernizing energy systems utilizing DaaP as the core in next-generation grid architectures.  © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: Data-as-a-product; renewable energy; smart grids

titulo: Institutionalizing post-occupancy evaluation in African universities: a framework for student-centered housing governance
autores: Attakora-Amaniampong, E; Appau, MW; Anugwo, IC
resumo: Purpose – This study systematically reviews the application and effectiveness of post-occupancy evaluation (POE) in student housing across African universities. This study aims to understand how POE is used, the methodologies used and whether the findings inform policy and management practices. Design/methodology/approach – This study used a systematic review of 25 empirical studies published between 2020 and 2024. These studies span 11 African countries and were selected based on predefined inclusion criteria. Data were synthesized thematically, focusing on POE methods, performance dimensions measured and institutional responses. Findings – The review reveals that POE in African universities is fragmented, largely academic and not systematically institutionalized. Evaluations rely heavily on cross-sectional surveys with limited use of standardized tools or digital systems. Common student housing challenges include overcrowding, sanitation issues and poor maintenance. Student feedback is often collected but rarely integrated into decision-making processes. Practical implications – This study recommends institutionalizing POE through low-cost digital tools, recurring evaluation cycles and participatory governance models. This would align African universities with global best practices and support the achievement of Sustainable Development Goal 11, which focuses on inclusive and sustainable settlements. Originality/value – To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study is the first to comprehensively synthesize recent POE applications in African higher education. It offers a strategic framework for embedding POE into university governance, bridging the gap between research, policy and practice. © 2025 Emerald Publishing Limited

titulo: Operating Factors for Hydroelectric Power Plants: A Systematic Literature Review
resumo: Energy sustainability is gaining more and more relevance with the search for more efficient renewable energy sources. In this context, hydropower is one of the most studied and developed; however, the main operational factors related to how hydropower plants are conceived, financed, developed, and operated in their various denominations, have not been sufficiently addressed in a work that determines the state of the art of these factors and their influence. This paper analyzes the main operational factors of hydropower plants through a systematic literature review (SLR). Based on a conceptual map, and the formulation of five research questions, a semantic search script is structured in five levels; resulting in the consideration of 83 scientific articles, published in the last 6 years, that address the relationship between water storage and generation capacity, environmental impact assessment, technical-economic feasibility, simulation and automation models, and operation and maintenance schemes of hydroelectric power plants. The results of the systematic literature review can serve as a reference for future research in this field. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

titulo: Application of Lightweight Neural Network Model in Garbage Classification
fonte_periodico: 2025 5th International Conference on Computer Science and Blockchain Ccsb 2025
resumo: Waste sorting is crucial for resource recycling, environmental protection, and sustainable development. This paper explores the application of lightweight neural network models in waste classification for a lithium - battery - powered, Raspberry Pi 4B - based real - time system. Although image classification models are widely used, this study compares four lightweight models (TripleNet, EfficientNet - B0, YoloV5 - lite under TinyML framework, MobileNetV2) on edge devices. After comprehensively evaluating training duration, inference time, accuracy rates, and memory consumption, the MobileNetV2 model was chosen as the core architecture due to its easy operation and maintenance. In system implementation, a Raspberry Pi 4B ran neural network models and integrated cameras, conveyor belts, and servo motors for waste recognition and sorting. Experimental results show that MobileNetV2 achieved high accuracy in waste classification with low memory usage and fast inference speeds, suitable for resource - constrained edge devices. The system enables rapid waste sorting in practice, improving efficiency and accuracy in municipal waste management and offering insights for urban waste processing. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Enhancing sustainable urban design using machine learning: comparative analysis of seven metaheuristic algorithms in energy-efficient digital architecture
resumo: Metaheuristics optimization algorithms used in this research include PSO, ACO, GA, and SA and represent effective approaches toward reaching an optimal or near-optimal solution for decision variables with an intention to improve energy efficiency, increasing indoor comfort whilst reducing the carbon footprint of building operations. These algorithms will be applied across different sizes of a synthesized data pool prepared with important features like window-to-wall ratio, efficiency in HVAC systems, renewable systems integration, among others. PSO demonstrated the best scenario in both cases with an optimum convergence rate of 24.1%; ACO produced almost the same best result as mentioned with high rates of reductions in carbon footprints. These had their best energy-savings while convergence in GA and SA was extremely slow with energy efficiencies that turned out to be pretty low. This could enable real proposals to be made to architects, urban planners, and policy thinkers, allowing them to turn such ideal cases into viable realities within sustainable development initiatives. titulo: Synergizing Artificial Intelligence with Sustainable Design for Smart Built Environments
resumo: The convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and sustainable design principles offers a promising path for advancing smart built environments. This paper presents a framework that merges AI with sustainability to develop intelligent, resource-efficient, and resilient built environments. It integrates AI algorithms and data analytics throughout building design, construction, and operation to enhance energy efficiency, reduce carbon footprints, and improve performance through predictive modelling, real-time monitoring, and optimisation. The framework emphasizes user-centric design, utilizing AI systems like smart sensors and IoT devices to personalize occupant experiences for better comfort and productivity. It also addresses resilience by employing AI for risk assessment and scenario analysis to manage climate change and other uncertainties. This approach aims to create more adaptable and sustainable built environments, contributing to a future with smarter and more environmentally conscious infrastructure. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2025.
palavras_chave: Artificial Intelligence (AI); Climate Change; Smart Built Environments; Sustainable Design; User-centric Design

titulo: Annual Hourly E-Mobility Modelling and Assessment in Climate Neutral Positive Energy Districts
fonte_periodico: Conference Proceedings 2025 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2025 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe Eeeic I and Cps Europe 2025
resumo: This paper presents a full-year hourly district emobility model and its integration into a Positive Energy District simulation and assessment model including building operation, use and embodied energy and emissions. The aim of this work is to model the operation and energy flexibility potential of an EV fleet in a district through mono- and bi-directional charging and enable its assessment in terms of self-utilization of local and volatile regional RES surpluses. Results of example residential, office, school and supermarket use cases show an increase in self-utilization of local PV of up to 30% due to EV inclusion, even if PV installation size exceeds legal building code requirements by a factor of two to four. Bi-Directional charging can cut annual grid electricity by up to 30% but require an increase in battery full equivalent cycles of 20%. © 2025 IEEE.
palavras_chave: electric mobility; multimodal energy systems; positive energy districts

titulo: Feasibility and Economic Assessment of a PV-Wind Hybrid Charging Station in the Bronx, NY
resumo: This work presents a technical and economic feasibility assessment of a photovoltaic (PV)-wind hybrid charging station located in the South Bronx, New York, with a 100-kW demand. The study evaluates the technical requirements for sizing the hybrid system, including determining the appropriate capacity of solar PV panels, wind turbines, and battery storage to meet the energy demand of the charging station. The analysis also explores the economic feasibility by considering key financial parameters such as capital costs, operation and maintenance (O&M) costs, system efficiency, and the system’s lifetime. A financial model is developed to estimate the costs, payback period, and overall economic viability, incorporating sensitivity analysis on the Net Present Value (NPV) and Return on Investment (ROI). Environmental impact metrics, including carbon emission reduction, energy efficiency gains, renewable energy utilization, and air quality improvement, are also examined to assess the broader environmental benefits of the hybrid system. The study highlights the potential of renewable energy-based charging stations in urban areas, providing valuable insights into the technical, economic, and environmental aspects of hybrid energy systems for electric vehicle (EV) infrastructure. © 2013 IEEE.
